    run with `--mortality on --mass-balance --workers 2` completed.

116.8 Checkpoints
    Not invalidated formally - no observation shape, FG set, grid layout
    or Observability entry moved - but a policy trained with the flag on
    and run with it off, or the reverse, is being evaluated in a
    different world. The flag is recorded in the `training_progress`
    config so a run says which one it was.

117 A/B: --mass-balance x PHYTOPLANKTON 0.125. THE RESOURCE LEVEL IS INVARIANT (2026-09-29)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

117.1 Why this 2x2
    Section 113 recommends raising `phytoplankton.growth_rate` from
    0.0375 to 0.125 on the ground that 0.0375 is net of the grazing the
    tick applies. Section 116 implements a mass-balanced growth term
    behind `--mass-balance`. Section 115.7 ranks the two as independent
    defects and predicts that fixing the growth term first will change
    what the phytoplankton change buys. This measures it.

    All four arms: 60x60, 3000 ticks, frozen greedy, colocated,
    `--mortality on`, zooplankton at its library value 0.0913.

117.2 Conservation and throughput
    `tools/probes/growth_mass_balance.py`, means over the last 300 ticks:

      arm                  zoo t    phyto t  zoo:phyto  grazed  prod   eff.
      legacy    0.0375     28395     9964     2.85:1     100.0  467.8  468 %
      legacy    0.125     176522    26180     6.74:1     861.0 1864.9  217 %
      mass-bal  0.0375      3959     1448     2.73:1      51.5    9.9   19 %
      mass-bal  0.125      12700     1570     8.09:1     171.9   33.9   20 %

    (grazed and prod in t/tick; eff. = production/grazed against the
    28.9 % ceiling of 114.4. Production is read off the losses, the only
    estimator valid under the flag - 116.4.)

    The result is in the phyto column. Under `--mass-balance`, tripling
    phytoplankton's growth rate moves its standing stock from 1448 to
    1570 t - EIGHT PER CENT. What moves is the throughput: grazing
    51.5 -> 171.9 t/tick, +234 %, and zooplankton 3959 -> 12700 t,
    +221 %. Conservation holds either way, 19.2 % and 19.7 %.

    That is the textbook R* result and it is what a mass-balanced
    consumer is supposed to do: the equilibrium resource level is set by
    the CONSUMER's break-even, not by the resource's growth rate. Faster
    primary production buys more flux at the same standing stock.

    The legacy rows do not show it - phytoplankton goes 9964 -> 26180 t,
    +163 % - because a consumer whose growth is decoupled from its
    ingestion does not have a well-defined R* to pin the resource at.
    Finding the invariance only after the growth term is fixed is
    itself a check on the fix.

117.3 The food web
    `tools/probes/zoo_growth_sweep.py`, 3 seeds, ranges over seeds:

      arm                 phy_end      zoo_end     zoo_min      gad_end
      legacy   0.0375   0.069-0.149  0.64-1.16  0.000-0.001  0.10-0.24
      legacy   0.125    0.325-0.337  5.09-5.11  0.049-0.058  0.65-0.98
      mass-bal 0.0375   0.018        0.113      0.001-0.002  0.14-0.32
      mass-bal 0.125    0.020        0.362      0.361-0.362  0.37-0.51

    Two things stand out beyond 117.2.

    First, the OSCILLATION IS GONE. In the mass-balanced 0.125 arm
    zooplankton's trough over the whole 3000 ticks is 0.361 against a
    final-window mean of 0.362 - it never dips below its equilibrium at
    all. The legacy arm at the same phytoplankton value swings from a
    trough of 0.049 to a mean of 5.11, a factor 100. The predator-prey
    cycling that dominated every measurement in sections 109 to 113 was
    the fabricate-then-starve cycle, not ecology.

    Second, the SEED SPREAD collapses. Legacy phy_end spans 0.069-0.149
    across three seeds; the mass-balanced arms read 0.018, 0.018, 0.018
    and 0.113, 0.113, 0.113. A deterministic equilibrium, which is what
    made the legacy arm's 190.8 / 273.7 / 343.8 / 467.7 % efficiency
    spread across runs (116.4) unmeasurable.

    Gadoids improve with the phytoplankton change in BOTH worlds, 0.10-
    0.24 -> 0.65-0.98 legacy and 0.14-0.32 -> 0.37-0.51 mass-balanced.
    The absolute level is lower under the flag because part of the legacy
    gadoid biomass was fed by zooplankton that was never paid for.

117.4 The viability corner
    `--spawn colocated --behaviour greedy --mortality on`, 20x20, 7300
    ticks, 3 seeds. The 0.0375 column is from 116.5:

      fg             phyto 0.0375              phyto 0.125
                   legacy      mass-bal      legacy      mass-bal
      gadoids      FAIL floor  FAIL ext@3506 FAIL floor  FAIL floor
      pelagic      FAIL floor  FAIL floor    FAIL floor  FAIL floor
      porpoises    ext@212     ext@86        ext@229     ext@97
      benthic      PASS 0.702  PASS 0.721    PASS 0.402  PASS 0.634
      phyto        FAIL 0.065  FAIL 0.018    PASS 0.302  FAIL 0.019
      zoo          PASS 0.702  PASS 0.113    PASS 4.891  PASS 0.359
      overall      NOT VIABLE  NOT VIABLE    NOT VIABLE  NOT VIABLE

    Raising phytoplankton RESCUES its own viability criterion in the
    legacy world - 0.065 FAIL to 0.302 PASS - and does nothing for it
    under the flag, 0.018 to 0.019. Same invariance as 117.2, now with a
    verdict attached.

    Under the flag both plankton groups sit at drift 1.00 with
    zooplankton's trough at 0.357 against an equilibrium of 0.359. One
    improvement worth noting: gadoids go from `extinct@3506` back to
    below-floor-but-alive when phytoplankton is raised.

    The overall verdict is NOT VIABLE in all four arms, still driven by
    the same pre-existing failures (73, 74, 90-92).

117.5 What this settles, and what it changes
    * Section 113's recommendation stands but its VALUE changes. Raising
      phytoplankton to 0.125 is a productivity fix, not a standing-stock
      fix: +234 % throughput and roughly double the gadoids, and 8 % on
      phytoplankton's own biomass. It does NOT repair the inverted
      zoo:phyto ratio - it makes it worse, 2.73:1 -> 8.09:1, because
      zooplankton scales with throughput while its food's stock does not.
      113.9's withdrawal of the spawn recalibration was right for a
      better reason than the one it gave.
    * The inversion is now unambiguously defect (2) of 115.7 -
      zooplankton's maintenance / intake / energy-content triple setting
      an R* far below any plausible phytoplankton standing stock. Not
      the growth term, and not phytoplankton's growth rate. Both of the
      other two candidates have now been eliminated by measurement
      rather than by argument.
    * The next lever is therefore that triple. The R* condition is
      f(P) * energy_gain = resting_metabolism * cost_eat, and the
      quantity to check first is `resting_metabolism = 3.5 MJ/t/tick`
      against 1300 MJ per ton grazed: a maintenance cost that cheap
      pins the resource at a refuge level whatever else is done.
      Untested.

117.6 Probe note
    `zoo_growth_sweep.py`'s `realPB` column is the growth-term WISH, not
    production, when `--mass-balance` is on - the reserve caps the term,
    so `growth_rate * <s-u> * 1460` is what was wanted rather than what
    was spent. It reads 0.2-0.3 in the flagged arms, which is the
    surplus collapsing to the maintenance line, not production
    collapsing. The probe now prints that warning itself.
    `growth_mass_balance.py` reads production off the losses and is the
    one to quote. Nothing in the library or in `lib/` changed for this
    section; the phytoplankton value was overridden in memory, except
    for the corner runs, where the library was edited and restored.

118 ZOOPLANKTON resting_metabolism IS ~1/6 OF A COPEPOD'S, AND THE CONSTRAINT THAT SET IT NEVER BOUND (2026-09-29)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

118.1 The number
    `resting_metabolism: 3.5` MJ/t/tick, i.e. 14.0 MJ/t/day, against
    `energy_content: 4500` MJ/t:

      14.0 / 4500 = 0.311 % of body energy per day at rest
      x cost_eat 1.45                = 0.451 %/day while feeding

    Section 117.5 named this triple as the remaining defect. This is the
    metabolism leg of it.

118.2 How it got there: fitted backwards from a starvation window
    `tools/starve_calibration.py` is the calibration of record. It drives
    one isolated cell with `pi_rest = 1` and no prey and reports T1
    (days to drain the reserve from u_X) and T_total (days to 95 %
    biomass loss), against a literature target of 3-30 days for
    zooplankton - "active copepods 3-14 d; lipid-rich up to 30+". At the
    library values it prints

      zooplankton   ME 450   rm 3.5   starve 0.200   T1 16.2 d   T_total 15.0 d   OK

    So `resting_metabolism` was solved for a window, given a fixed
    `max_energy_reserve`. It was never set from a respiration rate, and
    nothing in the repo records one.

118.3 The constraint does not bind, and that is the finding
    Re-running the same tool with only zooplankton's rate changed:

      zoo rm    %/day    T1 (d)   T_total (d)   verdict
      3.5        0.31     16.2       15.0       OK (lit 3-30 d)
      22.5       2.00      2.5        8.2       OK (lit 3-30 d)
      56.2       5.00      1.2        7.5       OK (lit 3-30 d)
      112.5     10.00      0.5        7.2       OK (lit 3-30 d)

    The window stays inside the literature range across a 32-FOLD range
    of `resting_metabolism`, because T_total is dominated by
    `starve_rate = 0.2` catabolising biomass and not by the reserve
    drain. T1 moves by a factor 32; T_total moves by a factor 2.

    That is biologically the right structure - a starving copepod burns
    its lipid store and then its body, and the second phase is the long
    one - but it means the calibration that produced 3.5 had almost no
    power to determine it. Any value in the table passes. The number was
    under-determined and has been treated ever since as though it were
    measured.

118.4 What the literature says
    Sources located (see 118.8): the daily minimum carbon demand of
    NON-FEEDING copepods - respiration plus pellet plus egg production -
    is about 10 % of body weight per day; respiration or excretion
    accounts for roughly 50 % of ingestion in carbon terms; and carbon
    demand for calanoids feeding on dispersed food is 2-3x the resting
    rate.

    Two readings of that against the model:
      * Respiration alone is less than the 10 %/day figure, since that
        figure includes egg production - which in this model IS the
        growth term, not the metabolism. A respiration rate of 2-5 %/day
        is the defensible band, and 0.311 %/day is 1/6 to 1/16 of it.
      * `feeding_cost: 1.45` is the model's feeding multiplier against a
        literature 2-3x. Low, and not investigated here.

118.5 Measured: what the rate does to the world
    `tools/probes/growth_mass_balance.py --mass-balance --zoo-rm`, 60x60,
    3000 ticks, means over the last 300, frozen greedy, colocated,
    `--mortality on`, library values otherwise. Run under
    `--mass-balance` deliberately: it is the only regime where the tick's
    energy budget closes, so shares of ingested energy mean something
    (the gap column below).

      rm     %/day  resp/ing  built/ing  gap    zoo t   phyto t  zoo:phyto
      3.5     0.31   19.5 %    43.2 %    2.3 %   3959    1448     2.73 : 1
      11.25   1.00   37.6 %    26.0 %    1.4 %   3230    1978     1.63 : 1
      22.5    2.00   46.1 %    17.9 %    1.0 %   2837    2875     0.99 : 1
      56.2    5.00   49.5 %    18.8 %   -3.4 %   5666   22524     0.25 : 1
      112.5  10.00     -          -       -         0   86376     extinct

    (resp/ing and built/ing are shares of INGESTED energy; assimilation
    is 0.65, so the two should come to 65 % and `gap` is what is
    missing. zoo:phyto at spawn is 0.44:1.)

    Reading it:
      * The INVERSION IS A METABOLISM ARTEFACT. zoo:phyto goes 2.73:1 ->
        0.99:1 -> 0.25:1 as the rate rises through its plausible band,
        crossing the spawn ratio 0.44:1 between 2 and 5 %/day. Nothing
        else in sections 109-117 moved it: section 117 showed tripling
        phytoplankton's growth rate made it WORSE.
      * Phytoplankton's standing stock rises with it, 1448 -> 22524 t,
        which is the R* mechanism working in reverse: a more expensive
        grazer breaks even at a higher resource density.
      * There is a WALL just above 5 %/day. At 10 %/day zooplankton goes
        extinct and phytoplankton sits at its carrying capacity. The
        usable band is narrow and its upper edge is close.
      * The respiration share moves onto the literature ~50 % exactly
        where the ratio becomes plausible.

118.6 Two caveats on those numbers
    * The respiration column is an UPPER BOUND. It is computed as
      `biomass * rm * cost_eat`, i.e. as though the whole standing stock
      paid the feeding multiplier every tick; a resting or moving mix
      pays 1.0 or 1.2 instead. The true share is between 69 % and 100 %
      of the printed value - so rm 22.5 sits at 32-46 % of ingestion
      rather than exactly 46 %. The DIRECTION is unaffected: 3.5 gives
      13-19 % against a literature ~50 %.
    * The -3.4 % gap at rm 56.2 is that same over-estimate showing up as
      an impossible closure, which is the check that the bound is a
      bound.

118.7 Correction to sections 114-117: GGE was compared on the wrong basis
    Those sections quote an implied gross growth efficiency of ~19 %
    against a literature copepod GGE of 20-40 % and read it as "inside
    the band, at its floor". The 19 % is a WET MASS ratio, tons of
    zooplankton per ton of phytoplankton; the literature band is CARBON.
    A wet ton of zooplankton carries 4500 MJ against phytoplankton's
    2000, so the carbon-basis figure is 19.2 * 4500/2000 = 43.2 %, i.e.
    ABOVE the band rather than at its floor. That is the `built/ing`
    column in 118.5.

    What this does NOT change: the 28.9 % ceiling of 114.4 is itself a
    mass ratio derived from the same two energy contents, so
    "19.2 % against a 28.9 % ceiling" is apples to apples and stands, as
    does everything built on it - the legacy term's 198-468 % is over the
    ceiling on either basis. What changes is which direction the
    mass-balanced arm errs in: it is slightly too EFFICIENT at rm 3.5,
    not slightly too poor. Raising rm to 22.5 brings it to 17.9 %, just
    under the band.

118.8 Recommendation
    Set `zooplankton.resting_metabolism = 22.5` MJ/t/tick - 2 % of body
    energy per day, a 6.4x raise. It is the value where the respiration
    share reaches the literature order, the zoo:phyto ratio stops being
    inverted (0.99:1), the carbon-basis GGE lands just under the 20-40 %
    band, and the starvation window stays comfortably inside 3-30 days
    at 8.2. 56.2 (5 %/day) is arguably better on the ratio alone but its
    energy accounting does not close, and 112.5 is past the extinction
    wall.

    Do it WITH `--mass-balance`. Under the legacy growth term a higher
    metabolism is partly absorbed by the fabricated biomass and the two
    changes are not separable.

    Not applied - the instruction was to investigate. Companion items
    this raises and does not settle: `max_energy_reserve = 450` (10 % of
    body energy) becomes a 5-day buffer at 2 %/day and a 1-day buffer at
    10 %, so it should be re-derived alongside (115.6 asked for the same
    thing for a different reason); and `feeding_cost: 1.45` against a
    literature 2-3x.

    Sources: Ikeda et al. (2001) Metabolic rates of epipelagic marine
    copepods as a function of body mass and temperature, Mar. Biol.
    139:587-596, for the mass/temperature scaling; and the non-feeding
    carbon-demand, respiration-share and feeding-multiplier figures from
    the copepod metabolic-budget literature located by search rather than
    read in full - they are orders of magnitude, not point citations, and
    should be checked against Ikeda's tables before being quoted as
    settled.

    APPLIED by section 119.

119 APPLIED: ZOOPLANKTON resting_metabolism 3.5 -> 22.5 (2026-09-29)

    *** ONE TEST IS RED AND UNRESOLVED - READ 119.3 AND 119.7. ***

119.1 The change
    `fgconfig/fg_library.yaml`, zooplankton only:

      resting_metabolism: 3.5  ->  22.5      MJ/t/tick
                                             = 90 MJ/t/day
                                             = 2.0 % of body energy/day

    A 6.4x raise, on the grounds section 118 establishes: 0.311 %/day is
    1/6 to 1/16 of copepod respiration, the starvation window that set
    the old value does not bind (T_total stays inside the literature
    3-30 d across a 32-fold range of this parameter), and 2 %/day is
    where the respiration share reaches the literature order without
    hitting the extinction wall just above 5 %/day.

    No other parameter moved. `growth_rate` stays at 0.0913 (111),
    `natural_mortality` at 0.0025 (108), phytoplankton's `growth_rate`
    at 0.0375 - section 113's recommendation to raise that one was
    still open when this section was written and is APPLIED by 121.

119.2 It presupposes --mass-balance, and that is now a live problem
    Section 118.8 says to make this change with the mass-balanced growth
    term, because under the legacy term a higher metabolism is partly
    absorbed by fabricated biomass. `--mass-balance` is OFF by default
    (116), so as the repo now stands

      python3 train.py --project mareld2.yaml

    runs a zooplankton with 6.4x the metabolism inside a growth term
    that fabricates mass - a combination that is neither calibrated nor
    measured, and worse than either coherent state.

    This is the same shape as 110.5, and it was resolved there by the
    calibration ceasing to presuppose a setting. Here it does not. The
    options are to flip `DEFAULT_MASS_BALANCE` to True, or to revert
    this value. Flipping a default changes every run that does not pass
    the flag and is not a decision to take from a probe result, so it
    was left open.

119.3 Validation: one test turns red, and it is informative
    `tests/test_phyto_zoo_sanity.py::test_zoo_bounded_in_closed_phyto_zoo_system`
    FAILS. Suite 756 passed, 1 failed, 12 skipped (was 757/0/12).

    The test drives a closed phytoplankton + zooplankton world for 200
    ticks (~50 days) from 1000 t each and asserts zooplankton ends
    within a factor 0.03-100 of where it started. At rm 22.5 it ends at
    0.013 of start.

    Attribution, by re-running the same fixture across the rate and both
    growth terms (zoo end / start after 200 ticks):

      rm      legacy   mass-bal   legacy   mass-bal
              default  default    greedy   greedy
      3.5     14.22    1.18       41.31    1.37
      11.25    2.29    0.75        4.04    1.01
      22.5     0.013   0.011       2.52    0.97
      56.2     0.000   0.000       0.23    0.19
      band: PASS is 0.03-100

    The collapse is BEHAVIOURAL, not energetic. The fixture calls
    `env.step()` with no action provider, so the zooplankton makes no
    foraging decisions at all. Give it the viability rig's frozen
    `greedy` behaviour and rm 22.5 passes in both growth terms - and so
    does 56.2. What fails is a zooplankton that does not forage.

    The same table says something about the OLD value. At rm 3.5 with
    the legacy term, zooplankton grows 14x in 50 days WITHOUT FORAGING,
    and 41x with. A metabolism that cheap is why the contract was
    satisfiable; the test was not protecting an ecological property, it
    was measuring how little the metabolism mattered.

    The same fixture defect shows up a second time in a contract that
    still passes. `test_predation_visibly_suppresses_phyto` requires
    zooplankton to depress phytoplankton by more than 0.3 % relative to
    a no-zooplankton baseline:

      rm      phyto alone   with zoo   suppression   margin
      3.5       21279.6     18985.6     10.78 %      x35.9
      11.25     21279.6     20437.9      3.96 %      x13.2
      22.5      21279.6     21174.3      0.50 %       x1.6

    Grazing in the default-action fixture is now barely detectable: one
    more step and that test goes red as well, for the same reason. A
    world where a decision maker does not forage is one where predation
    pressure does not exist, which is what both contracts are really
    measuring.

    Two other test files step decision makers with no action provider -
    `test_population_stability.py` and `test_ecosystem_refactor.py` - so
    whatever is decided here has a scope beyond this one file. Neither
    failed.

    NOT ACTED ON. The fixture, not the threshold, is what looks wrong -
    "the ecosystem must be stable when its decision makers do not
    decide" is a statement about the default-action path, not an
    ecological contract - and the repo-standard fix would be to install
    `greedy` and leave the 0.03-100 band untouched. But editing a test
    so a parameter fits is the inversion this whole arc has been
    correcting, so it is a decision to take deliberately and not a
    side effect of a calibration. The suite is left red.

    Both plankton groups now sit at 3-8 % of their `mareld2.yaml` spawn

    ratio of 0.44:1. Section 113.9 argued those spawn levels look

    capacity, zooplankton at 0.44 of it. So the model now gets the

    wrong by a factor 15-30.

    The obvious next combination is this value together with section
    113's phytoplankton 0.125, which 117 showed raises throughput 3.3x
    and zooplankton 3.2x while barely moving phytoplankton's own stock.

120 FIXTURE FIXED, --mass-balance ON BY DEFAULT, AND THE COMBINATION MEASURED (2026-09-29)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    The three decisions 119.7 left open, all taken.

120.1 The sanity fixture now forages
    `tests/test_phyto_zoo_sanity.py::_build_env` called `env.step()` with
    no action provider, so its zooplankton never made a foraging
    decision, and all four contracts in the file were measuring an
    ecosystem whose decision makers do not decide. It now installs the
    viability rig's frozen `greedy`, which is the repo's standard for
    behaviour-free measurement, and skips it for the phyto-only baseline
    that has no decision makers.

    THE BANDS ARE UNCHANGED. Only the behaviour is. That is the whole of
    the change: no threshold was widened to fit a parameter.

    Why the fixture and not the threshold, stated so the argument can be
    checked rather than trusted: at the OLD `resting_metabolism` of 3.5
    the non-foraging zooplankton grew 14x in 50 days, and 41x with
    greedy. The green state was the absurd one. The grazing-pressure
    contract in the same file said it from the other side - its margin
    against the 0.3 % threshold fell 36x -> 13x -> 1.6x as the
    metabolism went 3.5 -> 11.25 -> 22.5, because a grazer that does not
    forage exerts no grazing pressure, so that test was about to go red
    for the same reason.

    `test_population_stability.py` and `test_ecosystem_refactor.py` also
    step decision makers with no action provider. Neither failed and
    neither was touched; the same question applies to them.

120.2 --mass-balance is ON by default
    `DEFAULT_MASS_BALANCE = True`, and `EcosystemEnvironment`'s
    constructor default with it. The library is calibrated for that tick
    - zooplankton's `growth_rate` (111) and `resting_metabolism` (118)
    are both set in that world - so a run that passes no flag has to get
    it. 119.4 is the quantified version: with the legacy term at the
    current library, zooplankton converts mass at 45.6 % against a
    28.9 % thermodynamic ceiling and the energy budget over-accounts by
    105 %.

    `--mass-balance` is kept as a no-op so scripts written against
    section 116 keep working, and `--no-mass-balance` is the way back to
    the pre-116 tick. Its help text says the library is not calibrated
    for it.

    One thing that must NOT follow the default: what an OLD run was
    doing. `LEGACY_MASS_BALANCE = False` is a separate constant and
    `training_progress.comparable_config` defaults histories to it, so
    flipping the default cannot retroactively relabel a recorded run.
    Asserted by `test_legacy_constant_is_separate_from_the_default`.

    Caught while doing this, and worth recording because it is the same
    trap one level down: `tools/probes/growth_mass_balance.py` and
    `zoo_growth_sweep.py` each had their own `--mass-balance`
    `store_true` with an implicit default of False. After the flip they
    silently forced the LEGACY term - the first run of 120.3 came back
    with a -139 % closure gap before that was found. Both now default to
    `DEFAULT_MASS_BALANCE` and carry `--no-mass-balance`.

    Suite: 760 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed. Was 756/1/12 at the end of
    section 119.

122.2 Where the deck deviates from the May edition, and why
    One slide states these explicitly, because the May document is a
    draft to develop further and not a spec to conform to:

      growth term      mass-balanced and charged to the reserve (114-116,
                       120); the documented B*(1+MG*q) was free mass
      hunger           the May deck had BOTH the s > 0.8 eat mask and
                       h = max(0, 1 - s/0.8). The code kept the factor,
                       now per-FG via satiation_scale (69), and dropped
                       the mask. Remaining difference: mass that eats
                       while satiated still pays feeding_cost
      predation        Holling II/III + Beddington-DeAngelis (86), the
                       0.999 harvest cap (73), per-pair visibility
                       floors (71.12)
      fitness          mean_t log(E_tot(t)/E_tot(0)) with
                       E_tot = B*energy_content + R; alpha/beta survives
                       as --legacyreward only
      rollouts         15-200 ticks, not the documented H = 2
      training         co-evolution (all DMs perturbed in one shared
                       rollout) instead of the alternating schedule
      memory           the N(c,t-1) extension is not implemented; the
                       only cross-tick state is prev_hidden_frac
      size ladder      3x3 -> 60x60 is not the recommended flow; --grid
                       remains and the viability rig runs 20x20

    a run parameter (97, 103-106), currents, migration, the extinction
    threshold and split suppression (69), the local per-cell reward

124 APPLIED: ZOOPLANKTON feeding_cost 1.45 -> 2.0, max_energy_reserve
    450 -> 675 (2026-09-29)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

124.1 What was open
    The two zooplankton parameters 118.8, 120.4 and 121.4 left as not
    set from the literature: `feeding_cost` 1.45 (against a quoted
    "2-3x") and `max_energy_reserve` 450 MJ/t (10 % of body energy,
    fitted to a starvation window, and under --mass-balance also the
    growth ceiling ME/ec = 0.100 with growth_rate at 91 % of it,
    115.3/115.6). Plus 118.8's caveat that the copepod figures had been
    located by search and not read.

    Assemblage (decided by the user): a MIXED Skagerrak mesozooplankton,
    small neritic copepods (Acartia, Temora, Pseudocalanus, Centropages,
    Oithona) with a Calanus finmarchicus/helgolandicus component,
    weighted 2/3 : 1/3 by biomass. 8-12 C.

124.2 Literature
    Tags: [V] number read in the source (abstract or text), [2H] quoted
    second-hand, [C] computed (lipid 39.5 kJ/g, non-lipid 23.6 kJ/g).

    Feeding cost = respiration fed / respiration starved:
      Acartia tonsa        1.9          Thor 2000, JEMBE 245:171 [V/2H]
      A. clausi, C. helgo. 1.6-2.5      Svetlichny et al. 2022 [V]
      Temora/Acartia/Cent. ~2           Koski et al. 2017, PLoS ONE [V]
      -> band 1.8-2.5, central 2.0. The "2-3x" is Koski's TOTAL carbon
      demand of feeding calanoids (respiration + pellets + eggs), not a
      respiration ratio. Eggs are this model's growth term, so the
      respiration ratio is the one that belongs in feeding_cost.

    Storage lipid as a share of body energy:
      small neritic copepods   total lipid 3-7 % of DM (Kreibich 2008
                               [V], Svetlichny 2022 [V]), mostly
                               phospholipid -> mobilisable 3-6 % [C]
      Calanus CV active season 20-40 % lipid of DM (inferred; wax ester
                               ~90 % of lipid, Kattner & Krause 1987 [V])
                               -> 25-45 % of body energy [C]
      -> assemblage ~15 % (band 10-25 %).
    Starvation: lipid exhausted after ~3-7 d, mortality rises after
    ~1-2 weeks for the assemblage (Dagg 1977 [2H], Tsuda 1994 [2H],
    Kreibich 2008 [V], Niehoff 2000 [V]). Copepods respire 50-65 % of
    body carbon before death - most of it protein after the lipid is
    gone, which is the model's starve_rate phase, not the reserve.

    Resting rate (cross-check of 119, not changed): starved Acartia
    ~2.4 %/day at 10 C [C from Svetlichny]; in-situ Temora 3.9-6.0
    %/day (Castellani & Altunbas 2014 [V]); Ikeda et al. 2001 (fasting,
    units inferred, not read) predicts ~7.5 %/day for a 5 ug C copepod
    and ~3.2 %/day for a Calanus CV. So 22.5 MJ/t/tick = 2.0 %/day reads
    as the FASTING floor, and with feeding_cost 2.0 the feeding rate is
    4 %/day, inside the measured in-situ band. The two parameters are
    consistent without double-charging. 2.0 %/day stays at the low edge
    of the literature and is the one number here Ikeda would raise.

    Energy density: 4.1-5.4 kJ/g wet for the mix [C from Laurence 1976,
    McKinstry 2013, via 2H]; 4500 MJ/t unchanged.

    Not read in full (paywall): Lee, Hagen & Kattner 2006; Kiorboe et
    al. 1985; Ikeda et al. 2001; Tsuda 1994; Dagg 1977.

124.3 Checks
    Energy-balance gate: max allowed feeding_cost at rm 22.5 is
    h(u) * ceiling / rm = 0.375 * 325 / 22.5 = 5.42; 2.0 passes.

    tools/starve_calibration.py (PYTHONPATH=. needed when run directly):
      ME 450   T1 2.5 d   T_total 8.2 d
      ME 675   T1 3.8 d   T_total 8.8 d   (lit: lipid 3-7 d, death 1-2 w)

    Growth ceiling under --mass-balance: ME/ec 0.100 -> 0.150, so
    growth_rate 0.0913 is no longer at 91 % of the bound.

124.4 Measured
    tools/probes/growth_mass_balance.py, extended in this section with
    --zoo-fc, --zoo-me (the spawned reserve is rescaled so s_X(0) is
    unchanged), --behaviour policy --checkpoints DIR (configured spawn,
    trained policies), --migration and --currents. Default behaviour is
    unchanged.

    Run-to-run spread, found and FIXED in this section. The numbers below
    were measured before the fix, when repeated default runs with the
    same --seed gave zoo 9326-9589 t and phyto 3705-4077 t, about +-3 %.
    Cause: benthic_community has seed_rate 1e-06, and its recruitment
    noise (population_change.py, np.random.uniform) is drawn from NumPy's
    GLOBAL RNG, which inference.build_env never seeded - --seed reached
    the spawn only. Two runs differed from tick 0 (benthic, 6e-9
    relative) and the predator-prey dynamics amplified that to per cent
    over 3000 ticks. Isolated by elimination: fixed PYTHONHASHSEED and
    OMP/MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 still diverged; np.random.seed(0) gave
    bit-identical 3000-tick traces; benthic seed_rate 0 with the global
    RNG unseeded also gave bit-identical traces. The per-tick FG shuffle
    (environment.py, np.random.shuffle) uses the same RNG but does not
    change the result - every FG's update is independent of the order.

    Fix: build_env(seed=...) now also seeds the global RNG
    (np.random.seed(seed & 0xFFFFFFFF)); seed=None leaves it alone.
    Covers inference.py, tools/viability.py, api.py and every probe
    built on build_env. Training is untouched: train.py workers seed the
    global RNG per rollout (parallel_worker) and the GPU engine seeds in
    lib/gpu/config.py. After the fix two full growth_mass_balance.py
    runs print identical output. Regression test:
    tests/test_inference_determinism.py (fails without the fix).

    Consequences: differences under ~3 % between two single rollouts
    measured before this fix are noise - in the tables below that is the
    reserve's effect on the levels under trained policies (-4 %). The
    3 % also says something about the model: a 1e-5 t/cell/tick
    perturbation grows to per cent in 3000 ticks, so single-seed
    comparisons should use several seeds, not one.

    Trained policies (results/pzbpgp248nsrpfix35, migration + currents
    on, 3000 ticks, last 300):
      fc     ME     zoo t    phyto t   zoo:phyto   GGE wet   GGE carbon
      1.45   450    75322    44567     1.69:1      11.8 %    26.6 %
      2.0    450    65290    44364     1.47:1      10.8 %    24.3 %
      2.5    450    56493    44029     1.28:1       9.7 %    21.8 %
      2.0    675    62525    45454     1.38:1      10.6 %    23.9 %

125 GPU TRAINING: COST AND VALUE OF --n_deltas (2026-09-29)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

125.1 Cost
    New probe tools/probes/ars_delta_budget.py builds the trainer from
    train_gpu.py's own parser (flags after --) and times train_step per
    --n_deltas. RTX A3000 12 GB, 60x60, 3 worlds, migration + mortality +
    currents on, 2x48 tanh, --profile info:

      N     100 ticks s/upd   500 ticks s/upd   s/pair @500   peak VRAM
      1          0.46               -               -          0.09 GiB
      2          0.80               -               -          0.18 GiB
      4          1.51              7.37            1.84         0.33 GiB
      8          2.95             14.85            1.86         0.64 GiB
      16         5.82             30.39            1.90         1.27 GiB
      32        11.75             63.84            2.00         1.28 GiB*
      64          OOM            124.35            1.94         1.30 GiB*
      * with --pairs-per-batch 16

    The GPU is saturated from ~2-4 pairs (24 worlds of 3600 cells); from
    there every pair costs the same, ~0.37 s per 100 ticks, so there is
    no free range to fill. VRAM is ~80 MB per simultaneous pair; 64 pairs
    in one batch runs out of memory, --pairs-per-batch caps it at the
    same cost per pair.

125.2 Value: what the cosine of independent steps measures
    Six independent ARS steps from the same weights
    (results/pzbpgp248nsrpfix35), 500 ticks, pairwise cosine per DM:
    within +-0.01 of zero for every DM at N = 4..64, i.e. at the noise
    floor 1/sqrt(d) = 0.016. First read as "no gradient signal"; that
    was WRONG. An ARS step is a sum over N random directions in
    d ~ 3500-3950 dimensions, so even with noise-free rewards two
    independent steps agree only to E[cos] = N/(N+d) - 0.004 at N = 16,
    0.016 at N = 64. The sweep measured the dimensionality, not noise.
    The probe now prints that reference instead of a fitted N0.

    Controls at N = 16 (trained policies, 4 repeats):
      held fixed           gadoids  pelagic  porpoises  zooplankton
      worlds + deltas       1.000    1.000     1.000      1.000   (probe ok)
      worlds only          -0.001   +0.007    +0.005     -0.003
      deltas only          +0.481   +0.386    +0.529     +0.885
    Fresh (untrained) policies, nothing fixed: 0.004-0.015 at N = 16 and
    64 - again the dimensional level.

    Reading: the delta draw is what makes two steps differ; the world
    draw costs only part of the agreement - the same deltas in new
    worlds still point 0.39-0.89 the same way. So the rewards DO rank
    the directions reproducibly; zooplankton most, pelagic_fish least.

125.3 What N buys
    With ARS-V2's normalisation, lr / (b * sigma_f), the component of
    each step along the true gradient is roughly independent of N; what
    a larger N (b = N/2) shrinks is the random sideways component, as
    1/sqrt(b) - measured: |step| 1.2 at N = 16, 0.6 at N = 64, same lr.
    Cost is linear in N. So more deltas buy a straighter path, not a
    longer stride, at proportional wall-clock. This is the geometric
    argument, not a measured learning curve: the decisive test is equal
    wall-clock training runs at N = 8 / 16 / 32, not done.

125.4 Are the perturbations run at the same time? Yes - and why that
    does not make them free
    --pairs-per-batch defaults to n_deltas, so every perturbation pair
    and every world of an update is already one batch on the GPU. The
    time is linear in N because the GPU is COMPUTE-saturated, not
    memory-bound: nvidia-smi sampled every 0.5 s during an N = 16,
    100-tick run read 100 % utilisation in 44 of 50 samples.

    The OOM at N = 64 is the CUDA-graph execution, not the model:
      N = 64, 96 ticks        s/pair   peak / outcome
      --execution cuda-graph    -      OOM: 11.3 GiB allocated, 7.3 GiB
                                       of it in CUDA-graph private pools
      --execution eager       0.366    5.00 GiB
      (N = 16: cuda-graph 0.348 s/pair, eager 0.360 - graphs buy ~3 %)
    --graph-ticks 32 / 8 / 4 all OOM at N = 64 and time identically at
    N = 16, so the pool size does not follow the captured tick count.

    Practical: up to N ~ 32 the default cuda-graph path fits; above it
    use --execution eager (~5 GiB at N = 64, so roughly N ~ 128 fits in
    12 GB) or keep cuda-graph with --pairs-per-batch 32. Either way the
    cost per pair is the same ~0.36 s per 100 ticks.

126 THE VIABILITY RIG DEMOTED TO A DIAGNOSTIC; DECK FORMULAS AS MATH
    (2026-09-30)
---------------------------------------------------------------------

126.1 Why
    Section 123 showed trained policies keeping gadoids, pelagic_fish and
    phytoplankton viable over 10 000 ticks where the rig's normative
    corner (--spawn colocated --behaviour greedy) fails all three. The
    premise VIABILITY.md was written on - "if the world fails the rig,
    no amount of training can fix it" - is therefore false. greedy is an
    upper bound on per-tick intake, not on persistence: every group
    taking the most it can over-exploits the shared resource (phyto at
    ~0.05x spawn under greedy, ~0.56x stationary under trained policies).

126.2 VIABILITY.md
    - Intro: the question is viability with the behaviour the world will
      run with; the rig is a diagnostic for the mechanics, fast and
      deterministic, not the judge. The converse still holds: failing
      both frozen and trained (today porpoises) is structural.
    - Section 1: stationarity (two-window ratio) flagged as unable to
      tell a slide from a cycle; the trained gadoid cycle (1.0-3.1x,
      last-two-quarters ratio 0.44) would fail max_drift 2.0. A
      cycle-tolerant test is proposed, not implemented.
    - Section 2 renamed "What the rig's verdict means"; section 4's
      "a FAIL in the normative corner closes the question" replaced by
      "closes it only if trained policies fail too".
    - New section 6: measuring viability with trained policies, via
      tools/viability.py --behaviour policy (verified: per-arm PASS/FAIL,
      overall NO VERDICT, exit 0) or a long inference.py rollout; the
      123 table frozen vs trained; the rig has no --currents flag.
    Code unchanged: the policy arm still never decides the exit code.
    AGENTS.md's two viability lines toned down accordingly.

126.3 Strategy deck (section 122)
    - Part 7 "Acceptanskriterier" -> "Diagnostik och livskraft"; the

    - Formula slides (steps 2-5, 7 x2, fitness, local reward, ARS) are

127 LIVE VIEWER: PLOT COST NO LONGER GROWS WITH ROLLOUT LENGTH (2026-10-01)

127.1 Symptom and cause
    Inference --visual rollouts past ~10000 ticks dropped to a few fps
    (and, since rendering runs in the simulation thread, the tick rate
    dropped with it). The heatmaps and status bar are constant cost;
    _draw_plot was O(N) per frame. Inference keeps every tick in the
    plot buffers (unbounded), and each frame (a) scanned every point of
    every series in Python for the y-range, (b) scanned forward from
    tick 0 for the visible window, and (c) when zoomed out, handed all
    N points to pygame.draw.aalines. Measured on 16 series: 1 ms at
    t=0, 42 ms at 10000, 72 ms at 20000 (live window), 1.4 s per frame
    at 20000 zoomed out. 10000 ticks is roughly where the plot alone
    passes the 33 ms frame budget (fps_cap 30), hence "drastic at 10k".

127.2 Fix (lib/viz/pygame_viz.py)
    - _SeriesBuffer replaces deque for every plot tab except "progress"
      (still a list). Growable int64 steps / float64 values, optional
      maxlen (train mode keeps reward_window), deque-compatible append /
      clear / len / iter / [i]; arrays() returns numpy views and
      is_sorted tracks non-decreasing steps.
    - _draw_plot: y-range and visible-window slicing via searchsorted
      (mask fallback when a series is not sorted), coordinates computed
      vectorised with the same int truncation and clipping as before.
    - _decimate_polyline: when a series has more than 2 points per
      pixel column, each column is collapsed to first/min/max/last.
      Pixel-exact, since segments inside one column are vertical.
    - Tooltip lookup uses searchsorted.
    - A NaN/inf neighbour just outside the window used to raise in
      int() and drop the whole frame; such points are now skipped.
    Old vs new rendering compared pixel by pixel (live, zoomed out, log
    scale, action tab, train reward with maxlen, tooltip): identical.

127.3 Result
    draw_plot at 20000 ticks, 16 series, realistic data: live window
    37.8 -> 3.6 ms, zoomed out 366 -> 43 ms; flat in N. What remains
    is aalines ink (proportional to drawn pixel length, not to N).
    A 12000-tick headless inference --visual run kept a steady
    ~13-17 s per 1200 ticks to the end. Test:
    tests/test_viz_series_buffer.py.

127.4 Inference rollouts up to 50000 ticks
    The rollout-length slider (and --ticks when --visual is on, via
    set_ticks_default) was clamped to 25000. _ticks_max is now 50000 in
    inference mode; train mode keeps 25000. Without --visual, --ticks was
    never capped.
    The recorded film used to keep at most 10000 frames by deleting every
    other frame in place each time it overflowed, while new frames kept
    arriving at full rate - so a long rollout became a film whose early
    part was sparse and late part dense. Now the overflow also doubles a
    capture stride (_capture_stride), so frames stay evenly spaced in
    ticks (50000 ticks -> stride 8, ~6250 frames), and
    end_rollout_recording appends the final state when the last tick
    fell between two captures. Cap: LiveVisualizer._MAX_ROLLOUT_FRAMES.

128 ACTION-LEVEL SHAPING OFF BY DEFAULT, NOT ONLY IN THE PROFILES (2026-10-02)
    The three --profile presets (sanity/info/deep) set entropy_coef 0,
    argmax_penalty 0, temp_start = temp_end = 1 and uniform_bias_init
    off, but a run without --profile still got entropy_coef 0.1,
    argmax_penalty 0.3 and softmax-temperature annealing 3.0 -> 1.0 over
    10 generations. Those terms act on the action distribution, not on
    the biology (section 7 of AGENTS.md), so the ordinary defaults now
    match the profiles:
        train.py        --entropy_coef 0.0, --argmax_penalty 0.0,
                        --temp_start 1.0 (was 0.1 / 0.3 / 3.0)
        train_gpu.py    --temp-start 1.0 (was 3.0)
        lib/gpu/cli.py  --entropy-coef 0.0, --argmax-penalty 0.0
    temp_end (1.0) and uniform_bias_init (off) were already neutral;
    with temp_start == temp_end, temp_anneal_gens has no effect. The
    flags remain for explicit opt-in; the former behaviour is
    --entropy_coef 0.1 --argmax_penalty 0.3 --temp_start 3. The profiles
    still list the same keys, so they are now no-ops for these settings
    unless a user flag overrides them - explicit flags still win.
    Updated: tests/test_training_profiles.py (no-profile expectations),
    GPU_TRAINING.md, AGENTS.md, and the "Profiler och formande termer"
    table in both deck generators (the PDFs are not rebuilt).

129 GROWTH_RATE DERIVED FROM A LITERATURE BUDGET AND THE PREDATION MATRIX
    (2026-10-03)
------------------------------------------------------------------------

129.1 What changed
    growth_rate is no longer a free per-FG number. lib/world/growth_budget.py
    derives it, and the loader (both FG builders, before the tick rescale)
    and the FG editor call the same function:

      DM   g = (r_max + M1 + sum_j M2_ij) / ((min(satiation_scale,1) - u) * 1460)
      NDM  r = (r_max + sum_j M2_ij) / 1460

    r_max     new species key, 1/yr. DM: literature maximum NET population
              growth at low density. NDM: net growth after natural mortality
              and predation by groups that are not FGs.
    M1        natural_mortality (per tick, converted with the loss rule). It
              now holds ONLY losses that are not predation by an FG: M0,
              predation by non-FG groups, and predation by NDMs (they cannot
              hunt in the tick).
    M2_ij     new pair key predation_mortality, 1/yr: literature predation
              mortality of prey i caused by FG j. Counted while preys_on is
              true, the predator is a DM and the predator is active (unmuted)
              in the project.
    Checking a predator raises the prey's g by its share, unchecking lowers
    it; net low-density growth stays r_max. An FG without r_max keeps its
    stored growth_rate (legacy).

129.2 Values (report: reports/Litteraturbaserad growth rate per FG.md)
    M and M2 come from the North Sea 1991 Ecopath model (Mackinson &
    Daskalov 2007), with every species under the umbrella terms. The diet
    matrix was parsed from the PDF and validated against the report's own
    EE-based M2; rows 24-25 are duplicated and several gadoid columns do not
    sum to 1 in the printed table. r_max comes from FishBase CMSY priors
    (fish), from observed recovery (seals, porpoise), Niel & Lebreton
    (seabirds), Huntley & Lopez (copepods), Hiddink 2017 (benthos), and
    Kattegat 14C PP (phytoplankton).
      FG            r_max   M1/yr   checked M2 on it         g (mareld2)
      phyto          5.66     -     zoo 22.63                0.0194
      zooplankton   33.4    19.7    pelagic 5.24             0.0799
      benthic        0.82     -     gadoids 0.0048           5.65e-4
      pelagic_fish   0.648   0.580  gad 0.300 porp 0.012     0.00211
      gadoids        0.511   0.683  porp 0.056               0.00171
      porpoises      0.10    0.10   -                        2.74e-4

130 SATIATION_SCALE REMOVED; LOADER DROPS M1 FROM g WHEN MORTALITY IS OFF
    (2026-10-03)

130.1 satiation_scale removed
    The hunger gate is h = max(0, 1 - s) for every FG. Gone:
    HUNGER_SATIATION_SCALE and resolve_satiation_scale (energy_balance.py),

    growth_budget.max_gate = 1 - u. A stale key in an old library is
    ignored by FunctionalGroup and dropped by the FG editor on apply.
    Reason: below 1 the top of the literature max_energy_reserve was never
    reachable; above 1 (porpoises 1.37) a satiated FG kept eating and the
    reserve clip discarded the surplus. Porpoise feeding_cost 1.1 (129)
    keeps its budget closed under h = 1 - s.

131 PHYTOPLANKTON r = LOW-DENSITY IN SITU RATE, NOT THE ANNUAL MEAN
    (2026-10-03)
------------------------------------------------------------------------

131.1 The error
    Section 129 set phytoplankton r_max 5.66 /yr (g 0.0194 /tick): annual
    14C PP over mean biomass in Kattegat/Skagerrak (0.31 d-1) minus every
    loss. That is a steady-state remainder; a logistic population near K
    realises r(1 - B/K), so the remainder is ~0 by construction - the same
    error that gave benthos r = 4e-6 before it was corrected to Hiddink's
    low-density recovery rate. It cut rK/4 to 0.12 t/cell/tick (0.75 at the
    old 0.125) and made test_phyto_zoo_sanity::test_zoo_bounded fail (zoo
    0.027x in 200 ticks). Diagnosis: restoring 0.125 alone gave 2.04x, the
    old zoo M1 alone 0.066x.

131.2 The value (user decision)
    Logistic r = highest in situ growth from dilution experiments, 0.67 d-1
    (Stelfox-Widdicombe et al. 2004, southern North Sea, April, 7-9.5 C),
    minus microzooplankton grazing 60 % (Calbet & Landry 2004) = 0.27 d-1 =
    0.067 /tick = 97.8 /yr. The zooplankton pair supplies 22.63, so
    r_max = 75.2 /yr and g = 0.0670068 /tick. Sinking/lysis not subtracted
    (would give ~0.055). rK/4 = 0.40 t/cell/tick.

131.3 Validation and open points
    Suite: 777 passed, 0 failed (zoo 1.07x, min 0.70x in the closed test -
    a diagnostic, not the basis of the value). One-generation training run.
    Open: one source, spring, southern North Sea; no seasonal forcing
    (seasonal_amplitude 0), so spring-like growth applies all year; K = 24
    t/cell not reviewed.

132.2 Zooplankton collapse in run pzbpgp248nsrpfix39 (train_gpu, mass
    balance, mortality, migration, currents on)
    Replaying its policies on CPU: mass balance OFF -> zoo 1.11x after 300
    ticks (s 0.68); ON -> 0.10x (s 0.56): production 0.0093 /tick against
    M1 0.0134 + predation 0.0037. Pelagic fish then starve (99 %).

    gut timescales, appetite should stay ~1 until reserves are nearly full;
    phyto 2 kJ/g WW is the large-diatom end (Ecopath 4.8); zoo->phyto

    0.26; feeding cost x2 vs >4x. Options and table:
    reports/Zooplankton energibudget.md. Nothing changed in the model.

134 ZOOPLANKTON -> PHYTOPLANKTON HALF-SATURATION 20 t/km2 (2026-10-03)
------------------------------------------------------------------------

134.1 Mechanism
    * Holling II f(B) = aB/(1 + ahB): ceiling 1/h, half-saturation 1/(ah).
      The library convention h = 1/a made every pair's half-saturation
      exactly 1 t/km2 and made a equal to the ceiling.
    * interactions.py now reads a pair-level max_intake_rate (attack rate)
      as an override of the species value; tick_time already rescaled the
      pair key (INTERACTION_RESCALE_RULES) but the matrix builder ignored
      it. Legacy pair keys (porpoises->gadoids 0.035, seals->pelagic 0.05)
      equal their species values, so nothing else moves.
    * energy_balance.intake_ceiling(a, h) = 1/h (a when h = 0). The GUI
      energy gate, the live-project gate tests and budget_gate.py use it
      instead of max_intake_rate.

134.2 Value
    zooplankton_preys_on_phytoplankton: max_intake_rate 0.0125, h 4 ->
    ceiling 0.25 t/t/tick (unchanged), half-saturation 20 t/km2
    (literature ~5-60 g WW/m2 for a 10-20 m feeding layer).
    tests/test_half_saturation.py; suite 783 passed.

134.3 Effect (mareld2, mass balance, mortality, migration, currents,
    1000 ticks, pre-133 policies): zoo 0.66x, pelagic 1.45x, phyto
    settles at 3-5 t/cell instead of crashing to 0.5-0.8. Losses now
    mostly M1 (zoo 75 %, pelagic 93 %). Greedy still loses pelagic fish.
    Porpoises starve in every run; gadoids eat 92-98 % benthos. Open:
    option 4 of reports/Zooplankton energibudget.md (zoo GGE ~0.26).
    Retrain policies.

135 ZOOPLANKTON feeding_cost 2.0 -> 4.0: RESPIRATION + EXCRETION (2026-10-03)
------------------------------------------------------------------------

135.1 Definition (user decision)
    feeding_cost now means respiration + excretion while feeding, in
    multiples of the fasting rate. Kiorboe, Mohlenberg & Hamburger 1985:
    both "more than 4 times higher" in saturation-fed than in starved
    Acartia tonsa. The model has no excretion term (NH4, DOC), so that
    loss belongs here. This SUPERSEDES the feeding-cost reasoning of
    124.2 (respiration-only ratio 1.6-2.5 -> 2.0; Thor 2000, Svetlichny
    2022, Koski 2017); the rest of 124 (reserve, energy content, resting
    rate) stands. Value 4.0 = the lower bound of the Kiorboe band.
    Kiorboe 2018's mf/m0 = 6.7 includes defecation, already booked as
    1 - assimilation, so it is not an upper bound.

135.2 Cross-check (not the basis)
    Steady-state GGE = AE * P*ec / (metabolism + P*ec) with P = 0.016
    /tick (M1 + fish predation): 0.40 at 2.0, 0.29-0.31 at 4.0 (Straile
    1997: mean 0.26, IQR 0.13-0.35). Feeding metabolism 7-8 %/day of body
    energy, top of the field routine band (3-7 %/day at 10 C).

135.3 Effect (mareld2, mass balance, mortality, migration, currents,
    1000 ticks, pre-133 policies): zoo 0.66x, pelagic 1.44x, phyto 5.6
    t/cell (at 2.0: 0.66x, 1.45x, 5.0). Greedy: zoo 0.32x, pelagic lost.
    Energy gate passes (ceiling 780 vs feeding cost 90). Suite 783 passed.
    Options 1-4 of reports/Zooplankton energibudget.md are now all
    applied. Still open: porpoises starve in every run; gadoids eat
    92-98 % benthos.

137 DAYLIGHT CALENDAR: LIGHT-DEPENDENT ATTACK RATES (2026-10-04)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
137.1 Why
    Visual predators (herring on zooplankton) detect prey far better in
    light than in darkness; zooplankton answers with diel vertical
    migration (DVM). The CAUSE is put in the model, not the response:
    the predator's attack rate a depends on light, and the prey's DVM is
    left to the policies (Rest = hide, which also stops grazing - the
    real cost of DVM). Observability and visibility_floor are unchanged:
    they say what a DM knows and how well hiding works; light only says
    how dangerous it is to be visible. In the Holling/BD response a and
    the visible prey biomass enter only as the product a*B, so scaling a
    is the same as scaling non-hidden visibility, without a second knob.

137.2 Model (lib/world/daylight.py)
    f(elev) = logistic((elev - theta) / 2 deg), elev = sun elevation at
    local solar time (declination 23.44 sin(2 pi (284 + n)/365)).
    F(t) = mean of f over the tick in 10-min sub-steps (f is strongly
    nonlinear, so mean f, not f of the mean). Per pair with dark_ratio
    rho < 1: m(t) = (rho + (1 - rho) F(t)) / annual mean of the same, so
    the library max_intake_rate IS the annual mean a and the growth
    budget (section 129) and budget_gate hold on average. Elevation, not
    lux: a fish's visual range grows with log(light) and saturates at
    twilight levels (Aksnes & Giske 1993; Aksnes & Utne 1997), so f is
    ~1 by day, ~0 by night and moves through twilight. Clouds ignored.
    Calendar: year tick k starts at hour k * tick_hours after 1 Jan
    00:00 solar time; 8760 h divides by every tick length 1-6, so the
    schedule is exactly periodic. Run tick t = year tick
    (start_tick + t) % ticks_per_year.

137.3 Settings
    Manifest: simulation_settings.daylight {enabled, latitude_deg,
    start_day_of_year: 1-365 | random}. mareld2.yaml ships enabled:
    false, latitude 58.15 (Mareld / Poseidon Nord, coordinates.txt).
    Library, per pair, both dimensionless and tick-independent:
    dark_ratio (absent or >= 1 = no light dependence; the column is then
    exactly 1.0, not 1 via the normalisation) and light_threshold_deg
    (default -6, end of civil twilight). FG editor: two matrices (Dark
    Ratio, Light Threshold) under Visibility Floor, and a Daylight row
    in the project header validated with the loader's own parser.
    Only pelagic_fish -> zooplankton is set: dark_ratio 0.1,
    threshold -8 deg. Herring bite zooplankton by sight down to
    0.001 lx (Batty, Blaxter & Richard 1990, Mar Biol 107:383); their
    stomach fullness peaks after dawn and before dusk and they switch
    to filter feeding at night (Darbyson et al. 2003, J Fish Biol).
    rho 0.1 is an estimate consistent with that, not a measured ratio
    - the first number to revisit. 0.001 lx at 10-40 m with
    Kd ~0.15/m is 0.005-0.4 lx at the surface, a sun 8-12 deg below the
    horizon. Seabirds, gadoids and seals have no values yet.

137.4 Engine
    Loader puts the same params['daylight'] = {latitude_deg,
    tick_hours, start_tick, random_start} on every FG, so all ~50 env
    construction sites get it without new arguments. A random start is
    drawn from spawn_seed (pseudo-FG '__daylight__'): every delta of a
    generation sees the same season (CRN). state.build_static_caches ->
    interactions.build_daylight_tables: env._has_daylight,
    _has_light_pairs, light_obs_table (T,), light_mult_table (T, N_dm,
    N_all). predation and the viability rig read
    interactions.attack_rate(env). Observation: one channel, F of the
    tick at the default threshold, appended LAST to every DM's compact
    layout (in_dim + 1), so everything before it keeps its slot;
    train.get_dynamic_policy_params mirrors it. GPU: TensorEcosystem
    mirrors both (light_index per world), RolloutRunner keeps a
    light_start buffer, WorldSpawner.light_starts draws it from the world
    keys (stream 503), shared by both ARS signs.
    Turning the calendar on or off changes in_dim by 1: checkpoints do
    not carry over; inference.py says so in the mismatch hint.

137.5 Validation
    Disabled: 30-tick rollout hash on mareld2 identical to HEAD
    (sha c6855a7f...), in_dim unchanged. tests/test_daylight.py (annual
    mean exactly 1 for tick 1-6 at 0/58/70 N, solstice elevations,
    loader/CRN, light slot, predation = a*m(t)); test_gpu_ecosystem
    daylight parity on CPU and CUDA (shifting the GPU index by one tick
    fails it). Suite green. 1-gen train.py, train_gpu.py and inference
    with a daylight-enabled copy of the manifest run.

137.6 Effect on herring's attack rate at 58.15 N (6 h ticks;
    tools/probes/daylight_table.py): a_light 1.54 a, a_dark 0.15 a.
    Monthly mean m: Jan 0.70 Feb 0.80 Mar 0.94 Apr 1.10 May 1.30
    Jun 1.42 Jul 1.36 Aug 1.17 Sep 0.99 Oct 0.84 Nov 0.72 Dec 0.66.
    In June the midnight sun is only -8.5 deg, so night ticks keep
    m ~ 1.3; in December two of four ticks are fully dark.

137.7 Open
    - Not trained with the calendar on yet; no biological results.
    - Run budget_gate against the winter low (m 0.66 in Dec): herring's
      winter break-even density rises by 1/0.66.
    - The phytoplankton seasonal term still uses its own random phase
      (seasonal_amplitude 0 in the library); tie it to this calendar
      before switching it on, or bloom and daylength drift apart.
    - 2D limitation: depth is collapsed, so night = prey shallow but
      unseen and day = seen but deep both become one encounter factor;
      herring's twilight feeding window is only approximated by F.
    - Policies see light but not the date; anticipatory seasonal
      strategies are out of reach at n_eval_ticks 15 anyway.

138 LIGHT-LIMITED PHYTOPLANKTON ON THE DAYLIGHT CALENDAR (2026-10-04)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
138.1 What changed
    The NDM sine forcing (seasonal_amplitude / seasonal_period, random
    phase per env, amplitude 0 in the library) is REMOVED everywhere:
    FunctionalGroup, population_change, env._season_phase, the GPU
    engine (amplitude/period tensors, the per-world ``phase`` argument
    of import_state / step / population, RolloutRunner's phase buffer,
    WorldSpawner.phases), tick_time (the "period" rescale rule had no
    other key and went with it), the FG editor fields, the library keys
    and tools/probes/dm_seasonal_reproduction.py, which was built on
    it. GPU signatures: import_state -> (b, r, hidden); step(b, r,
    actions, tick, seed_multiplier, ..., light_index);
    population(b, r, seed_multiplier, light_index); runner.reset(b, r,
    keys, ticks, mean, var, temperature, light_start=None).
    Side effect: the env constructor no longer draws from the global
    numpy RNG, so seeded rollouts are not bit-identical to before.

138.2 Model (lib/world/daylight.py, section 137 calendar)
    A non-decision maker with light_saturation (I_k) grows at
        r(t) = growth_rate * P(t) / P_ref
        P(t) = mean over the tick (10-min steps) and over the mixed
               layer (40 mid-points) of tanh(I0 exp(-Kd z) / I_k)
               (Jassby & Platt 1976)
        I0   = Haurwitz (1945) clear-sky global radiation x 0.45 PAR
               share x 4.57 umol/J (McCree 1972) x monthly cloud
               transmission
    P_ref = daily mean of P on light_reference_day (105, mid April):
    growth_rate is the April dilution-experiment rate of section 131,
    so the factor is 1 on that day, not 1 as an annual mean (unlike the
    attack-rate multiplier of 137). P = 0 at night. Monthly inputs are
    interpolated circularly between mid-month points. I_k may be one
    value or 12 monthly values (photoacclimation). Needs the site light
    climate in the manifest; a light-limited NDM without it raises.
    The growth multiplier also exists for NDM-only projects (the
    calendar runs without the DM light channel). growth_budget and the
    derived growth_rate are unchanged: the factor multiplies them.

138.3 Values (subagent research from primary monitoring data; most
    are DERIVED, not stated in a publication)
    Kd(PAR) 0.29 /m: Kd = 2.5 / Secchi (Aas, Hokedal & Sorensen 2014,
      Ocean Sci 10:177, Table 8) with Skagerrak Secchi 8.3 m (Aarup
      2002, Oceanologia 44:323) and SMHI SHARK 1990-2024 median 8.5 m.
      Monthly 0.25 (Jul) - 0.42 (Feb-Mar); one annual value used.
    Mixed layer (m, Jan..Dec) 13 9 6 6 6 6 6 7 10 10 17 15: SHARK CTD at
      A17 (58.28 N 10.50 E) 1992-2024, density threshold 0.125 kg/m3
      from the surface sample (de Boyer Montegut et al. 2004). Apr-Jun
      '<5-7 m' (bottle spacing) set to 6; Dec median 8 is sampling noise
      and replaced by the Nov/Jan mean. The Baltic outflow keeps a
      halocline all winter (0-50 m delta-sigma >= 1.3 in January), so
      winter darkness for the algae comes from the sun and the clouds,
      not from deep mixing. IMR Arendal 2017-2019 agrees (3-21 m).
    Cloud transmission (Jan..Dec) .66 .66 .73 .78 .75 .74 .74 .73 .70
      .66 .60 .69: SMHI Nordkoster (58.89 N) monthly mean global
      radiation 2011-2025 over the Haurwitz clear sky at that latitude.
    I_k (Jan..Dec) 114 132 161 165 208 248 298 257 193 149 111 113
      umol photons/m2/s: medians of Pmax/alpha from SMHI 14C P-I curves

    Bloom timing check: Feb-Mar diatom bloom (Gran-Stadniczenko et al.
      2019, J Eukaryot Microbiol 66:494), secondary Oct-Nov at A17.

139 EXPOSURE-WEIGHTED M1 (DEPTH RISK) - MECHANISM IN, LIBRARY OFF (2026-10-05)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
139.1 Why
    Run pzbpgp248nsrpfix43 (train_gpu, daylight on, floor 0.2) learned
    no diel vertical migration: zooplankton rests ~0.8 around the clock
    (day-night difference <= 0.05 in every month). Realised herring
    predation on zoo was 2.13 /yr against the budget's 5.24 (= the
    visible fraction 1 - 0.8 * 0.8), gadoid predation on herring 0.91
    against 0.31, herring starvation 1.04 /yr. Literature (subagent,
    mostly DERIVED from Mackinson & Daskalov 2007, North Sea Ecopath
    1991; Hirst & Kiorboe 2002; Maud et al. 2018): only ~2 of zoo's
    M1 19.7 /yr is visual (fish larvae, Norway pout, 0-group), ~10-15
    tactile (chaetognaths, gelatinous), 2.5-8.3 non-predation; tactile
    predators hunt where zoo hides by day (Tonnesson & Tiselius 2005,
    Gullmarsfjorden, abstract only; Ohman, Frost & Cohen 1983).

139.2 Mechanism (lib/environments/ecosystem_env/natural_mortality.py)
    Per tick and cell, pi = this tick's rest (hiding) fraction:
      M1(t,c) = M1 [ (1 - s_v - s_t) + s_v V/V_ref + s_t D/D_ref ]
      V = (1 - pi (1 - phi)) m(t),  D = (1 - pi) + rho pi
    phi = the FG's visibility_floor, m(t) = daylight attack multiplier
    (m1_visual_dark_ratio 0.1, m1_visual_threshold_deg -6; 1 without
    the calendar), refs at hide_reference (default 0.5) and annual-mean
    light, so M1 averages to natural_mortality at pi_ref and the
    growth budget is unchanged. Keys per DM species: m1_visual_share,
    m1_tactile_share, depth_risk_ratio, hide_reference (editor: 0 means
    default), m1_visual_dark_ratio, m1_visual_threshold_deg. Inert (and
    bit-identical) unless a share is set. CPU population_change and the
    GPU population() (needs this tick's hidden fraction, now passed from
    step) agree; env.loss_natural_parts books visual/tactile/other.
    FG editor: four fields under Natural Mortality.

139.3 Viability gate (tools/probes/depth_risk_viability.py): trained
    policies of pzbpgp248nsrpfix43 for every DM, zooplankton's hiding
    replaced by frozen schedules; 20x20, migration + currents +
    mortality on, 1460 ticks, 2 seeds; s_v 2/19.7, s_t 10/19.7.
        M1        schedule  zoo end  zoo mean  zoo min  M2 herring
        constant  trained    1.21     0.73     0.084     2.33
        constant  flat80     0.22     0.49     0.056     3.13
        constant  dvm80      0.25     0.49     0.050     2.92
        constant  flat50     0.35     0.35     0.037     3.84
        constant  dvm50      0.56     0.28     0.026     4.13
        rho 2     trained    1.16     0.69     0.082     2.42
        rho 2     flat80     0.15     0.45     0.051     3.38
        rho 2     dvm80      0.19     0.47     0.050     3.06
        rho 4     trained    1.10     0.66     0.079     2.51
        rho 4     flat80     0.15     0.38     0.086     3.96
    (50 % schedules are identical for every rho: pi = pi_ref.) Herring
    ends at 0.00-0.06 in every row.
    Readings:
    - The gate set before implementing (dvm beats constant hiding at
      rho 2) FAILS: no frozen schedule is viable, dvm vs flat at equal
      mean changes the zoo mean by <= 0.02, dvm50 vs flat80 is mixed
      (higher end, lower mean and minimum).
    - The trained, state-dependent policy beats every frozen schedule.
      Its ~0.8 rest is grazing restraint, not predator avoidance:
      flat50 doubles grazing (3.8-4.4 vs 1.8 kt per 3 days on 20x20),
      phytoplankton falls 7.4 -> 0.7 kt in 15 days and zoo starves.
      Zoo's grazing capacity exceeds phytoplankton's maximum production
      (rK/4) about twofold, so the population boom-busts unless it
      rests; the shared policy learns restraint at the population level.
    - Depth risk costs the trained policy ~5 % (rho 2) to ~10 % (rho 4)
      of mean zoo biomass and raises herring's realised M2 only
      2.33 -> 2.42-2.51. DVM timing alone lowers herring M2 (3.13 ->
      2.92) - the light-dependent herring attack rate already rewards
      it - but the gain is small next to the food dynamics.
    Decision: mechanism and tests stay, fg_library.yaml is NOT changed
    (no shares set). The open problems are food-side: zoo grazing
    capacity vs phyto production, herring starvation in winter.

140 HERRING: FLOOR SWEEP, OVERWINTERING, LEAN/RESERVE SPLIT (2026-10-05)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
140.1 Floor sweep (tools/probes/depth_risk_viability.py --floors):
    trained policies of pzbpgp248nsrpfix43, 20x20, migration+currents+
    mortality, 1460 ticks, 3 seeds. herring -> zoo visibility_floor
    0.2/0.3/0.4/0.6/0.8/1.0 -> realised herring M2 on zoo 2.40 ... 2.98
    /yr (budget 5.24), herring end 0.055 ... 0.20, starvation 0.85 ...
    0.56 /yr, zoo mean 0.71-0.72 throughout. The floor is NOT the main
    limiter. Per-month diagnosis: spring-autumn herring are satiated
    (reserve 0.89, hunger 0.2, overlap 1.0), winter (Dec-Feb) zoo falls
    to 0.6-2 t/cell and herring lose 60-90 % to starvation. Even well
    fed, herring growth at s = 0.89 (~1.2 /yr) does not cover the
    realised losses (M1 0.58 + gadoid predation ~1.0 vs budget 0.31).

140.2 Overwintering rules (tools/probes/herring_overwinter.py; herring
    rule replaces the policy, everything else trained): resting in
    winter or at low food made it WORSE (winter survival 0.13 -> 0.01-
    0.06): eating still nets -3..-7 MJ/t/tick against -8 for resting,
    and starvation mortality starts at half the reserve (u = 0.5), i.e.
    at 7.5 + 1.2 = 8.7 MJ/kg, while real herring reach ~4.5-6 kJ/g in
    spring and live. gadoids -> herring floor 1.0 changed nothing.

140.3 Literature (subagents; mostly DERIVED, see their reports):
    temperature at A17 (SHARK, derived): 0-10 m 4.0 (Feb) - 17.0 (Aug),
    annual 10.4 C; 50-100 m 6.8-9.9 C, annual ~8.2 C, warmer than the
    surface Dec-Mar. Q10 for respiration: herring 1.73 (NEMURO.FISH,
    Rose et al. 2008), cod 1.8-2.1, copepods 1.8-2.1 (Ikeda 2001), C.
    finmarchicus diapause 10-20 % of active respiration. Temperature
    alone lowers herring winter cost only ~7 % (ref 8.2 C).
    Herring energy density: lean ~4.1 kJ/g (protein 15-19 %, Warren et
    al. 2026); North Sea Q3 10.1-11.9 kJ/g, Q1 4.4-6.5 (Pedersen &
    Hislop 2001 via JNCC Report 633); fat 2.1 % (Baltic, March) to
    13.6-26 %; ED ~ 4.1 + 0.396 fat%. North Sea herring feed at a
    reduced rate in winter (Segers et al. 2007: 578/855 stomachs with
    food in February), they do not fast.

140.4 Engine: prey reserve is food (section 140). A DM species with
    prey_includes_reserve: true passes its reserve to the predator:
    gain = intake * assim * (energy_content + reserve per tonne in the
    cell). The static energy_gain_mat (gates, budget_gate, viability)
    is evaluated at reserve_reference_fill (default 0.5). CPU predation
    and GPU predation; tests/test_reserve_food.py and a parity test.
    Inert unless set. inference.build_env, tools/viability.py and
    herring_overwinter.py take a library override (--library).

141 FUNCTIONAL RESPONSE TYPE PER PAIR; GADOID PRESSURE ON HERRING (2026-10-06)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
141.1 Diagnosis chain (all tools/probes/herring_overwinter.py, trained
    policies of pzbpgp248nsrpfix44, 20x20, migration+currents+mortality)
    - Gadoids eat ~64-71 % herring by mass. Not a diet error: Ecopath
      1991 gives pelagic/(pelagic+benthos) = 0.53-0.63 for the gadoid
      group (subagent, derived from Mackinson & Daskalov 2007 + EcoBase
      457). But Ecopath gadoids take ~45 % of their food from prey the
      model lacks (Norway pout ~16 %, zooplankton/krill ~20 %, gadoids
      ~5 %, other fish ~4 %), so the model's gadoids, with Ecopath's
      Q/B (~4.3-4.5 /yr) and Ecopath's gadoid:pelagic biomass ratio
      (0.20-0.21), put about twice the Ecopath pressure on herring.
    - 1 yr, 5 seeds: dark_ratio 0.3 on gadoids->herring and/or the
      herring budget M2 0.30 -> 0.52 changed herring end 0.23 -> 0.26.
    - Ecopath 1991 is a fished state: F ~0.44 gadoids, ~0.40 pelagics
      (derived from Table 3.5); the library takes M = P/B - F, so the
      model is F = 0 by construction. ICES today (subagent): F ~0.12
      gadoids, ~0.20 pelagics (biomass-weighted, inference). 2 yr,
      4 seeds, r_max - F: gadoid mean 1.31 -> 1.22 (-0.19: 1.16),
      herring extinct in year 2 in every run anyway.
    - Herring hiding from gadoids (frozen rule, rest where gadoids are):
      predation 1.46 -> 0.48 but starvation 0.15 -> 1.80 /yr; herring
      die faster. Gadoids share every cell with herring, so hiding means
      not eating.
141.2 Engine: ``functional_response: 2 | 3`` on a predation pair forces
    Holling II or III for that pair; absent = the old rule (III for a
    specialist). _type3_pred_mask is now (N_dm, N_all, 1, 1); the GPU
    mask is [1, D, G, 1]. Bit-identical without the key (rollout hash
    = HEAD). Parity test (an all-pairs-of-a-predator mask fails it) and
    a validation test. Not set in the library.
141.3 Test, 2 yr, 4 seeds: gadoids->herring Type III
        variant          herring end  mean  gadoid mean  pred by gad
        current            0.000      0.38     1.31         1.46
        T3                 0.032      0.39     1.30         1.40
        T3 + r_max - F     0.034      0.39     1.21         1.33
    Type III stops the extinction but pins herring at ~3 % of spawn: at
    a h = 1 the refuge starts below ~1 t/cell, gadoids stay at ~0.9
    t/cell on benthos, and at that ratio their demand on herring (~2.5

142 Live viewer shows the daylight calendar (2026-10-06)
142.1 What: with simulation_settings.daylight on, the pygame viewer
    (train.py / train_gpu.py --visual, inference.py --visual, api.py)
    shows "month = Apr" after the simulated time and "light = 0.42"
    after gen/iter/T in the status bar, and draws a 2 px grey frame just outside every
    heatmap, black (F = 0, night) to white (F = 1, full daylight).
    F is the light observation channel (light_schedule at the civil
    twilight threshold), so the frame shows what the policies see.
    Without the calendar the viewer is unchanged (no month, no frame).
142.2 How: daylight.calendar_at(cfg, tick) -> year tick, day of year,
    month, F; daylight.month_of_day() and MONTH_NAMES. The viewer reads
    cfg from params['daylight'] on the FG objects passed to
    update_biomass (the loader's runtime_config, the same values the
    env's light tables are built from), so no caller had to change. The
    light is the one at the START of the given tick, matching the time
    label (callers pass tick = t + 1 after env step t).
142.3 Replay: the calendar is captured per frame and swapped in with
    the heatmaps; the status bar stays live as before EXCEPT month and
    light, which follow the frame on screen so they agree with the
    frame colour. The month is never dropped when the status line is
    too long; the light number is dropped first.
142.4 Frame width 2 px: the colorbar starts 3 px below the heatmap.
    The old 1 px (60,60,70) border is kept inside it, so the heatmap
    keeps an edge at night. tests/test_viz_daylight.py.
142.5 Frame changed to DAY LENGTH (user request, same day): the grey is
    the day's sun hours on the year's own scale, black on the shortest
    day, white on the longest, linear in hours between, constant within
    a day (steps at midnight). daylight.day_length_hours(lat) is the
    analytic sunrise equation (sun centre above the geometric horizon,
    no refraction or twilight; declination at the day's solar noon),
    checked against solar_elevation_deg to 0.1 h; 58.15 N spans
    6.1-17.9 h. day_length_fraction() is the 0..1 scale (0.5 at the
    equator, where there is no range). The status bar's "light = F"
    became "daylight = 14.2 h". F (per tick) is still in calendar_at
    but no longer drawn. 142.1-142.4 otherwise unchanged.

143 Water temperature: Q10 metabolism on the daylight calendar (2026-10-06)
143.1 Why: the model had no temperature, so every ectotherm paid its
    summer resting_metabolism all year. Probe on fix47 policies
    (pzbpgp248nsrpfix47, 60x60, currents/migration/mortality on, start
    late May): herring intake fell ~90 % in winter (zooplankton at
    herring cells 10.7 -> 1.2 t/cell, daylight attack multiplier 1.4 ->
    0.66) while cost fell only ~30 % (more resting). Reserve fill 0.81
    (Jul) -> 0.15-0.19 (Jan-Feb), 57-79 % of herring biomass below the
    starvation threshold, ~1600 t lost to starvation Dec-Feb, herring
    12500 -> 5150 t over the year. Lean herring (reserve ~1000 MJ/t)
    then starved the porpoises out in Jan-Feb (end 0.08 of 12 t); only
    an omniscient free-moving oracle survived. Literature
    (reports/Vintermetabolism sill och tumlare.md, notes in
    research_notes/Vintermetabolism sill och tumlare/): no source
    reports winter starvation of adult herring; Q1 herring hold ~6.5
    kJ/g (~5-8 % fat); fish metabolism Q10 ~2.2, krill/copepods ~2.0;
    porpoise FMR is flat over 0-20 C.
143.2 Model: a DM with metabolism_q10 pays resting_metabolism * m(t),
    m(t) = q10 ** ((T(t) - t_ref) / 10). Every action cost is a multiple
    of resting_metabolism, so rest/eat/move all follow. T(t) = the
    group's layer temperature at the tick mid-point, interpolated from
    12 monthly means (daylight.monthly_value, circular). t_ref is deg C
    or "annual_mean" (m normalised to average exactly 1 over the year,
    the attack-multiplier convention; slightly different from t_ref =
    mean T because q10**x is convex). Uses the daylight calendar's year
    tick (same start, same random start per world); an enabled block
    without daylight raises. No observation channel: checkpoints stay
    valid. Attack rate is NOT scaled (literature E ~0.4 eV, weaker than
    metabolism; on top of the daylight factor it would deepen the
    winter intake collapse) - a possible step 2.
143.3 Settings: manifest simulation_settings.temperature {enabled,
    layers: {name: 12 monthly C}, group_layers: {fg: layer}} (site
    data); library per species metabolism_q10, metabolism_t_ref
    (biology, tick-independent, not in RESCALE_RULES). A q10 group
    without a layer, or a q10 on a non decision maker, raises in the
    loader. q10 = 1 or absent is exactly inert.
    mareld2.yaml: enabled, SMHI SHARK stations A16+A17 1991-2020;
    mean_0_50m (unweighted mean of 0-2/10/20/30/50 m) for pelagic_fish
    and zooplankton, at_50m for gadoids.
    fg_library.yaml: pelagic_fish 2.2 / t_ref 14 C (8 MJ/t/tick is the
    Rudstam/Rose 2008 resting term at ~14 C, a summer value: m 0.50-0.55
    Jan-Apr, 0.95-0.98 Aug-Sep); gadoids 2.2 / annual_mean (cod SMR,
    Schurmann & Steffensen 1997; m 0.86-1.29); zooplankton 2.0 /
    annual_mean (Ikeda 2001, Saborowski 2000; m 0.74-1.33). Porpoises,
    benthos, phytoplankton: none (endotherm / no metabolism term).
143.4 Code: lib/world/temperature.py (parse_settings, species_settings,
    tick_temperatures, metabolism_multiplier, runtime_config);
    config_loader puts params['temperature'] = {layer, monthly_c} on
    each q10 DM; interactions.build_temperature_tables -> env.
    _has_temperature, env.metabolism_temp_table (T, N_dm), exactly 1
    for DMs without q10; movement.apply_energy_costs multiplies a fresh
    copy of dm_resting_metabolism; GPU TensorEcosystem.metabolism_temp
    indexed by light_index in movement() (step passes it). train.py
    banner prints the temperature line; tools/probes/daylight_table.py
    prints monthly T and m per group.
143.5 Validation:
    * tests/test_temperature.py (35) and a GPU parity case in
      tests/test_gpu_ecosystem.py (fails with an off-by-one table);
      full suite 1004 passed / 12 skipped; train.py and train_gpu.py
      1-generation smoke runs OK.
    * Same probe, temperature on, fix47 policies (trained WITHOUT it):
      no herring starvation in any month; fill 0.31 (Jan) / 0.32 (Feb),
      inside the literature target 0.28-0.45; porpoises survive the
      year at 2.7 of 12 t (were 0.08); herring end 6810 t (was 5150);
      gadoids 4257, zooplankton 47680 t. Herring summer cost is also
      a bit lower (Jul m 0.86).
    * tools/viability.py (frozen behaviour, normative corner) is NOT
      VIABLE with and without the term (exit 1 both). greedy and
      greedy_hide: herring ~0 and porpoises extinct by tick ~100 either
      way. eat arm: herring eq/spawn 0.001 -> 0.066, porpoises extinct
      at 608 instead of 539, gadoids 0.35 -> 0.41. The rig does not
      judge trained policies (VIABILITY.md section 6).
143.6 Open:
    * Fill minimum is still Jan-Feb, not Mar-Apr after spawning (no
      spawning cost in the model; the winter intake collapse is
      zooplankton + light, not cost).
    * Herring still lose ~43 % over the probe year, now dominated by
      predation (~8200 t eaten), not starvation.
