144 Gadoid -> herring light dependence (2026-10-06)
144.1 Literature (reports/Torskfiskars ljusberoende vid jakt.md, notes in
    research_notes/Torskfiskars ljusberoende vid jakt/): no measured
    night/day attack ratio exists for adult gadoids. Field stomach data
    (all senses, real prey behaviour) were weighted over lab vision
    thresholds (vision only; suggested ~0.25-0.3): cod stomachs with
    herring peak morning and evening (Adlerstein & Welleman 2000,
    snippet only), gadoids take sprat at night (Kaartvedt et al. 2009,
    abstract), whiting feed mainly at night (Mergardt & Temming 1997).
    Krill: no day/night difference in whiting (Onsrud et al. 2004,
    Oslofjord) -> zooplankton pair unset. Cannibalism: cod most
    effective at dusk/night/dawn (Strand et al. 2020) -> unset.
    Benthos: eaten MORE at night (Rindorf 2003), which dark_ratio >= 1
    cannot express -> unset.
144.2 Set gadoids_preys_on_pelagic_fish dark_ratio 0.6 (range 0.4-1.0),
    light_threshold_deg -5 (half detection ~0.01-0.03 lx at 30-40 m,
    effective Kd 0.15-0.2 /m; the manifest's PAR Kd 0.29 would blind
    gadoids at Dec noon). Monthly mean m 0.88 (Dec) - 1.13 (Jun),
    per tick 0.73-1.21, annual mean 1. No new observation channel.
144.3 Probe (fix47 policies, temperature on, same world as 143.5), with
    vs without: herring end 6766 vs 6811 t, porpoises 3.24 vs 2.71 t,
    gadoids 4260 vs 4257 t; herring and gadoid monthly budgets
    unchanged to the first decimal (gadoids stay satiated, hunger
    0.13-0.22). As expected: m averages 1, so it only moves predation
    from winter to summer; the ~43 %/yr herring decline is an annual
    budget question (predation_mortality / growth_budget), not light.
    Full suite 1005 passed / 12 skipped.
144.4 Herring -> zoo threshold re-checked (same day): Onsrud et al.
    2004 (ICES JMS 61:1278, Discussion) do not measure it; they cite
    Blaxter 1964 (J Exp Biol 41:155): biting stops at 0.007-0.036 lx.
    Batty, Blaxter & Richard 1990 (Mar Biol 107:383; the library's
    source, infra-red video 0.0001-270 lx) measured 0.001 lx on natural
    zooplankton and 0.01 lx on Artemia nauplii, so the direct
    behavioural value on the modelled prey supports 0.001 lx. Converted
    to sun elevation (surface ~3.4 lx at -6 deg, tenfold per 2 deg,
    Kd 0.15-0.2 /m): 0.001 lx -> -11.8 to -6.1 deg over 10-40 m;
    0.007-0.036 lx -> -10.0 to -3.0 deg; -8 sits mid-range (Blaxter at
    25 m: -8.1 to -5.6). Both sources give where biting STOPS, the
    model's threshold is half detection, so -6 would be as defensible.
    It hardly matters: thresholds -10/-8/-6/-4 give Dec monthly mean m
    0.67/0.66/0.65/0.64 and Jun 1.42/1.42/1.42/1.41 (day length sets
    the season; the threshold only moves the twilight switch). Kept at
    -8; no library change.
144.5 Probes kept in the repo: tools/probes/fg_year_budget.py (monthly
    budget of one DM with trained policies; FG, LIB, RUN, RM_WINTER,
    U_X) produced the numbers in 143.1, 143.5 and 144.3;
    tools/probes/porp_winter_oracle.py (trained / eatonly / oracle K /
    greedy porpoises, CHARGE_MOVE, CMOVE0) produced 143.1's
    positional-vs-budgetary test.

149 Porpoise diet: why they eat no gadoids (2026-10-09)
149.1 Trigger: porpoises eat 98-100 % herring, 0 % gadoids (fix50,
    one year). Ecopath 1991 implies ~49 % gadoids by mass on the
    model's prey: porpoise M2 0.0557 /yr on gadoids vs 0.0117 on
    herring, i.e. 4.8x more gadoid per tonne of prey, at a gadoid:
    herring biomass ratio of ~0.2. Stomach data agree in direction
    (Danish waters: gadoids in 62 % of stomachs, clupeids 35 %;
    western Baltic: cod + herring ~70 % of mass; Oresund: cod the main
    prey Apr-Oct, herring Nov-Mar; Belgian coast: whiting dominant).
149.2 Not the gadoid fix (148): marine mammal intake is mass-limited
    (Rosen & Trites 2000/2004, Steller sea lions on pollock could not
    eat 35-80 % more to match herring - the junk-food hypothesis the
    porpoise gate already uses), and the porpoise ceiling does not
    bind (ration 4-7 %/day vs 14 %/day). Mass ceiling kept.
149.3 Visibility floor 0.75 (porpoises -> gadoids): appeared via the GUI
    without a comment (section ~74). Literature check: no study tests
    seabed masking of porpoise sonar. For: cod rest near the bottom at
    night (Newfoundland telemetry); fish near the seabed are in the
    dead zone of vertical fishery echosounders. Against: porpoise sonar
    characteristics suit foraging near the surface or the bottom
    (ICES JMS 53:465), porpoises aim clicks downward when feeding on
    bottom fish and feed on the bottom in shallow water. Value kept,
    YAML comment states it is inferred, not measured. A higher attack
    rate on gadoids must therefore be justified by the diet data, not
    by easy sonar detection near the bottom.
149.4 Calibration (fix50 policies, current library, one year, every 2nd
    tick; porpoise eats only the prey with the higher energy rate in
    its cell; scratchpad collect_pred.py / calib_porp*.py). Gadoid
    share by mass, weighted by current porpoise biomass / every cell
    equally, and energy at full appetite (cost ~90 MJ/t/tick):
      a_herr  a_gad   share       E
      0.035   0.035    0 /  7 %   174 / 162   (library now)
      0.035   0.300    4 / 32 %   175 / 175
      0.035   1.000   16 / 44 %   176 / 181
      0.020   0.300   19 / 48 %   148 / 156
      0.015   0.150   16 / 46 %   132 / 139
      0.010   0.300   51 / 69 %   120 / 136
    Raising a_gad alone cannot work where porpoises are: herring there
    already give 174 MJ/t/tick, more than gadoids give AT the mass
    ceiling (4620 / 28.6 = 162). Gadoids win only where herring are
    well below saturation, so an Ecopath-like diet also needs a lower
    a on herring, which costs the porpoise budget (E 174 -> ~150).
149.5 Open: user decision on a_herr / a_gad for porpoises (nothing
    changed yet); redo on fix51 fields since porpoises would move.

150 GPU calendar start per world, not per delta pair (2026-10-10)
150.1 Finding: the GPU trainer drew the daylight start tick from the
    pair keys (fold_in(seed, iteration, pair, world)), so every delta
    pair had its own season; only +/- shared it. Section 137.4, the
    light_starts docstring and the CPU trainer (start from spawn_seed)
    all say the start belongs to the world. The pair keys were the
    trainer's existing keys for reserves and in-rollout noise (fe5b305)
    and were reused when the calendar came in (e6a1364).
150.2 Season coverage is not the issue: fix50/fix51 run 1460-tick
    rollouts (one year), starts are uniform (8 gens x 1600 starts,
    chi2 12.4 on 11 df), so every season is in every rollout.
150.3 Measurement (fix51 gen 7 checkpoint, frozen, lr 0, CPU, 6 ARS
    iterations x 16 pairs x 2 worlds x 1460 ticks; each iteration run
    twice with identical deltas, fields, reserves and noise, only the
    starts differing - per pair vs one per world):
      DM            start share of     diff sd  sigma_f  top-8    cos   |step|
                    between-pair var   p/w      p/w      overlap  step  p/w
      gadoids       0.98               0.97     1.61     0.54     0.57  0.36
      pelagic_fish  0.99               1.03     1.94     0.54     0.52  0.35
      porpoises     0.68               1.03     0.85     0.73     0.49  0.78
      zooplankton   0.99               0.90     3.13     0.56     0.67  0.24
    The +/- difference (the gradient signal) is unchanged, but the
    pairs' reward LEVELS were set by their season: the top-b selection
    on max(r+, r-) was near random (overlap 0.5 = chance) and sigma_f
    was inflated, shrinking the step to ~1/3 for three of four DMs.
150.4 Fix: TensorARSTrainer.refresh_worlds draws world_light_start from
    the world keys with the fields; train_step broadcasts it to every
    pair and sign. Saved in the checkpoint; an older checkpoint with a
    locked epoch recomputes it from its keys. Test:

    herring and zooplankton. A resumed run may need lr ~0.01 to keep
    the old step size. Policies stay valid (no observation change).

    gadoids 13x more easily; it is needed because herring saturate the
    porpoise and porpoises have learned to sit on herring. The margin
    falls from 2x to 1.5x of cost, closer to wild porpoises that forage
    almost continuously (Wisniewska et al. 2016).

152 Porpoise indivisible unit 250 kg -> 50 kg (2026-10-10)
152.1 Trigger: the training log shows porpoise move_frac ~0.014, yet
    the viewer shows porpoises moving a lot. Both are true: below
    min_split_biomass a cell takes the argmax action with ALL its
    biomass (lib/gpu/ecosystem.py action_probabilities), and with
    250 kg every porpoise cell (~90 of them, 99 %) is one-hot, so ~1
    whole cell jumps per tick. Over a year 896 moves into empty cells,
    86 t arriving in new cells (12x the mean 4.8 t); 101 new cells
    appear on the edge (--migration on). move_frac is an unweighted
    cell mean of the post-collapse distribution.
152.2 History: 250 kg with extinction_threshold_factor 0.02 (sweep 5 kg)
    came in f594fd3 (2026-09-14) as the "cheap proxy" for coherent
    movement in 71.11: every cell one-hot, so small groups move as a
    unit. Cost: the argmax hides the policy's real distribution, and a
    moving cell gives up a whole tick of food (145.2).
152.3 Frozen fix53 policies (gen 5), one year, same world; one-hot
    threshold changed at runtime only (spawn and sweep unchanged);
    "wanted" = biomass-weighted move probability before the collapse:
      variant                       moved  wanted  end t  gadoid  cells
      250 kg argmax (library)       1.9 %  25 %    2.9    36 %    92
      50 kg argmax                  1.1 %  24 %    4.5    50 %    165
      never one-hot (fractions)     14 %   14 %    0.8    58 %    84
      250 kg, action SAMPLED        12-14  -       0.2/0.4 34-37  24
      50 kg, action SAMPLED         12 %   -       1.0/1.1 50 %   57
    (sampled: two noise seeds; start ~7 t). The policy carries a
    15-25 % move probability that cost nothing under argmax, so it was
    never shaped; executed as fractions or samples it starves the
    porpoises. Sampling (fix "B") can therefore only be judged by
    training, not frozen; not done.
152.4 APPLIED (fix "A"): porpoises min_split_biomass 250 -> 50 kg (one
    animal; Rojano-Donate et al. 2018 imply ~62 kg) and
    extinction_threshold_factor 0.02 -> 0.1 (sweep stays 5 kg). The
    spawn floor follows (5 x min_split = 250 kg per cell, was 1.25 t).
    Note: porpoise interference w is 0, so the 50 kg gain is NOT less
    crowding in a cell; cells above 50 kg split, which spreads the
    porpoises over more cells (165 vs 92) and more prey.

    unchanged (porpoise pairs ok); 1-gen CPU smoke OK. Frozen fix53

154.8 Is lr 0.1 too high? GPU ARS step (lib/gpu/trainer.py ars_update):
    theta += lr/(b sigma_f) sum_top-b (r+ - r-) delta, delta ~ N(0, I),
    perturbation sigma*delta, b = 8 of 16. Normalising by sigma_f makes
    the step length independent of the reward scale: |step| ~ lr * k *
    sqrt(d/b) with k = rms (r+ - r-)/sigma_f ~ 1-2, against a probe
    radius sigma*sqrt(d), so |step|/radius ~ (lr/sigma) k / sqrt(b):
    ~0.2k at lr 0.03, ~0.7k at lr 0.1 (sigma 0.05). Measured on the
    fix53 checkpoints 01:32 -> 10:34 (~280 iterations at lr 0.1, d
    3500-4200 per DM): |theta| 29-35 -> 64-75 for every DM, |dtheta|
    57-66, cos(old, new) 0.44-0.49, per-parameter rms change ~1.0 (sigma
    0.05). 35^2 + n s^2 = 75^2 gives s ~ 3.9 per step, 1.2x the probe
    radius 3.2, and the norm growth is that of a pure random walk
    (orthogonal increments): the update is noise-dominated and each
    generation moves the weights by ~s sqrt(50) ~ 27. The relative
    exploration sigma*sqrt(d)/|theta| fell from 9 % to 4 %, and larger
    weights saturate the tanh units and sharpen the softmax.
154.9 Is the lr-0.1 herring policy (winter rest 13-21 % Nov-Feb) better
    for herring? Old checkpoint + new herring policy (and obs stats),
    same three worlds: herring -0.083 / -0.049 / -0.165 vs old -0.072 /
    -0.029 / -0.131; gadoids -0.066 / -0.059 / -0.094 vs -0.042 / -0.038
    / -0.072; porpoises -0.193 / -0.142 / -0.165 vs -0.050 / -0.055 /
    -0.061 (with the new porpoise policy too: -0.087 / -0.144 / -0.222).
    With 154.7 the new herring policy is worse for herring than the old
    one in all six world x opponent cases (by 0.011-0.034), although a
    pure winter-rest overlay on the old policy gains (154.5). The rest
    came with other changes that cost more; consistent with the random-
    walk reading of 154.8, and with the rest share already falling
    (17 -> 12 %). If a burst is wanted to leave the flat softmax region,
    sigma (probe radius) is the knob, with lr kept at lr/sigma <= ~0.6.
154.10 Do policies become uniform in movement as training goes on?
    Training logs: per-cell action entropy falls monotonically in every
    run (fix40 gad 1.37 -> 0.66 over 40 gens; fix49 0.76 -> 0.42 gens
    3-22; fix53 0.53 -> 0.33 gens 3-13 at lr 0.03, -> 0.13 by gen 21
    after lr 0.1). Probe (tools: scratchpad spread.py; probe world,
    one year; "local dir" = biomass-weighted |sum_k p_k u_k| / p_move
    per cell, 1 = each cell moves one way; "global coh" = the same over
    the whole population per tick; eff cells = exp(entropy of the
    biomass distribution); Rg = radius of gyration, cells):
                    local dir (gad herr porp zoo)  global coh       eff cells gad / herr
      random        0    0    -    0               0    0    -  0   2904 / 3463
      fix53 01:32   .83  .85  .76  .66             .50  .64  .56 .50  2538 / 2719
      fix53 10:34   .94  .88  .95  .96             .22  .26  .58 .38  2263 / 2207
      fix53 11:47   .95  .90  .96  .94             .36  .39  .53 .59  2118 / 2099
    fix49/50/51 checkpoints: local .21-.81, global .16-.72. Rg 20-25
    for every DM and checkpoint except porpoises (whole grid covered).
    So: cells become one-directional and gadoids/herring patchier
    (eff cells -17/-23 %), but the population as a whole does not move

    Reading: the sharpening is at least partly the noise-driven weight

156 fix53 ten-year rollout read against nature; movement sweep leak
    closed (2026-10-11)
156.1 Setup. Frozen fix53 checkpoint of 20:57 (training still running,
    lr 0.06 sigma 0.1), the deterministic probe world (60x60, mortality,
    migration, currents 0.1/20/0/12, mass balance, daylight +
    temperature, calendar start May 28), 14600 ticks = 10 years. Every
    impact in mareld2.yaml is muted: this is the null scenario. Per tick:
    biomass, reserve, biomass-weighted action mix, reserve fill s and
    starving share, diet and loss-by-cause deltas, occupied cells,
    Lloyd patchiness, pred-prey cosine overlap. Monthly patterns are
    detrended (log biomass over a centred one-year running mean); raw

    year boundary (porpoises looked like they had a June "calving
    pulse"). A second run with another global seed (same spawn, only
    the FG order differs) stayed within 2 % (porpoises 18 %, few t): a
    small perturbation does not grow, no sign of chaos: the cycle is
    forced by the calendar (daylight, temperature), damped by
    interference, type III and reserves, and noise-free (fractions,
    frozen policies).
156.2 Trends, annual means year 1 -> 10 (t): herring 12710 -> 20650
    (+1 %/yr at y10, slowing), benthos 18950 -> 31030, gadoids 2300 ->
    1520 (-1.3 %/yr, slowing), porpoises 11 -> 3.6 (-12 %/yr,
    exponential), zooplankton 24400 -> 22800, phytoplankton flat 43400.
    Not at equilibrium after 10 years; everything past year 1 is also
    outside the 1460-tick training episodes.
156.3 Behaviour that matches nature (detrended, years 2-10):
    * Phytoplankton spring bloom in March (0.75 Jan -> 1.12 Mar).
    * Zooplankton minimum Jan, maximum May-Jun, ~9x, 2-3 months after
      the bloom (Calanus-like).
    * Zooplankton diapause-like: rest 0.78-0.85 in winter, most eating
      in Feb-Mar (0.33-0.40) when the bloom starts.
    * Zooplankton diel vertical migration where real night exists: rest
      day/night 0.93/0.60 (DJF), 0.73/0.44 (MAM). Gone at midsummer
      (no dark tick at 58 N with 6 h ticks).
    * Herring feed by day and rest at night (DJF rest 0.11 day / 0.75
      night): a visual planktivore. The winter rest (0.42-0.47 Nov-Jan)
      is mostly long nights.
    * Herring lipid cycle: s 0.23 in Feb -> 0.87 in Jun; biomass minimum
      Mar-Apr, maximum Oct-Nov.
    * Herring aggregate in winter (Lloyd 1.8 vs 1.4 in summer).
    * Gadoid-herring overlap highest in the feeding season (0.72 summer
      vs 0.59 winter); gadoid diet switches with season (summer herring
      + zooplankton, winter benthos 88 %).
    * Porpoises feed around the clock (eat 0.97-1.00, no rest), Q/B 22
      /yr (~6 % of body mass per day, low end of the literature).
    * Herring become food-limited as they grow: starving share of the
      losses 2 % -> 7 % over the run.
156.4 Behaviour that does not:
    * Realised M2 vs the budgeted predation_mortality (1/yr, years
      1..10):
        pair                    library   realised
        gadoids -> gadoids      0.217     ~0.001  (growth paid for a
                                                   loss never taken)
        gadoids -> benthos      0.0048    0.33 -> 0.17 (see 156.10;
                                                   the rate ratio is
                                                   not a diet error)
        gadoids -> herring      0.30      0.19 -> 0.14 (herring under-
                                                   cropped, they grow
                                                   until food brakes)
        zoo -> phyto            22.6      30.5
        herring -> zoo          5.24      3.2 -> 5.2
        porpoises -> gadoids    0.056     0.087 -> 0.020
        porpoises -> herring    0.0117    0.006 -> 0.003
    * The derived g = budget / ((1 - u) * 1460) pays the full budget at
      s = 1 only (growth_budget.py, "ideal conditions"), where the
      hunger gate closes intake. s sits at 0.6-0.75, so gadoids and
      porpoises realise 40-50 % of the designed production; for
      porpoises that does not even cover M1. By design, but it is a
      structural reason the top predators decline.
    * Phytoplankton has no post-bloom decline: a plateau 1.05-1.10 from
      Apr to Oct, annual range 1.6x. Nature: nutrient-depleted summer
      low, autumn bloom, 5-10x in chlorophyll. No nutrient pool.
    * Top predators do not track prey: porpoises Lloyd 25, overlap with
      prey 0.15-0.22, move 0-3 %, cells 250 -> 128; gadoids move 1 %,
      never rest, no spawning migration (154.6: staying is rational

156.6 Fix (lib/environments/ecosystem_env/movement.py, mirrored in
    lib/gpu/ecosystem.py), two rules next to section 69's split
    suppression, same principle (thr = extinction_threshold_factor *
    min_split_biomass, 0 opts out):
    * cancel_subthreshold_emigration / TensorEcosystem.cancel_emigration:
      with --migration, a DM whose off-grid pool this tick is 0 < pool
      < thr keeps every off-grid outflow (and its reserve) in the source
      cell. _concentrate_immigration / immigration are unchanged; their
      "no viable prefix -> spread over the whole edge" branch is now
      only reached by thr = 0 groups (and advect's passive groups).
    * follow_subthreshold_residues / TensorEcosystem.follow_residues:
      after the split suppression, a cell with 0 < B < thr that still
      sends biomass to an in-grid neighbour hands all its biomass and
      reserve to those neighbours in proportion to the remaining
      outflows. One pass is safe: cells only lose inflow when they
      were below thr with every inflow applied, so every destination of
      a non-cancelled outflow stays viable, and a residue cell holds
      only its own biomass (all inflows into it were cancelled). A
      residue whose only outflow leaves the grid stays and is swept.
    The local-reward flow books cancelled emigration as stay and a
    followed residue as outflow (stay 0 at the residue cell), so it
    still sums to the settled grid on CPU and GPU. Graph-safe
    (torch.where only). No observation change: checkpoints stay valid,
    but policies were trained against the leak, and the running
    train_gpu (code loaded at start) keeps the old movement until it
    is restarted.

156.10 Correction to 156.4 (gadoids -> benthos). The rate comparison
    (budget M2 0.0048 vs realised 0.17-0.33 /yr, first written as
    "40-70x, library implies ~1 % of the diet") is misleading: the
    Ecopath M2 is a rate on Ecopath's benthos biomass, while the model's
    benthos has K = 10 t/km2 (literature proposal ~100, section 136).
    The same absolute flux on a tenth of the biomass is a ten times
    higher rate, so the ratio says little about the diet. The right
    reference is Ecopath 1991's diet composition (141.1, 148.1):
                         benthos  herring  zoo     gadoids
      Ecopath, renorm.   ~28 %    ~40 %    ~25 %   ~6 %
      model, years 2-10  65 %     26-28 %  7-10 %  0 %
    Benthos / (pelagic fish + benthos) is 0.37-0.47 in Ecopath and
    ~0.70 in the model; per tonne of gadoid the model eats roughly 3-4x
    Ecopath's benthos (Q/B 5.7 vs 4.3-4.5, and the higher share; rough).
    For: "gadoids" is an umbrella (haddock mainly benthivorous, cod eats
    crabs, Nephrops, shrimp, polychaetes; whiting and saithe are fish /
    krill eaters); ~45 % of the Ecopath gadoid diet is prey the model
    lacks (Norway pout, krill beyond zooplankton, other fish), which
    the model's gadoids must replace, and benthos is everywhere, never
    hides and never moves; the winter switch (88 % Dec-Feb, 22 %
    Jun-Aug) follows herring's night rest and the dark_ratio 0.6 on
    gadoids -> herring. Against: the share is ~1.5-2.5x Ecopath, and
    with the energy-limited ceilings of 148 every pair fills the
    stomach at the densities present, so benthos wins on availability
    rather than value (148.2). Verdict: direction and seasonal switch
    plausible, share elevated, not one of the gross deviations.

159 Splits hand off whole units only (2026-10-14)
159.1 Reading of min_split_biomass (user): one unit = one individual
    (porpoises 50 kg), and the sweep at extinction_threshold_factor x
    unit (5 kg) is where that individual dies. Correction to 156.7 (last
    sentence) and 156.9(1): sub-animal pieces do not "die through the
    sweep". The sweep only zeroes cells below 5 kg, and the section-69
    split suppression and the 156 residue rule never create such a cell
    by moving; a 5-50 kg piece reaches the sweep only by shrinking (M1,
    catabolism, predation), which books everything above the last <5 kg
    on those channels. The real gap was elsewhere: below one unit the
    action distribution collapses to argmax (the cell moves whole), but
    from one unit the softmax split was continuous, so a 70 kg cell
    sending 30 % E and 20 % N made 21 kg and 14 kg "individuals".
159.2 Measurement, tools/probes/porp_fragments.py (rollout recorder with
    a per-cell split-origin lineage, mass-weighted; --rule-a / --rule-d
    probe variants; --fractional-splits reproduces the pre-159 baseline
    below). Frozen fix53 checkpoint of 2026-10-12 15:37 (md5
    porpoises d45593b2, herring 5cf33a1e, gadoids fc3175ca, zoo
    4d9a4f24; trained after the 14:12 restart, i.e. on the 156 rules and

        5-50 kg pieces landing alone     35 000, 6.0 t
        pieces joining a >= 50 kg cell   13 000, 2.8 t
        >= 50 kg sources left < 50 kg     7.4 t
        cells shrinking through 50 kg    3, 0.17 t
        sweep                            10 cells, 0.05 t (0.007 t of it
                                          split-origin)
    88 % of occupied cells and 73 % of the porpoise mass held less than
    one animal (156.5: 75-87 %), 95 % of that mass put there by splits.
    No mass leak: every loss rate is per kg and porpoise interference is
    0, so a 14 kg piece loses the same share per tick as the 70 kg cell
    it came from. The cost was semantic. (The 0.31 t/yr sweep of 156.7
    was the 22:27 checkpoint, which no longer exists.)
159.3 Rule A (probe only, rejected): cancel an in-grid outflow below one
    unit unless the destination's pre-move stay holds one. Frozen
    porpoises fell to 1.5 t (occupied cells 279 -> 67, 28 t/yr of
    outflow cancelled): the frozen policies spread moves over four
    directions, so A pins every 50-100 kg cell, and each cancelled move
    still paid movement_cost. A deterministic cancel fights a policy that
    outputs a distribution.
159.4 Rule D (user's proposal, implemented): a cell holding >= one unit
    splits over five spatial fractions, stay (rest + every eat action)
    and N/E/S/W. A fraction with B * p < unit is handed to the fractions
    holding >= one unit, proportionally; the eat/rest mix inside stay is
    kept. With no fraction at one unit the whole cell goes to the largest
    (first index on ties) - the sub-unit argmax collapse applied to the
    spatial split. Applied in the decision step, after the collapse and
    before the action diagnostics, so predation (hidden share) and the
    movement costs see the realised split and no cost is paid for a move
    that did not happen. Every DM with min_split_biomass > 0 (porpoises
    50 kg, herring and gadoids 0.5 kg; muted seals 80, seabirds 1).
    Code: decisions.merge_subunit_fractions (NumPy),
    TensorEcosystem.merge_subunit_fractions (graph-safe torch.where),
    EcosystemEnvironment(unit_splits=True); unit_splits=False is the
    pre-159 continuous split (env kwarg only, no CLI flag). The env's
    policy path is the only CPU entry point: env.step(actions) with a
    supplied distribution (tests, viability rig hand-coded arms) bypasses
    both the argmax collapse and D, as before. No observation change:
    checkpoints load, but behaviour changes and inference of a pre-159
    checkpoint now runs with D.

    gadoids. Structural: the reward is the group's own biomass and

    policy learns it, and the budget paid ~0.1 /yr of free production
    (the M0 report said the same). It is not in M1 (157: M0 0.20 + non-
    FG predation 0.214). APPLIED (user's call): pair unchecked; in an
    age-pooled group it is mostly a transfer from small to large fish,
    and r_max is already net at low density where it is small. The
    density regulation real cannibalism gives is gone either way; a
    density-dependent non-behavioural loss is the candidate if the
    overshoot stays after retraining. tests/test_fgconfig_field_help.py

160.7 s* (tools/probes/ideal_growth.py, lib/world/growth_budget.py).
    Ideal conditions: unlimited prey of the best checked, active pair,
    eaten every tick at the Holling ceiling, C = assimilation * prey
    energy (incl. the reference reserve, 140) / h_t, paying
    resting_metabolism * feeding_cost at the library (reference)
    temperature. Growth is debited from the reserve and dilutes it, so
    the reserve settles where h(s) C = cost + P (ec + s ME). With P the
    gross budget per tick, s* = (C/(1-u) - cost - P ec)/(C/(1-u) + P ME)
    and g = gross / ((s* - u) * 1460): closed form, no policy, no
    rollout (an earlier idea - calibrate s_ref on a trained policy's s -
    was dropped as circular). Errors: P >= Pmax = (C - cost)/(ec + u ME)
    (budget above the energy) and g > ME / ec (the mass balance would
    cap it). No energy data -> the old full reserve 1 - u (the toy
    budgets in tests/test_growth_budget.py). New GrowthBudget fields:
    maintenance, reference_fill (s*), ideal_intake, ideal_cost,
    best_prey, pmax_annual; ideal_intake() and ideal_reserve() are
    public. FG editor: the gate term's caption shows s*, u, best prey,
    C, cost and Pmax; field_help growth:gate rewritten. The annual-mean
    Q10 factor is left out on purpose so the budget stays a library
    property (herring t_ref 14 C: s* 0.857 here vs 0.880 with the annual

161 BASELINE IMPACTS AND IMPACT PRESSURE ON THE GPU ENGINE
================================================================

161.1 Why. fix55 (the section 160 library) let gadoids grow 35-40 %/yr
    with no density brake after cannibalism was unchecked. A literature
    review (reports/Taethetsberoende och interferens hos torskfiskar.md,
    notes under research_notes/; Swedish file names) found that
    interference cannot be that brake: w = 1 already gives 2-3 % less
    intake per doubling of biomass, inside the empirical 3-6 %, and a
    frozen-fix55 sweep needs w ~ 11 for zero net growth in year 1, with
    winter starvation and growth back by year 2. The missing piece is a
    loss. The user set the frame: the inference start biomasses are the
    area as it is today, under a restrictive fishery. 2500 t gadoids is
    therefore a fished state, and fishing belongs in the world as a loss
    outside the growth budget (r_max is unfished low-density growth).
    The impact maps (pelagic_trawling) were the intended vehicle.

161.2 Two findings blocked that.
    * The GPU engine (lib/gpu) had no impacts at all: no impact
      mortality, no energy_factor surcharge (open since 86.7).
    * Training zeroes every impact the policy cannot observe
      (train._sample_impact_maps, "treated as absent during training");
      only the probe and inference load inference.impact_maps. A
      non-observable fishery would have been absent from training on
      both engines.
    The user chose a new flag over making trawling observable (which
    would add input channels, invalidate checkpoints and let fish learn
    to dodge the trawl, lowering the effective F).

161.3 The baseline flag. impact_variables[i].baseline: true marks an
    impact as part of today's world (fishing), not a scenario pressure.
    * Training samples a field for observable impacts AND baseline
      impacts; everything else stays absent (lib/world/impact_maps.py:
      sample_impact_maps, trained_impact_vars; moved from train.py,
      train._sample_impact_maps kept as an alias). _EnvBuilder reads the
      baseline list from the project.
    * Inference worlds (inference.build_env, train._ProbeEnvBuilder, the
      progress evaluation lib/runners/training_progress.build_inference_env,
      which had no impact maps at all before) go through
      inference.load_inference_impact_maps: the project's npz map if
      there is one, else a baseline impact is sampled from its range and
      spawn strategy with the world seed, else zero. The noll and
      projekt scenarios are thus both fished.
    * config_loader: project_impact_ranges (factored out of
      load_project_config) and project_baseline_impact_vars.
    * FG editor: "Baseline (always present)" checkbox in the Impact
      Editor; the Spawn Strategy frame shows for observable or baseline
      impacts; field_help impact_baseline.
    Impacts stay outside growth_budget, which never read them.

161.4 GPU port (lib/gpu/ecosystem.py, rollout.py, trainer.py, config.py).
    TensorEcosystem keeps the reference's dm_impact_tables. impact_fields
    turns one world's fields into a per-cell loss rate (sum of
    biomass_factor) and cost surcharge (sum of energy_factor), [N, D, C],
    on the host once per world; the tick only multiplies:
    impact_mortality before predation (B -= B*loss, reserve shrinks with
    it, as impacts.apply_impact_mortality) and metabolism *
    (1 + cost) in movement (impacts.impact_energy_cost_factor). A
    missing field is skipped and an absent impact is a zero field read
    through the table, as on CPU. Without any table (mareld2 today:
    every impact muted) nothing is allocated and the graph is unchanged.
    RolloutRunner holds impact_loss / impact_cost buffers and reset takes
    impacts; TensorARSTrainer samples the baseline fields per world in
    refresh_worlds from the world keys (one small readback per refresh)
    and rebuilds them on load_state_dict. ProjectSpec carries the impact
    recipe and raises NotImplementedError for an active observable
    impact (the engine builds no impact observation channels; it used to
    ignore them silently).

161.5 Validation. tests/test_gpu_impacts.py (19 with CUDA): full-tick
    CPU/GPU parity with two impacts, a table non-zero at value 0, a field
    beyond the table, a missing field, migration and mortality; the
    summed fields against interp_impact; impacts change the trajectory;
    no tables keep the old graph; baseline sampled in training while a
    non-observable scenario impact stays zero; muted baseline skipped;
    inference fallback deterministic per seed; trainer fields per world,
    reproducible per epoch, expanded into the runner and restored on
    resume; observable impacts refused. tests/test_gpu_ecosystem.py
    make_env takes impacts. Full suite 1093 passed / 12 skipped.
    Smoke: train.py 1-gen on mareld2 OK; on a copy with pelagic_trawling
    un-muted as baseline (value_max 1000, the placeholder table removes
    up to 100 %/tick) herring is gone on both engines (train_gpu reward
    -9.4, train.py probe "imp 100%"), with value_max 0.001 it trains
    normally.

161.6 Open. The fishery itself: bottom_trawling FG entries for gadoids
    (they are caught in demersal and Nephrops trawls, not pelagic), real
    per-tick tables (F/1460, ~1.6e-4/tick for F 0.24), the pelagic
    trawling placeholder table, an effort map or a uniform field, and
    calibration so the effective F (biomass-weighted over where the
    policies put the fish) matches today's restrictive fishery. Next to
    it the density-dependent M1 for gadoids (SMS: 0.016 + 0.0875 B per
    year, B in t/km2; only the intercept paid by the budget). Frozen
    fix55: F + k B_ref must close a surplus of ~0.36/yr at 2500 t, e.g.
    k B ~ 0.12 and F ~ 0.24. Observable impacts on the GPU engine are
    still unsupported.
161.7 Observable impacts on the GPU engine (follow-up, same session).
    The NotImplementedError of 161.4 is gone; the engine now follows
    train.py's implementation (observations.build_observation_batch):
    each observable impact is one raw-valued channel after the observed
    groups in the own cell and again in each neighbour block (N, E, S,
    W; zero outside the grid), the light channel still last; a missing
    field reads as zeros. TensorEcosystem builds those indices from
    env.observable_impact_vars (bank: biomass, visible, energy, light,
    impacts) and takes impact_obs [E, n_obs, C] in observations;
    impact_observations / import_impact_observations build it per world.
    RolloutRunner keeps an impact_obs buffer (reset(impact_obs=...));
    TensorARSTrainer samples observable and baseline fields together per
    world with train.py's rule (spawn strategy, colony jitter, value
    range) and restores them on resume. ProjectSpec, EnvironmentBuilder
    and the progress evaluation world build their envs with the
    observable list, so in_dims match the CPU trainer and exported
    policies load in CPU inference; EnvironmentBuilder also samples the
    training-world fields. Side fix: EnvironmentBuilder.with_world passed
    tick_hours into the mass_balance slot (positional); it now uses
    dataclasses.replace.
    Tests (tests/test_gpu_impacts.py, 32 with CUDA): observation and
    tick parity with one, two and a field-less observable impact, with
    and without the daylight channel; trainer fields per world into the
    runner and on resume; exported policy widths equal the CPU world's.
    Full suite 1106 passed / 12 skipped. Smoke: train_gpu with
    windfarm_noise observable (cuda-graph, 2 iterations) and the exported
    policies stepping a CPU inference world.
161.8 Baseline maps replace the baseline flag (follow-up, user design).
    The user's frame: a fishing map holds the effort in each cell; a
    scenario (closed wind farm, changed quotas) is another map for the
    same impact, never a second impact on top (impacts add up). An
    impact without a map has no effect, in training too. So the
    baseline: true flag and the sampled baseline fields of 161.3 (from
    the value range, in training and as an inference fallback) are gone.
    * Impact Editor: "Baseline map" row (Browse / Clear) stores
      impact_variables[i].baseline_map, a .npz path relative to the
      project file (same validation as the Inference tab, shared in
      _read_impact_npz); the list shows [baseline map]; the Spawn
      Strategy frame shows only for observable impacts without one.
    * Training (train._EnvBuilder, GPU ProjectSpec/trainer,
      EnvironmentBuilder): an impact with a baseline map gets that map in
      every world, observable or not; otherwise observable impacts are
      spawned per world (behaviour against them, as before) and the rest
      is absent. lib/world/impact_maps.py: project_baseline_maps,
      sample_impact_maps(baseline_maps=...), load_impact_map_npz (moved
      from inference.py, alias kept).
    * Inference worlds (inference.build_env, the probe, the progress
      evaluation) read only inference.impact_maps; the baseline map is
      not read there - the user adds the same file under the Inference
      tab to keep today's fishing, or a scenario file instead.
    Why a hidden baseline impact belongs in training: the policies cannot
    react to fishing itself, but they train in the states it creates
    (lower densities, more food per fish), and the world settles near the
    reference instead of drifting to an unfished state (fix55). Scenario
    impacts that are not observable stay out of training, so noll and
    projekt are compared with the same policies.
    Tests: tests/test_gpu_impacts.py (33 with CUDA; the baseline ones
    rewritten: the map is the training field and replaces an observable
    impact's spawned field, project_baseline_maps resolves, resamples and
    skips muted / missing files, inference ignores the baseline map until
    the Inference tab has it, every GPU world gets the same map, no map
    means zero in training), tests/test_fgconfig_baseline_map.py (Browse
    stores a relative path and marks the list, Clear removes it, an
    invalid file is not stored). Full suite 1109 passed / 12 skipped.
    Smoke with a 1000-everywhere baseline map on pelagic trawling (the
    placeholder table, 100 %/tick): herring gone in training on both
    engines (reward -13.8), untouched in the train.py probe (103 %),
    which is an inference world without the map.
    Next: the fishery maps themselves (EMODnet effort per km2 per cell,
    multi-window mean, bottom otter trawls for gadoids), linear tables
    with catchability q = F / mean effort reaching well above today's
    effort (interp_impact clamps at the last row), F 0.12 gadoids and
    0.10 pelagic fish (reports/Fiskeridodlighet i Skagerrak idag.md).
161.9 The fishery: effort maps and calibrated tables.
    tools/make_fishing_maps.py fetches the EMODnet Human Activities WFS
    layers fishingbottomottertrawls and fishingpelagic (mw_fshn per 0.05
    deg c-square, VMS vessels > 12 m, five overlapping 4-year windows
    2015-2018 ... 2021-2024), divides by the c-square area to get effort
    density and rasterises it onto the 60x60 SWEREF 99 TM grid by
    sampling each c-square (80 x 80 points, no shapely/pyproj; the
    Gauss-Krueger projection hits coordinates.txt within 2 m). Today's

    Skagerrak total falls ~60 % after 2018-2021), scaled to the 2021-2024
    grid mean. Output maps/fishing_bottom_otter_trawls.npz (key

    scenario maps with more effort are not clamped.
    Check, frozen fix55 policies (copy of 2026-10-15), probe world, a

162 HERRING WINTER FEEDING: INTERFERENCE, REFUGE AND RESPONSE TYPE (2026-10-15)
================================================================

162.1 Why herring underproduce (frozen fix57 copy 2026-10-15 15:37,
    probe world with today's fishing maps; tools/probes/herring_losses.py,
    herring_monthly.py, fg_year_budget.py). Year 1 from 12000 t: gross
    production 0.94 /yr against the budget 1.54 (r_max 0.648 + M1 0.58 +
    M2 0.31); losses M1 0.58, gadoids 0.39 (budget 0.30), fishing 0.07,
    porpoises + starvation 0.03; net -0.13. Apr-Aug production 1.36-1.55
    /yr (88-100 % of budget, s 0.78-0.86 ~ s* 0.857); Oct-Feb 0-0.95 with
    intake below cost Nov-Jan (6-18 vs 23-35 MJ/t/day), s 0.71 (Sep) ->
    0.26 (Jan): ~90 % of the shortfall is the winter half. From year 2
    the gadoid take rises 0.39 -> 0.68 -> 1.00 (gadoids 2800 -> 4500 t,
    per-gadoid take about constant).
162.2 Literature (research_notes/Sillens vinterfoda/, Swedish dir name):
    winter_food_and_feeding.md - SHARK A17 Dec-Feb mesozooplankton
    0.7-1.7 g WW/m2 (0-25 m), ~1.5-4.4 whole column vs model 1.5-3.2:
    realistic (the Apr-May peak 19-36 vs model 10.5-12.5 is 2-3x low);
    herring winter ration 0.4-1.0 % BW/day (Lohmeyer 1977, Bernreuther
    2007) vs model 0.18-0.30 Dec-Jan; winter cost not above the Rudstam
    model; krill possibly missing (NS Ecopath 0.8-2.4 g WW/m2, no
    Skagerrak value). herring_functional_response.md - every herring fit
    is Type II or linear, no sigmoid response reported for any clupeid;
    Type III came only from the "one prey -> Type III" rule (state.py).
    herring_interference.md - no behavioural interference measured in
    herring; intake falls 0-5 % per doubling (depletion included), the
    model's w 0.7 gave 40 % (winter) / 11 % (summer); w 0.7 was set in 86
    against the band artefact and only {0, w/3, w} were tried.
    zooplankton_refuge.md - shelf copepods mostly do not migrate, a
    non-feeding copepod is still visible, daytime accessible share
    0.65-0.9 (summer) / 0.5-0.8 (winter) vs ~0.3 in the model; floor 0.2
    fits a deep basin, 0.4-0.6 a 100 m bank.
162.3 Mechanism (checked in code and a day/night probe): Dec intake
    computed from holling_a_eff + visible_prey_biomass = 0.15 % BW/day vs
    0.18 measured. Zooplankton rest 81-88 % all year (94-96 % of daylight
    ticks, 60-81 % of dark ticks in Oct-Feb; likely energetic - feeding
    costs 4x resting, section 135), so visible ~0.45 t/km2 in Dec; Type
    III squares it; I = 0.7 x 3.4 = 2.4 dominates the denominator; light

163 PROGRESS EVALUATION FOLLOWS THE ROLLOUT LENGTH (2026-10-15)

163.1 --eval-ticks (lib/runners/training_progress.py, train.py and
    train_gpu.py) defaulted to 1000, so with 1460-tick training rollouts

    ... evaluating up to 1000 inference ticks"). Without --eval-ticks it
    now follows the training rollout length (train.py --n_eval_ticks,
    train_gpu.py dest "ticks"); an explicit --eval-ticks still wins
    (args.eval_ticks_default records which). A resumed run whose
    progress/config.json was written with another cap keeps that cap when
    --eval-ticks is not given (prints a note) so its graph stays
    comparable; an explicit different value is still refused ("settings
    changed", use a new --plot-dir). Recommendation recorded with it:
    train on whole years (1460 ticks; random start day, every season in
    every rollout, 150.2), read multi-year effects with separate
    inference runs, not a longer training horizon.

    ticks, an explicit value wins, the GPU parser resolves it, resume
    keeps the stored cap unless one is given. Full suite 1142 passed / 12

165 PORPOISE BYCATCH ON THE BOTTOM-TRAWL MAP (2026-10-16)

165.1 Literature: trawls catch almost no porpoises (ASCOBANS NSG14,
    2017-23: ~24/yr in bottom otter trawls over ~111,000 days at sea vs
    ~389/yr in trammel nets over ~10,500; UK experts class bottom trawls
    low risk; the pelagic-trawl problem is common dolphins in Biscay pair
    trawls). Porpoise bycatch is gillnet bycatch, ~1.7 % of the
    population per year in the North Sea region (Kindt-Larsen et al.
    2023 / OSPAR 2020, snippet only; no Skagerrak figure).
165.2 Static-gear effort (VMS > 12 m) in the grid is ~0 and gillnets are
    0.6 % of the 45G0 catch (local_fishery.md), so a gillnet map would be
    empty. As for the herring F, the closed pool carries the population's
    loss met outside the grid. User's call: carry it on the bottom-trawl
    map, the way the gadoids' seine and gillnet share already is.
165.3 fg_library.yaml: porpoises_impacted_by_bottom_trawling, linear,
    q = 0.017 / 1460 / 3.0142 = 3.863e-6 per tick per unit (row 100 ->
    3.863e-4). Today's map: 0.017/yr at mean effort, 0.054/yr in the
    busiest cell. Outside the growth budget; the library M1 is survival
    excluding bycatch, so nothing is double counted. bottom_trawling is
    not observable: no observation channel, checkpoints stay valid.
    Side effect to keep in mind: a scenario that closes trawling also
    removes the porpoise bycatch there, which gillnets would not do.

167 SEALS: LIGHT AND PREY REFUGE (2026-10-16)
================================================================

167.1 Targeted review (three searches; report "reports/Salars jakt i
    ljus och morker.md" with Swedish letters in the file name, notes in
    the matching research_notes/ folder). No study, for any phocid,
    measures capture success in light vs darkness, so every value below
    is inferred.
167.2 dark_ratio / light_threshold_deg: NOT set on either seal pair
    (= 1, no light effect). Harbour seals hunt with their vibrissae
    (blindfolded seals follow fish wakes up to ~35 s old, Dehnhardt
    2001, Wieskotten 2010; find flatfish breathing currents of ~4 cm/s,
    Niesterok 2017); blind wild seals did well; field dive data show as
    much or more foraging at night (Blanchet 2015 Svalbard, Jessopp
    2013 grey seals 44 % pelagic dives at night vs 28 % by day),
    benthic feeders little diel difference (Bjoerge 1995, Tollit 1998,
    via Wilson 2014). Day-biased time at sea (Kattegat, Galatius 2026,
    snippet) is when seals are out, not how well they hunt, and is
    left to Rest + the light input; a dark_ratio would count it twice.
    Not "dark anyway": at 40-50 m day and night differ by 7-8 decades
    of light. Herring alternative 0.8 / -6 deg rejected: month means
    0.95-1.06 on a ~16 t/yr pair.
167.3 APPLIED, fg_library.yaml: seals_preys_on_gadoids visibility_floor
    0.85 (range 0.75-0.95; was the gadoid default 0.6). Resting or
    buried bottom fish are a seal's normal prey (sandeel 40 % of
    otoliths in Skagerrak 2020, Kappa 2026; flatfish 46 % of energy,
    GU 2019; Baltic EwE gives grey seal fish prey no refuge, Costalago
    2018); at or above porpoises -> gadoids 0.75. seals_preys_on_
    pelagic_fish keeps the herring default 0.35 (range 0.3-0.5): seals
    have no sonar, so schooling protects; and the herring floor is what
    holds the 95:5 diet (in-memory probe at grid mean density: unhidden
    herring yields 161 vs gadoids 141 MJ/t/tick; fully hidden 79). The
    gadoid floor raises the seal's yield from hidden gadoids by +3 % at
    half hiding and +11 % at full (saturation). Growth budget and
    budget_gate unchanged (the floor is not in s*). No observation
    change; checkpoints from section 166 onward stay valid.
167.4 Note: fg_library.yaml was re-saved by the FG editor between 166
    and 167 (growth_rate rounded to 6 significant digits, interference
    0.0 written for seals); the stored rates still pass the 1e-5 test.
167.5 Checks: full suite 1148 passed / 12 skipped; train.py 1-gen smoke
    OK. Open: reanalyse the public Vance et al. 2021 Wadden Sea capture
    timings by day/night for a measured dark_ratio; floor sensitivity
    at the range ends.

      is NOT an overconsumption: 1.3 t/km2/yr eaten vs 0.15-2 from

      model's benthos stock is 10-35x smaller (K 10, section 136), and

168.2 Cause: seals_preys_on_pelagic_fish has functional_response 3 but
    kept max_intake_rate 0.015 from the porpoise Type II pair (section
    151). Under Type III, a is per (t/cell)^2 and the effective rate
    is a*B: ~0.1 at 7 t/cell, half the gadoid pair's 0.2, and the

    ceiling. Herring was also fat (seal-weighted 8000 MJ/t vs static
    6600), so it beat gadoids in ~80 % of the seals' cells. The h
    equalisation in 166 (189 vs 180 MJ/t/tick) only holds at saturation
    with reference-fill herring; the floor argument in 167.3 only at the
    grid-mean density.

168.5 Open: (a) measure the retrained diet against 95:5 with
    tools/probes/pair_intake.py; (b) seals still have no density
    dependence: near K (Carroll et al. 2025: x = 0.90 today, mu 0.28
    /yr) they should grow ~0-0.03 /yr, not r_max. Once their diet runs
    through the 2500 t gadoid stock, measure whether food limitation

    on growth (pups, fecundity), not on adult M1.
168.6 Is 1e-4 biologically defensible? As a calibration, yes; as a
    measurement, no. For: the TARGET is literature (herring 3-10 % of
    the Skagerrak harbour seal diet: 2.8 % of energy in 2019 scats, Qi
    10 % in Soerlie 2020); the mechanism is real (seals forage on the
    bottom with their vibrissae, herring school in the water column, and
    the model's single layer per cell co-locates them far more than in
    reality; a low a is the only place to put that separation); Type III
    keeps prey switching, so herring patches above ~17 t/cell can still
    draw seals; and the old 0.015 was no literature value either (a
    Type II porpoise rate in the wrong units). Against: the per-tonne
    selectivity it implies (a*B / 0.2 = 1/670 at 3 t/cell, 1/290 at 7,
    1/120 at 17) is stronger than the empirical (5 %/12000 t) / (95 %/
    2500 t) ~ 1/90, because the policy maximises energy and access has
    to carry the whole avoidance (real seals add preference and
    individual specialisation); the fit used fix60's policy-shaped
    fields; and the ~4 % assumes a greedy seal. Test: the retrained
    diet. Below ~3 % herring raise a toward 2e-4, above ~10 % lower it.

169 HAND-CODED HEURISTICS VS A TRAINED POLICY; greedy_flee ARM (2026-10-17)
================================================================

169.1 Question (user): is the behaviour not just "go towards food, run
    from predators, eat when hungry", so that shorter rollouts or a
    plain heuristic would do as well as the trained nets (fix58)?
169.2 New arm greedy_flee (lib/diagnostics/viability.py): greedy, but a
    cell whose predator biomass >= its own (HIDE_PREDATOR_RATIO) moves
    all its mass to the legal neighbour with the least predator biomass
    if that is strictly less (otherwise greedy), and a cell with reserve
    >= 0.95 full rests (HIDE_SATIATION). It never hides. Normative like
    greedy_hide; verdict precedence greedy > greedy_hide > greedy_flee.
    tools/viability.py gains the --currents flags (default off, as
    before) so a policy trained with currents is compared on its own
    world. Tests: three new cases in tests/test_viability.py (21).
169.3 Setup: mareld2.yaml copy with seals muted and absolute map paths
    (= fix58's world; seal entries in the library are inert when
    muted; 165 bycatch may or may not have been in fix58's run),
    60x60, --spawn configured --mortality on --migration on --currents
    on, 5 years, 3 seeds, arms greedy, greedy_hide, greedy_flee, eat,
    policy (fix58). ~1-1.5 min per seed per arm on CPU.
169.4 Final-year mean / spawn (range over seeds):
      fg            greedy     hide       flee       eat        fix58
      phyto         0.12       0.15-0.25  0.15-0.23  0.14       0.59-0.62
      zoo           0.16       0.18-0.19  0.17-0.18  0.16       0.72
      benthos       0.13-0.27  0.04-0.11  0.05-0.07  1.24-1.32  0.55-0.62

169.5 Why the heuristics lose (traces, seed 20260530):
    - Perpetual travel. Under greedy the herring put 95-98 % of their
      mass on move from tick ~100 and their reserve falls 0.7 -> 0.02
      by tick 500: the reachable-payoff potential (max over the grid,
      0.85 per km) always shows a better cell than the depleted one
      they stand on. Porpoises do the same from tick 3: the greedy
      herring dissolve the dense patches the porpoises spawn on (101 ->
      13 t/cell in three ticks), after which 0.85 * best neighbour
      (~196) beats the local payoff (<20) forever and they starve
      walking (extinct@43-49). Under eat (no movement) porpoises live
      ~1755+ ticks. The move-vs-stay threshold is what the nets learned
      and the heuristic got wrong.
    - No restraint at the bottom. Every arm's zooplankton eats with
      all its mass and holds phyto at 0.12-0.25x; under fix58 phyto
      sits at 0.6x and zoo at 0.72x (section 123 saw the same with
      fix35).
    - Flee vs hide is NOT tested by this run: both are within seed
      noise, but herring and porpoises starve from travelling before
      predation pressure matters, so the comparison is masked by the
      move rule (the same rule killed porpoises in 121.3).
169.6 Reading: the behaviours are simple in kind (fix58 is a 1x16
    memoryless per-cell map, and section 87.3 / fix58's log show most
    learning in the first ~50 updates), but the THRESHOLDS - when to
    stop moving, how hard to graze - decide the outcome, and the
    obvious hand-coded rules set them badly. A satisficing heuristic
    (stay while intake covers the cost) was not tried; it would be the
    fair next arm. The rig still applies one heuristic to every DM at
    once; whether a heuristic can replace the net for one group alone
    needs a mixed arm (policy for the rest).
169.7 Follow-up (user: "do the next steps"). Two additions to the rig:
    - _stay arms (greedy_stay, greedy_hide_stay, greedy_flee_stay): a
      cell that can feed does not climb while its intake at full
      appetite is >= STAY_COST_RATIO (1.0, break-even) x the feeding
      cost the tick charges (_feeding_cost: resting metabolism x Q10 x
      feeding_cost x impact factor). Stops at the first cell that pays.
    - Mixed arms (install_mixed, tools/viability.py --mixed-fg FG,...):
      fix58 policies for every DM except FG, which runs the hand-coded
      arm. Label behaviour@FG; diagnostic, never decides the verdict.
    Tests: feeding cost equals what apply_energy_costs charges; a stay
    cell that pays never moves and the rule changes nothing elsewhere;
    a mixed arm overrides exactly one group.

169.9 What the nets do that the rules do not (year 2, seed 20260530,
    biomass-weighted action shares, tools: scratch shares.py):
      fix58:         zoo rest 0.78 eat 0.21; herring rest 0.20 eat 0.70
                     move 0.09, reserve fill 0.73; gadoids eat 0.97
                     move 0.03; porpoises eat 1.00
      stay@zoo:      zoo rest 0.00 eat 1.00 (same reserve fill 0.52)
      stay@herring:  herring rest 0.00 move 0.23, reserve fill 0.42
      stay@gadoids:  gadoids move 0.00 (a cell that pays on benthos or
                     zoo never leaves for herring)
    Reading: porpoises (no predators, one prey field) are the only
    group a plain rule replaces. The other three need a group-specific
    setting the rules get wrong in opposite directions: zooplankton
    must rest ~80 % (restraint plus refuge; the hide rule never fires
    because herring rarely outweigh zoo in a cell), herring must stop
    travelling sooner and rest some, and gadoids must NOT stop at the
    first cell that pays but keep searching for herring. A per-group
    threshold sweep would be hand-doing what ARS does. Caveat: the
    other groups' nets were co-evolved with fix58's version of the
    replaced group, which favours the net in a mixed arm.

170 THE TRAINED ZOOPLANKTON POLICY AGAINST COPEPOD BIOLOGY (2026-10-17)
================================================================

170.1 Question (user): how well does the model's zooplankton policy
    match reality? fix58 policies in fix58's world (169.3), 3 seeds,
    3 years with the first discarded. New probes (untracked, like the
    rest of tools/probes): zoo_behaviour.py (monthly / diel / binned
    action shares, stocks, ration, grazing vs gross production) and
    zoo_tradeoff.py (per cell: what eating instead of resting gains a
    unit of zooplankton vs what it risks from herring). Literature is
    the existing notes, no new search: research_notes/Sillens
    vinterfoda/zooplankton_refuge.md (DVM, time budget, refuge),
    .../winter_food_and_feeding.md (SHARK A17 seasonal stock),
    Zooplankton energibudget/copepod_energetics.md (ration, hunger,
    zoo:phyto), Litteraturbaserad growth rate per FG/plankton.md
    (grazing share of PP).
170.2 What the zooplankton can perceive: own biomass and energy,
    phytoplankton (cell + 4 neighbours) and the light level. It does
    NOT observe herring, so no predator-dependent behaviour is
    possible (field copepods start/stop DVM within 12-24 h of fish
    being added/removed, Bollens & Frost 1991).
170.3 Measured (mean of 3 seeds; seed spread of the annual rest share
    0.771-0.776):
      month  rest  eat   move  vis_h  zoo t/km2 phyto t/km2 ration/d grazed/prod grazed/stock/d
      Jan    0.67  0.33  0.00  0.68   0.8       10.1        0.26     0.89        0.022
      Apr    0.79  0.18  0.03  0.62   9.8       13.3        0.16     1.00        0.117
      Jun    0.79  0.16  0.05  0.62   12.7      13.6        0.14     1.00        0.133
      Sep    0.82  0.18  0.00  0.61   6.2       12.4        0.16     1.02        0.077
      Nov    0.83  0.17  0.00  0.61   1.9       10.3        0.14     1.13        0.026
      year   0.77  0.21  0.02  0.63   6.3       12.1        0.18     1.00        0.078
    (vis_h = share visible to herring where herring are, floor 0.5;
    ration = t phyto per t zooplankton per day, x 4800/4500 in body
    energy; reserve fill before the decision 0.51 everywhere, the
    growth step drains it to u each tick, so hunger cannot be read.)
    Diel: eat share per 6 h block (00-06, 06-12, 12-18, 18-24):
    DJF .30 .21 .31 .43; MAM .11 .13 .22 .29; JJA .12 .12 .20 .23;
    SON .14 .14 .21 .24. Night/day eat ratio by sun elevation 1.42
    (DJF), 1.17, 1.08, 1.08. Rest vs herring:zoo ratio in the cell:
    0.82 at < 0.01, 0.74 at > 1 (falls where herring are; correlation,
    the policy cannot see them).
170.4 Individual trade-off (zoo_tradeoff.py): eating instead of resting
    gains 0.12-0.13 of the unit's biomass per tick in energy (intake at
    its appetite minus the extra feeding cost, priced at 4838 MJ/t =
    energy content + reserve at u; capped by growth it is still
    <= 0.064), while the extra herring risk of being visible is
    0.0002-0.002 per tick (0.006-0.018 on winter/autumn days; the
    estimate is 0.67-0.94 of the realised herring intake). Eating pays
    in 99.99-100 % of the zooplankton biomass, yet 62-83 % of it rests.
    The rest is not anti-predator and not individually rational: it is
    group restraint learned from the group-energy reward (with a rule
    that eats, phyto 0.13 and zoo 0.16 of spawn, section 169.8). The
    restraint holds phytoplankton at 10-13.6 t/km2 against K 24, i.e.
    at ~K/2 where logistic production peaks - the harvest optimum of a
    group, not of an individual. Caveats: the risk counts herring only
    (gadoids also eat zooplankton, M2 0.089 /yr, too small to close a
    30-600x gap); there are no individuals, so "individual" means a
    marginal unit of the cell's biomass.
170.5 Against the literature:
    - Time budget: eat 16-34 % (year 21 %) vs 27-99 % (median ~51 %)
      for non-ambush Skagerrak copepods (Tiselius & Jonsson 1990),
      81-98 % for Acartia (Saiz 1994). Low, but the 6 h tick is
      linear in the eat share, so a time budget is weakly defined;
      the ration is the better test.
    - Ration 0.14-0.28 t/t/day (0.15-0.30 body energy/day): inside
      the field range (C. finmarchicus ~19-40 % body C/d; lab max
      median 0.44 at 10 C). Plausible. But it is HIGHEST in Jan-Feb,
      where real copepods eat least (low food, Calanus absent or in
      diapause), because model phyto barely drops in winter.
    - Diel: the clean test is by sun elevation: night/day eat ratio
      1.08-1.42 against ~3x (Durbin et al. 1990; nocturnal feeding,
      Daro 1988). The 6 h blocks rise through the day in MAM-SON
      (min 00-12, max 18-24), most likely following the phytoplankton's
      own light-driven daily cycle (production by day only), which the
      zooplankton observes; not tested. 6 h ticks limit resolution. Rest by night 0.63-0.81
      protects where nature has no refuge (double count with
      dark_ratio, small in absolute terms).
    - Refuge: visible to herring 0.61-0.69 vs the literature daytime
      0.65-0.9 (summer) / 0.5-0.8 (winter) - consistent since the
      floor went to 0.5 (section 162).
    - Predator response: none possible (170.2).
    - Seasonality of behaviour: rest highest Sep-Nov (0.82-0.83),
      lowest Jan-Feb (0.66-0.67). Neritic copepods do not go dormant
      on the bank; the Calanus diapause (Aug/Sep-Jan) happens in the
      Norwegian Trench. A superficial match at best, for a different
      reason (food per capita).
    - Stock: annual mean 6.3 t/km2 vs A17 0-25 m 7.1-10.0; winter
      0.8 vs 1.2-1.7; peak Jun 12.7 vs May 26-36. Level right, peak
      late and 2-3x low (as in the winter-food note).
    - Grazing: 1.5-13 % of the phytoplankton stock per day (summer
      12-13 %). That grazing equals gross production (0.89-1.13 per
      month) is a tautology of a near-stationary stock with one loss
      term, not a finding.
      Literature: mesozooplankton 6 % (mode) / 22.6 % (mean) of PP
      (Calbet 2001), central North Sea 3-14 %, Kattegat/Skagerrak
      < 4 % of stock per day (summer up to 48 % of PP). Even taking the
      model's r as net of microzooplankton grazing (plankton.md), 15-57
      % would be the comparable share: the model's phytoplankton is
      top-down controlled (stock ~K/2, not near K). Phytoplankton stock is nearly flat
      over the year (9.8-13.6 t/km2), with no spring bloom, against a
      ~10-fold seasonal PP cycle in the region.
170.6 Reading: the policy's numbers that matter for the rest of the
    food web (stock level, ration, visible share) are in or near the
    literature ranges, but for the wrong reason. The behaviour is a
    commons restraint that real copepods do not show (selection acts
    on individuals, and a unit that eats where eating pays outgrows
    one that holds back); it compensates for a phyto-zoo structure in
    which nothing but zooplankton grazing controls phytoplankton and
    zooplankton can track phytoplankton without a generation lag, so
    an eating zooplankton suppresses the bloom. The density-dependent
    zooplankton M1 is NOT the fix (gamma ~ 0 in the Taethetsberoende
    report). Candidate structural directions, untested: phytoplankton
    losses other than mesozooplankton grazing (sinking, lysis,
    microzooplankton as an explicit sink), a recruitment lag in the
    zooplankton growth, or a reward that does not credit a group for
    restraint. Weak links: hunger and food dependence cannot be read
    (fill and phyto have no spread); 6 h ticks blur the diel test;
    one checkpoint.

171 WHY THERE IS NO PHYTOPLANKTON SPRING BLOOM (2026-10-17)
================================================================

171.1 Question (user): why does the phytoplankton have no spring bloom?
    Under fix58 (170) the stock is 9.8-13.6 t/km2 all year (max/min
    1.4, peak June), although the light growth factor of section 138
    runs 0.10 (Dec) - 1.14 (Jun), a ~10x cycle in the growth RATE.
171.2 Observed (SHARK, A17 58.28 N 10.51 E, 2010-2023, 0-10 m bottle
    mean per visit, monthly mean / median, n 8-14 visits per month;
    POST https://shark.smhi.se/api/sample/download, tableView
    sharkdata_physicalchemical, dataTypes ["Physical and Chemical"],
    stationName ["A17" with the Swedish ring]):
      month       J    F    M    A    M    J    J    A    S    O    N    D
      chl ug/l   1.21 3.88 3.28 1.48 0.94 0.80 0.46 0.65 0.79 1.81 1.54 0.77
      (median)   0.60 1.07 1.47 1.28 0.97 0.67 0.43 0.63 0.67 1.43 1.40 0.60
      NO3 umol/l 4.90 5.13 2.60 0.43 0.14 0.11 0.10 0.10 0.10 0.24 1.00 3.37
      SiO3       4.71 5.12 1.43 1.17 1.06 0.51 0.25 0.63 0.97 1.82 1.77 4.36
    Bloom Feb-Mar (mean 8.4x the July minimum, median 3.4x; monthly
    sampling misses short peaks), second peak Oct-Nov, summer MINIMUM
    in July when nitrate sits at the detection limit (0.1) from May to
    September. Chl is not carbon (C:chl rises in summer light), so the
    carbon amplitude is somewhat smaller, but the phase is clear: the
    model's summer maximum is the real summer minimum.
171.3 Experiments (tools/probes/phyto_bloom.py, fix58 policies frozen,
    fix58 world, 2 seeds, 3 years with the first discarded; phyto
    t/km2 by month J..D, max/min):
      base        10.1 11.5 13.1 13.4 13.5 13.6 13.3 13.0 12.4 11.5 10.3  9.8   1.4  (Jun)
      nograze     20.9 22.2 23.3 23.6 23.6 23.6 23.6 23.5 23.3 23.0 22.2 21.1   1.1  (K = 24)
      eat (zoo)    3.1  3.8  3.1  2.5  2.5  2.6  2.8  2.9  2.9  3.0  2.7  2.8   1.5  (Feb)
      loss 0.005   7.6 11.6 15.9 14.4 13.4 13.3 13.1 12.7 12.0 10.9  9.4  7.8   2.1  (Mar)
      loss 0.01    2.7  4.5 14.7 20.1 20.7 19.8 18.0 16.3 12.7 10.5  7.5  4.2   7.7  (May)
      loss 0.02    0.1  0.1  0.7 10.0 17.3 17.6 17.0 15.7 12.7  8.6  3.3  0.7   219  (Jun)
    (loss = extra phytoplankton loss per tick after growth.) In base,
    grazing per day equals the specific growth per day in every month
    within ~5 % (Jan 0.021/0.024, Jun 0.132/0.134); the zooplankton
    cycle (0.8 -> 12.7 t/km2, 15x) carries the seasonality instead.
    With loss 0.01 the frozen zooplankton is ~0 from January to May
    and recovers only in summer (3.4); with 0.02 it dies. The bloom
    appears exactly when the grazer is absent in spring: so it did in
    138.5 (all-eat arm, zooplankton ~0 Feb-Apr, phyto 0.02 -> 1.26),
    while eat@zoo here keeps 0.2-0.3 t/km2 of zooplankton through the
    winter and stays flat.
171.4 Reading, three mechanisms:
    (a) The phytoplankton has no loss of its own. Logistic growth with
        a light factor >= 0 can never be negative, so light only sets
        how fast the stock is replaced, not where it sits: alone it
        stays at K all year (nograze, 1.1x). Winter decline in nature
        comes from respiration, sinking and lysis exceeding light-
        limited growth; here only grazing can lower the stock.
    (b) The zooplankton absorbs the production. It tracks the
        phytoplankton without a lag and grazes what grows each month,
        holding the stock near K/2 (170.4); the seasonal forcing moves
        one trophic level up (a 2-level chain with top-down control has
        a prey level independent of productivity). With a zooplankton
        that always eats, the stock sits lower (2.5-3.8) but is just as
        flat.
    (c) No nutrients. K is one constant, so nothing ends a bloom: the
        summer has the most light and the highest production, and the
        stock stays highest there. In reality nitrate is used up by
        April and the summer is the minimum.
    A loss term alone (0.01-0.02/tick = 0.04-0.08 /day, inside
    respiration-plus-sinking ranges) does create a large cycle, but it
    peaks Apr-Jun (light), not Feb-Mar, keeps the summer high, and the
    frozen zooplankton cannot survive the low winter stock - a retrain
    and a recalibration would be needed: growth_rate is derived from
    the April dilution rate, which is already net of some of these
    losses, so a loss term needs r raised to keep the April net rate.
    The Feb-Mar timing and the summer minimum need a nutrient pool
    (winter replenishment, drawdown by growth; 138.7 listed "no
    nutrients" as open, 171.2 puts data under it). A third candidate
    is the grazer lag: the zooplankton growth_rate is not temperature
    scaled (the Q10 of section 143 acts only on action costs in
    movement.apply_energy_costs, so winter is CHEAPER for it, m
    0.74-0.80 Jan-Apr), whereas copepod growth has a 3-4x seasonal
    range from temperature alone (Hirst & Bunker 2003: 0.039 /d at
    5 C vs 0.128 at 15 C; plankton.md section 5). Real copepods at
    5-6 C cannot follow a February bloom; the model's can. Ranking:
    (a) is necessary (light alone gives 1.1x), (c) sets the phase,
    (b) sets the level and erases what amplitude is left. Not
    implemented; nothing in engine or library changed.

172 NUTRIENT POOL FOR LIGHT-LIMITED PRODUCERS (2026-10-18)
================================================================

172.1 User request after 171: implement a nutrient pool for the
    phytoplankton. Implemented OPT-IN; mareld2.yaml carries the block
    with enabled: false (fix61 was training and the probe reloads the
    manifest). No observation channel, so checkpoints still load, but
    enabling it changes the world: every policy needs retraining.
172.2 Model (lib/world/nutrients.py, Evans & Parslow 1985 form). Per
    cell a pool N in the producer's own units (t/km2 it could become).
    Growth dB = min(r L(t) B N/(N + k_N Y M(t)), N, K - B), paid out of
    N: the logistic factor is gone, K stays only as a ceiling (kept
    because without an own loss the stock has no way down; not
    calibrated for this, and in an ungrazed world it pins B at K and
    blocks uptake). Supply per tick N' = N keep(t) + supply(t) from
    dN/dt = Y [m (N0(t) - c) + max(dM/dt,0) N0 - max(-dM/dt,0) c],
    c = N/(Y M), M(t) the daylight light climate's mixed-layer depth,
    N0(t) 12 monthly values just below it. Grazing returns
    grazing_regeneration x the biomass it removes; that is the only
    closure, the budget is open. Initial N = Y M c_surface(start day).
172.3 Engine. The pool rides in the producer's unused energy_reserve
    slot: currents and the open boundary already move it with the
    water on both engines, and nothing that reads a reserve as energy
    reads a non decision maker's (observations, local reward, mass
    balance, movement clamp, population stability, GPU rollout
    reward are per DM). Guarded writers: predation (pool kept, regen
    added), impact mortality, the empty-cell sweep (CPU) and the
    b <= 0 zeroing (GPU). The per-group "energy" in the inference and
    training plots shows the pool for a nutrient producer (that number
    had no meaning for a non decision maker before). CPU:
    interactions.build_nutrient_tables / initialise_nutrient_pools
    (once, in the env constructor) / is_nutrient_producer,
    population_change._nutrient_limited_delta. GPU: TensorEcosystem
    nutrient tables (T, G, 1), population/predation/impact_mortality,
    initial_nutrients(reserve, light_start) used by the trainer.
    Loader: params['nutrients'] on every FG. FG editor: three NDM
    fields with help (the project block is edited in the manifest;
    the GUI keeps unknown simulation_settings keys).
172.4 Values. Library (phytoplankton; tick-independent):
    nutrient_half_saturation 1.0 umol N/l (0.5-2; MacIsaac & Dugdale
    1972 ~1.0 in nutrient-rich water [F], Fennel et al. 2006 NPZ 0.5
    [F], NORWECOM diatoms 2.0 [F]); nutrient_yield 0.795 t/km2 per
    (umol N/l x m) = 14 mg N/m2 x Redfield 5.68 g C/g N / C:WW 0.10
    (North Sea Ecopath 1:10 [F]); grazing_regeneration 0.3 (0.25-0.45;
    Acartia excretes ~0.25 of ingested N, Kioerboe et al. 1985 via
    Kuijper et al. 2004 [F]; pellets are export). Notes:
    research_notes/Naringspool for vaxtplankton/nutrient_parameters.md
    (Swedish dir name; Fasham 1990 not obtained). Manifest: N0 = SHARK
    A17 2010-2023 NO2+NO3 at 20-30 m by month (5.7 6.6 6.8 7.0 4.9 4.4
    2.8 1.4 0.9 0.9 2.5 3.9); surface (initial) = 0-10 m (171.2);
    exchange_m_per_day 0.2 = the top of the literature range (0.01-0.2;
    Hasager et al. 2003 Kattegat entrainment flux and halocline Kz
    analogues give 0.01-0.17 [D]), fitted below - PROVISIONAL.
172.5 Calibration (tools/probes/phyto_bloom.py, now with an optional

173 PHYTOPLANKTON LOSS TERM M1; SEASONAL PYCNOCLINE EXCHANGE (2026-10-18)
================================================================

173.1 User request after 172: implement the loss term. A non decision
    maker's natural_mortality is now its own loss M1: removed from the
    biomass before growth (CPU population_change.
    _apply_non_decision_maker_mortality, GPU mortality_keep for every
    group, the NDM path on biomass * keep), with --mortality on only,
    scaled by --mortality_multiplier, booked as natural mortality, and
    never touching the reserve slot (a nutrient pool is the water's;
    lost producer biomass is not remineralised). The growth budget
    counts it for an NDM as for a DM: g = (r_max + M1 + sum M2)/1460,
    left out with --mortality off. NDMs without natural_mortality are
    bit-identical; the library has none set (see 173.4). FG editor:
    "Natural Mortality M1" field and help on the NDM editor.
173.2 What M1 is (research_notes/Naringspool for vaxtplankton/
    phytoplankton_losses.md, subagent; Swedish dir name). The growth
    rate behind phytoplankton g (Stelfox-Widdicombe et al. 2004, 0.67
    /d, section 131) is a dilution rate [F]: 24 h in closed bottles,
    no nutrients added, so it is NET of respiration and of lysis
    (both act in every bottle) and GROSS of sinking. So M1 = the
    sinking loss (0.03 /d, range 0.01-0.1 for growing cells over a
    6-17 m mixed layer; Kattegat intact-cell flux ~0.025 /d), and
    respiration/lysis must not be added again. g stays 0.0670 /tick;
    r_max is re-derived: 97.8 - 22.63 - M1 /yr. After nutrient
    exhaustion the literature losses rise to 0.1-0.5 /d (stress lysis,
    aggregate sinking; ERSEM, NORWECOM): not implemented.
173.3 Seasonal exchange: exchange_m_per_day accepts 1 or 12 monthly
    values. Summer stratification vs winter storms (Hasager et al.
    2003: summer entrainment flux small against storm events [F]); the
    pattern 0.3 0.3 0.2 0.1 0.05 0.05 0.05 0.05 0.1 0.2 0.3 0.3 m/d is
    PROVISIONAL (shape from that contrast, levels fitted), inside the
    0.01-0.2 literature range in summer and above it in winter.

    pool, k_N 1.0, rho 0.3, g fixed at 0.0670, years 2-3). Seed

      0.005    seasonal  0.61         +0.42              4.6x Mar   0.01
      0.005    0.2       0.82         +0.24              3.7x Mar   0.02
      0.0075   seasonal  0.45         +0.02              17x Apr    0 (extinct)
