175 NUTRIENT-STRESS LOSS: IMPLEMENTED, NOT SWITCHED ON (2026-10-18)
================================================================

175.1 User request after 174: fix what remains (summer too high,
    no autumn bloom). The literature mechanism (173.2): after nutrient
    exhaustion lysis and aggregate sinking rise to 0.1-0.5 /d (ERSEM:
    lysis 0.045 / 0.125 / 0.5 /d at nutrient limitation 1 / 0.3 / 0;
    Si-triggered sinking up to 3.5 m/d; NORWECOM likewise).
175.2 Implemented: a producer with stress_loss_max L_s loses
    L_s c (1 - f)/(f + c) of its biomass per tick, f = N/(N + half)
    its growth limitation, c = stress_loss_shape (default 0.1 =
    ERSEM's curve without the replete baseline, which the dilution
    rate already holds). After supply, before growth; exported, booked
    as natural mortality. CPU population_change._nutrient_limited_delta,
    GPU population (stress_max / stress_shape tensors), nutrients.
    stress_settings / stress_loss, FG editor fields and help.
    Tests: test_nutrients (ERSEM shape, order vs growth, pool spared),
    GPU parity case with L_s 0.08 on CPU and CUDA.
175.3 Calibration attempt (phyto_bloom.py, fix58 world + pool + M1
    0.005 + seasonal exchange, year 2-3, seed 20260530):
    - frozen fix58 zooplankton, L_s 0.01 / 0.025 / 0.05 / 0.1 per
      tick: the summer minimum appears (Jul/peak 0.13-0.26 vs A17
      0.12) but the zooplankton goes EXTINCT in every run, after which
      the dynamics are grazer-free (peak April, winter 0.1-2 t/km2).
    - zooplankton on the eat rule (intake upper bound), L_s 0.01:
      P 1.4 3.6 12.5 4.9 2.5 2.2 2.2 2.2 2.2 1.9 1.6 1.4 (peak Mar),
      zooplankton max 2.4 t/km2 (A17 May 26), summer NO3 1.2-0.4
      (A17 0.1): the grazer holds the producer down and still cannot
      build biomass. M1 only + eat: zooplankton max 2.3.
    The two bracket the observed state (low chl, nitrate at the
    detection limit, 5-26 t/km2 of copepods) from opposite sides.
175.4 Diagnosis (tools/probes/budget_gate.py on the library): an
    always-eating zooplankton breaks even on its feeding cost alone at
    2.6 t/km2 of visible phytoplankton; covering its M1 (19.6 /yr) and
    the herring budget needs roughly 5 [D]. A17 summer chl 0.46-0.8
    ug/l is ~1.5-3 t/km2 in model units (C:chl 50, C:WW 0.1, 6 m mixed
    layer) [D], yet copepods hold 5-26 t/km2: their summer food is
    microzooplankton (copepods control ciliates year-round, Nielsen &
    Kioerboe 1994, plankton.md section 5) and the subsurface
    chlorophyll maximum below the mixed layer (~30 % of Kattegat
    production), neither of which the model has. The gap is energetic;
    a retrain cannot close it. stress_loss_max is therefore NOT set in
    the library: any value would be calibrated against an extinct or
    an eat-rule grazer.
175.5 The autumn bloom is the same story (nutrients and a grazer that
    does not collapse); exchange was not tuned to chase it.
175.6 Options for the user: (a) give the zooplankton summer food - an
    explicit microzooplankton pool on regenerated production, or a
    subsurface producer layer - structural, needs its own literature
    pass; (b) revisit the zooplankton half-saturation 20 t/km2
    (section 134) against the model's phytoplankton units, a
    calibration with a known footprint; (c) then set L_s and retrain.

176 MICROZOOPLANKTON POOL: FEASIBILITY CHECKED, NOT BUILT (2026-10-18)
================================================================

176.1 User's choice after 175: option 1, give the zooplankton summer
    food. Design: an explicit microzooplankton NDM grazing the
    phytoplankton (the 60 % micrograzing section 131 subtracts from r
    would become a transfer, and phytoplankton g gross, ~0.1675/tick
    via M2_micro ~147 /yr). Literature: research_notes/Mikrozooplankton/
    microzooplankton.md (subagent): mixed-layer biomass central ~1.5 t
    WW/km2 (winter 0.3-0.5, early summer 0.3-1, late summer 1-5, HD
    peaks ~10; upper bounds, protozoa peak below the mixed layer);
    pool umax 0.5 /d at 10 C (HD-dominated), Q10 2.6, GGE 0.3, Imax 1.7
    /d, K ~30 ug C/l (field), Type II; grazes 50-60 % of annual PP
    (spring 10-25 %, summer 50-100 %+); 25-30 % of copepod diet (50-80 %
    late summer), no size-independent preference; excretes ~0.4 of
    ingested N; non-predatory mortality 0.05 /d.
176.2 Feasibility in the engine's own terms. The DM predation splits
    the eat mass over the prey (shares), each prey with its own
    Holling term, so a second prey does not add a second ceiling: the
    intake per eating tonne is at most the best single prey's. The
    zooplankton needs ~172 MJ/t/tick (feeding cost 90 + M1 + the
    herring budget, at s = u); at the zoo -> phytoplankton form
    (ceiling 0.25, K 20 t/km2) and ciliate quality 0.8 x 4500 that is
    >= 4.7 t/km2 of microzooplankton, against a literature central 1.5
    (0.3-1 in early summer). The pool alone does not close the gap.
176.3 Zooplankton half-saturation (option 2 of 175.6), full engine,
    fix58 world + pool + M1 0.005 + seasonal exchange: K 8 or 5 t/km2
    (100 ug C/l in a 6-10 m layer; K 20 is ~330 ug C/l in summer's 6 m,
    above the 50-150 of copepod_energetics.md) changes little: frozen
    zooplankton same as K 20; eat-rule zooplankton max 1.6-1.9 t/km2
    (K 20: 2.4) - it grazes the phytoplankton lower and its stock stays
    supply-limited. A 0-D box (scratch) was too crude (mean field, no
    rest/hide) to judge persistence and was not used for conclusions.
176.4 The actual ceiling: production. Model gross phytoplankton
    production with pool + M1 ~12 g C/m2/yr (C:WW 0.1), July 0.14 t/km2
    /d at a stock of ~7.7 t/km2 (P/B 0.02 /d, f ~0.07 at 0.07 umol/l
    with k_N 1.0); before the pool 37 g C/m2/yr. Observed 14C PP
    190-290 g C/m2/yr (plankton.md section 3); net of the 60 %
    micrograzing the model removes, 76-116 - the model is 6-10x low,
    ~20x in summer (North Sea summer PP 700-1000 mg C/m2/d). Real summer
    production is regenerated (Kattegat ~30 % of annual PP in summer
    subsurface layers; microzooplankton excretion 35-50 % of summer N
    demand) at low stock and fast turnover; the model has high stock,
    no turnover, and exports every non-grazing loss.
176.5 What a fix needs, together (not built; user to decide):
    (a) explicit microzooplankton (176.1) with Q10 (it lags the bloom
        at 3-5 C), excreting ~0.4 of intake to the pool;
    (b) fast regeneration of the producer's own losses (lysis -> DOM ->
        NH4 in the mixed layer) instead of full export, and an NH4-like
        low half-saturation (0.1-0.5 umol/l) for regenerated N;
    (c) a concentration-based (mixed-layer-scaled) half-saturation for
        grazers, as the nutrient half-saturation already is;
    (d) then stress loss, recalibration of g/M1/m against A17 and a
        retrain. Phytoplankton g ~2.5x and the K question reopen.
    Nothing in engine or library changed in this section.

177 MICROZOOPLANKTON, CONCENTRATION-BASED GRAZING, REGENERATION (2026-10-18)
================================================================

177.1 User's call after 176: build the whole package. Built:
    (a) Grazing non decision makers (interactions.build_ndm_grazing /
        ndm_grazing_rate, population_change.apply_ndm_grazing, GPU
        TensorEcosystem.ndm_grazing): an NDM with a checked pair that
        carries max_intake_rate takes B_g m(t) a' F/(1 + a' h F) of the
        prey at the start of the population step (before M1, fixed
        order), F = B_p, or B_p^2/(B_p + F0) with food_threshold F0
        (ERSEM's food-perception term); a' = a x M_ref/M(t) with
        mixed_layer_reference_m; m(t) = grazing_q10^((T - t_ref)/10) on
        its temperature layer (inert without the calendar); capped at
        MAX_HARVEST_FRAC; grows growth_efficiency x intake; returns
        excretion_regeneration x (1 - gge) x intake to the prey's
        nutrient pool; booked as predation. growth_budget counts an
        NDM predator whose pair has an attack rate.
    (b) mixed_layer_reference_m on a DM pair: folded into the per-tick
        pair table (light_mult_table), so the GPU needed no new code.
    (c) stress_regeneration: the lysed share of the stress loss
        returns to the pool (CPU and GPU).

        cost, else rest), needed because every checkpoint is invalid
        (a new FG changes the action layout, 5 + N_all).
    (e) FG editor fields and help for the new species keys (the FG
        Interactions editor does not show NDM predators; the pair is
        edited in fg_library.yaml).

178 ZOOPLANKTON SWITCHES AWAY FROM SCARCE MICROZOOPLANKTON (2026-10-18)

178.1 Probe of fix62 at generation 4 (checkpoint copied first;
    tools/probes/phyto_bloom.py base, 3 years, burn-in 1, seeds
    20260530/31; tools/probes/pair_intake.py 2 years). The trained
    zooplankton is 2.5x the rule's (mean 2.4 t/km2, max 10.2 in March vs
    0.92 / 3.4) and eats 97 % phytoplankton. It grazed the
    microzooplankton from 1.2 to 0.008 t/km2 in two weeks of early
    March (zooplankton 9-10 t/km2) and on to ~1e-18: every cell stays
    positive (no extinction threshold), but nothing regrows from there,
    so years 2-3 have no microzooplankton at all. Without it the bloom
    is bigger and later (Mar, 17 t/km2) and nitrate is gone by March
    (0.10 vs A17 2.33 umol/l): nitrate logRMSE 0.98, r(P,chl) +0.83.
    This is the caveat of 177.4: the calibration ran a rule-driven
    zooplankton that never peaked above 3.4.

178.2 Cause: Type II on zooplankton -> microzooplankton gives no
    low-density refuge; at 10 t/km2 the zooplankton's per-capita take of
    the microzooplankton exceeds its best growth (0.3 x 0.425 per tick).
    Fix: functional_response 3 on that pair (prey switching: copepods
    turn from suspension to ambush feeding as ciliates become common,
    Kioerboe, Saiz & Viitasalo 1996). a per (t/km2)^2 at 10 m, still
    scaled by M_ref/M(t). Same checkpoint, scratch library copies:

      a     NO3 logRMSE  r(P,chl)  r(Z,obs)  Z mean/max  micro  micro/PP

    0.1 (= the Type II clearance 0.05 at 0.5 t/km2 of microzooplankton)

    microzooplankton M1, microzooplankton egestion (1 - GGE 0.3 -
    excretion 0.4 = 0.3 of its intake). D -> nutrient pool at k(T) = k
    2^((T - 10)/10) per day, sinking export w/M. Zooplankton respiration
    is NOT added: grazing_regeneration 0.3 already stands for its NH4
    excretion (Kioerboe et al. 1985), adding it double counts (an early
    run with it, 0.5/0.5, gave PP 18-20). Phytoplankton M1 and faecal
    pellets stay export.

179.2 Literature (subagent, research_notes/Detritus och
    remineralisering/detritus_remineralisation.md): ERSEM pe_R1
    0.5 (half of zooplankton mortality/excretion to labile DOM, half to
    POM sinking 5-10 m/d), labile DOM turnover up to 1 /d, Q10 2 at 10 C;
    NEMURO PON->NH4 0.1 /d at 0 C, Q10 2, PON sinking 40 m/d; Fennel et
    al. 2006 0.03 / 0.01 /d. Recommendation: one fast pool, share 0.5
    (0.4-0.7), k 0.4 /d at 10 C, Q10 2, w 0.5 m/d. Field: summer f-ratio
    < 0.02 - 0.1 in the Norwegian Trench / Kattegat (Bendtsen &
    Richardson 2018 [F]) - summer production runs on N recycled in the
    layer; the model's f-ratio is ~0.7.

    below the mixed layer, zooplankton mean 1.0 -> 2.0-4.1, r(Z, A17)

    production (the layer reaches nitrate the mixed layer cannot), not
    only relocates it. Go.

180.3 Mechanism (lib/world/nutrients.py docstring; both engines):
    manifest nutrients.subsurface_layer {bottom_m, light_attenuation_
    per_m, reservoir_umol_l, reservoir_exchange_m_per_day}; library
    water_layer: mixed|subsurface on a producer. Exactly one producer
    per layer, one nutrient_yield. Per tick a linear 2x2 map
    (layer_tables) moves water AND algae: entrainment f_up = dM+/H,
    detrainment f_dn = dM-/M, diffusive exchange e (the old
    exchange_m_per_day, now between the layers) and e_b with the
    reservoir; total new N is the one flux e_b (N_res - c_d). Each
    producer's own table is then keep 1, supply 0, half k_N Y x its
    layer thickness; sub_mixed_layer_umol_l becomes the initial
    subsurface concentration. Light (daylight.subsurface_light_
    schedule): surface PAR x exp(-Kd M) x exp(-Kd2 z) over the layer,
    normalised like the mixed layer (the species' I_k in the mixed
    layer on day 105). Grazer pairs with mixed_layer_reference_m on a
    subsurface prey scale by M_ref / H(t). Runs first in the
    population step (population_change.apply_layer_exchange; GPU
    TensorEcosystem.layer_exchange). Without the layer block a
    subsurface producer is inert under daylight-only projects and
    refused when nutrients are on. Bug caught by the parity test: the
    GPU first wrote the mixed column, then read it as a view.

180.4 Library / manifest. subsurface_phytoplankton: the phytoplankton's
    r_max, M1, energy, pool keys and grazing pairs (derived g 0.1675,
    same as phytoplankton), light_saturation 30 (shade-adapted, 20-60),
    spawned on the phytoplankton layout; zooplankton_preys_on_ and
    microzooplankton_preys_on_subsurface_phytoplankton as their
    phytoplankton pairs; zooplankton observes it. Manifest: bottom 30 m,

    exchange [1.0 1.0 0.6 0.3 0.2 0.2 0.2 0.2 0.3 0.6 1.0 1.0] m/d;
    initial 20000-60000 t (inference 40000).
    Scratch calibration (rule eat_pays, plankton world, seed 20260530):
      variant           NO3   NO3d  r(P,chl) col/obs PP    Z mean r(Z)
      eb 0.3            0.69  0.62  +0.63    0.34    35.9  2.96  +0.73

181.3 Literature (subagent, research_notes/Zooplankton vinterdodlighet/
    zoo_autumn_closure.md, Swedish dir name): copepod feeding/growth
    Q10 2.8 (Hansen, Bjornsen & Hansen 1997, used by Kioerboe & Hirst
    2014 [F]), Huntley & Lopez growth 3.0 [S], Hirst & Lampitt 2.3 [S];
    in situ fecundity 1.4-1.6 (Hirst & Bunker 2003 [A]); ERSEM 2.0 at
    10 C, NEMURO 2.0, PISCES 2.14, all on the whole response [SRC];
    Fennel and ECOSMO none. Quadratic closures (NEMURO, PISCES, Fennel)
    give 0.37-1.3 /d at 26 t/km2 and would remove the May peak; PISCES
    chose the square form for stability, not data. Regional
    invertebrate predation PEAKS in Aug-Oct (Sagitta setosa in Gullmar
    310 ind/m3 on 1 Oct 1998, up to 48 %/d of single copepod species
    [F]; Mnemiopsis 5-16 %/d Aug-Sep [F, slides]) and is gone by
    December: a lower autumn M1 is contradicted. Gullmar 1978-81
    (Lindahl & Hernroth 1983 [F]): mesozooplankton highest Oct-Dec,
    primary production ~800 mg C/m2/d in the second half of the season
    vs 500 in the first - the autumn stock is fed by autumn production.

181.4 Diagnosis. The zooplankton's daily ration is 12-19 %/d from June
    to October (gen 9 base: deep layer + microzooplankton; it eats
    almost no mixed-layer phytoplankton in summer). That does not pay
    M1 5.3 %/d plus herring 1-3 %/d at 12-14 C, where the Q10 2.0
    metabolism costs 1.3x its annual mean; the same 19 %/d grows the
    stock in a 5 C March. A17 October food is 0-10 m chl 1.8-1.9 ug/l
    (~70-90 ug C/l) against the model's ~8 ug C/l mixed-layer
    phytoplankton (0.8-1.2 t/km2 at 10 m), ~20 ug C/l in the fading
    subsurface layer and ~8 ug C/l of microzooplankton. The October
    deficit is top-down: switching the microzooplankton's grazing on
    the phytoplankton off in Sep-Nov (diagnostic only) lifts October
    phytoplankton 1.2 -> 3.4 t/km2, r(P,chl) +0.75 -> +0.86 and
    November zooplankton 0.20 -> 1.17; halving it gives 2.0 / +0.85 /
    0.47. In the model the microzooplankton (0.6-0.8 t/km2, ~1:1 with
    the phytoplankton, Q10 2.6 at 13-14 C) holds the autumn mixed layer
    once the zooplankton has collapsed - a cascade with a low-zooplankton
    state. Without it the phytoplankton still only reaches 3.4 (A17
    ~7-9 at C:chl 40-50): light (factor 0.37 in October) and nitrate
    limit the rest. Literature (subagent, research_notes/
    Mikrozooplankton/autumn_microzooplankton.md): field autumn
    ciliates + heterotrophic dinoflagellates are 10-30 ug C/l
    (Helgoland Sep-Oct 2007/08 9.5-31 [D from F data]; Kattegat HD 42
    in Aug-Sep, 163 in November, Hansen 1991 [F]), so the model's 6-8
    is plausible to low, and its 8 %/d grazing is not excessive
    (Kattegat HD took 6-9 %/d of a Ceratium bloom that still grew,
    Nielsen 1991 [F]). The real October gap is the phytoplankton
    itself (~90 vs ~10 ug C/l): the Skagerrak/Kattegat autumn bloom is
    chain diatoms and Tripos/Ceratium, a size refuge from ciliates
    (prey < ~35 um) with a slow, lagged HD response, fed by nutrients
    entrained at destratification. The model's single phytoplankton
    has neither the refuge nor the entrainment in October (mixed layer
    10 m in Sep and Oct). Candidate next step, for the user: an
    autumn/large-cell share the microzooplankton cannot eat (an
    edibility term or a second producer), not a weaker grazer.

181.5 Implemented (both engines): ``ingestion_q10`` on a decision maker
    (lib/world/temperature.py ``ingestion_q10``; the loader requires a
    DM and a temperature layer; interactions.build_temperature_tables
    builds ``env.ingestion_temp_table`` (T, N_dm) =
    metabolism_multiplier(layer, tick, q10, annual_mean), 1 for a DM
    without it; predation multiplies ``effective_intake_rate`` by
    interactions.ingestion_temperature(env), GPU ``predation`` its rate
    by ``self.ingestion_temp[light_index]``). The whole response
    scales (a and 1/h together), so the half-saturation stays and the
    annual mean is 1: library a and h are annual means and the growth
    budget's s* is unchanged. Library: zooplankton ingestion_q10 2.8
    (layer mean_0_50m: Feb-Mar x0.68, Sep x1.37). FG editor field
    "Ingestion Q10" + help. Not adopted: density-dependent M1 (it
    reopens the early spring - Feb 1.9 vs 0.5 - and a realised mean M1
    off the 0.0134 the growth rate is derived from), herring Type III,
    Q10 on M1, M1 regeneration.

    the layer (section 179) to keep A17's subsurface maximum - left to
    the user.

      mixed, e = 1-0.8N/(N+0.3)   1.10  +0.78  0.60  +0.80  +0.75  13.7  0.84/0.60/0.45
      both,  e = 1-0.9N/(N+0.3)   1.09  +0.79  0.71  +0.87  +0.80  13.5  1.21/1.38/0.44
      subsurface, e = 0.3         0.94  +0.79  0.69  +0.83  +0.86  10.3  1.33/1.07/0.25
      subsurface, e = 0.15        1.06  +0.79  0.79  +0.78  +0.86  11.4  1.53/1.37/0.38
      subsurface, e(N) 0/1        0.81  +0.76  0.67  +0.66  +0.87  6.7   1.36/0.82/0.16
      subsurface, e(N) 0/2        0.84  +0.76  0.74  +0.63  +0.88  7.1   1.58/1.09/0.21
      subsurface, e(N) 0.1/2      0.81  +0.77  0.67  +0.69  +0.88  6.7   1.37/0.94/0.19
      subsurface, e(N) 0.15/1     0.77  +0.76  0.60  +0.73  +0.87  6.6   1.28/0.67/0.14
    (e(N) floor/K = floor + (1-floor) N/(N+K), N the layer's nitrate in
    umol/l; A17 Z Mar 4.3, Oct/Nov/Dec 2.9/3.5/1.2.) An edible share on
    the MIXED-layer producer, constant or rising with nitrate (the
    diatom rule: large cells at high N), starves the winter
    microzooplankton (Feb 0.02-0.23 vs 2.4) and pulls the spring back to
    February (Z Mar 13.5 vs A17 4.3, nitrate gone in March): rejected. A
    constant share on the subsurface producer does the same more mildly
    (inedible winter algae seed an early bloom). The share that FALLS
    with the layer's nitrate keeps the spring (r(Z) +0.88) and stocks
    the late-summer subsurface maximum that the autumn deepening
    entrains. Column chlorophyll (t/km2 x 2, A17 obsCol 26/25/25 Jul-Sep,
    40 Oct, 34 Nov): base 12.8/17.7/19.7, 10.9, 5.2; e(N) 0.1/2
    24.2/28.2/29.0, 29.1, 9.4 - summer at A17, October 11 -> 29, not
    banked above the data. Herring year-mean 2.37 -> 2.59.

182.3 Biology and sign. The share falls at LOW nitrate, the opposite of
    the diatom size rule; it encodes the subsurface producer's
    late-summer community: in the stratified, nitrate-poor pycnocline
    layer Tripos/Ceratium dominate (Kattegat Aug-Sep, >50 um = 57-62 % of
    chl, Nielsen & Kioerboe 1994 [F]), ciliates take prey up to ~35 um
    (Hansen 1991 [F]); heterotrophic dinoflagellates take 6-9 %/d of
    Ceratium production and lag the bloom (Nielsen 1991 [F]) -> floor
    0.1, not 0. At winter nitrate (4-5 umol/l) e ~0.75. floor 0.1 and K
    2 umol/l are [D]. The micro's predation_mortality (146.7 rate ratio)
    is unchanged; the realised grazing falls below it in late summer.

182.4 Implemented (both engines). Pair keys edibility_floor and
    edibility_half_saturation_umol_l (together; K > 0, floor in [0,1]):
    the grazer perceives e B before the food threshold and Holling,
    e = floor + (1-floor) pool/(pool + half(t) K/k_N), pool the prey's
    nutrient pool before this pair grazes. Raises when the pools are on
    and the prey has none; inert without any pools (as Q10 and the
    mixed-layer scale without the calendar). interactions._edibility,
    ndm_grazing_rate(env, entry, prey_biomass, prey_pool),
    population_change.apply_ndm_grazing passes the pool; GPU
    ecosystem.ndm_grazing mirrors it. Library: microzooplankton_preys_on_
    subsurface_phytoplankton floor 0.1, K 2.0. AGENTS.md section 5.

    the gap, Nov-Dec still 4-6x short. (c) The gain rides on the summer

182.12 Second mixed-layer producer (the entrained Ceratium stock) -
    PARKED. Prototype: water_layer 'entrained', a pool-less mixed-layer
    stock that receives the entrained subsurface algae (b_md) and
    detrains with the small producer. Two findings: (a) the rule-driven
    world (rule:eat_pays) builds no late-summer subsurface stock (Aug-Oct
    ~2 t/km2 vs ~11 under trained policies), so the prototype tested
    nothing; (b) every DM's policy output has 5 + N_all columns and the
    groups sort alphabetically, so any new FG changes all five output
    heads (large_phytoplankton lands at index 2): checkpoints invalid,
    or surgery on every head. The CPU-only engine path was backed out
    (no unmirrored path); the scratch library/manifest stay in
    scratchpad aw/large/.

183 WINTER: WHAT A17 MEASURES, SPLIT M1, AND A Q10 ON ZOOPLANKTON GROWTH (2026-10-20)

183.1 Literature + SHARK (subagent, research_notes/Zooplankton
    vinterdodlighet/winter_stock.md). Every A17 zooplankton haul is a
    WP2 90 um net, 25 m -> surface, at a ~345 m station; carbon (2019-23)
    is computed (HELCOM C7 stage weights), wet weight never reported.
    Calanus + Metridia share of carbon Jan..Dec:
      0.82 0.75 0.64 0.89 0.77 0.35 0.48 0.67 0.78 0.30 0.23 0.23
    In Dec-Mar these are deep-water animals rising from the Norwegian
    Trench (a 30 m column cannot hold them); in Apr-May it is the new
    generation growing near the surface. Resident (all minus Calanus and
    Metridia), t WW/km2 at C/WW 0.084:
      0.21 0.18 1.56 2.12 6.10 7.40 3.59 1.50 0.79 2.03 2.66 0.92
    against the model's obs row (total) 1.2 0.7 4.3 19.3 26.0 11.4 6.9
    4.6 3.7 2.9 3.5 1.2. The flat total Dec->Jan is a composition
    change: resident carbon falls -0.052/d while Calanus rises. n = 2-4
    visits per month, 2-50x within a month. So the Feb-Mar 0.7/4.3 that
    ingestion_q10 2.8 was fitted to (181) is 64-75 % imported Calanus.
    Scratch scorer sc.py now also prints lZ(res): RMS log error against
    resident Dec-Mar + total Apr-Nov.

    5.4 C, Q10 ~3.0. The DM growth term g (s - u) has no temperature, so
    a full reserve in cold water grows as fast as in summer. Scratch,

183.5 Open decision (user): is the model's zooplankton the resident
    0-25 m community, or everything the herring eats including the
    imported Calanus? Under the resident target growth Q10 3.0 (literature
    value) with ingestion Q10 2.0 (the models' value) is the recommended
    pair; under the total target it undershoots April 3x and costs the
    herring a third. A Calanus import (seasonal advective source) would
    be the way to keep both.

183.6 Decision (user, 2026-10-20): resident target, growth_q10 3.0 on.
    - Target: the model's zooplankton is the resident 0-25 m community.
      Dec-Mar is compared with A17's resident stock (all minus Calanus
      and Metridia, C/WW 0.084): Dec 0.92, Jan 0.21, Feb 0.18, Mar 1.56
      t/km2. Apr-Nov keeps the A17 total, because the Apr-May Calanus is

      hybrid row is Jan-Dec 0.21 0.18 1.56 19.3 26.0 11.4 6.9 4.6 3.7
      2.9 3.5 0.92 (scratch l2/sc.py, lZ(res)). There is no repo tool
      with these targets.
    - Where the Calanus comes from: diapause C5 in the Norwegian Trench,
      entering with the deep Atlantic inflow (Falkenhaug et al. 2022;
      Kaartvedt et al. 2021 for C. helgolandicus at 80-150 m). A17 sits
      on the 345 m trench slope and gets them rising into 0-25 m in
      Jan-Mar. A ~100 m bank such as Mareld has no diapause habitat, so
      any supply there is lateral, and its size is unknown. Not modelled.
    - Library: zooplankton growth_q10 3.0 (Huntley & Lopez 1992, not
      fitted). ingestion_q10 stays 2.8; its comment now says it was

183.8 Why the herring falls in fix67 g1 (scratch hz/hloss.py: monthly
    herring budget per year after a burn-in year, probe year starts at
    day 147, so each block runs Jun -> May).
    - fix67 g1: Jun 2.98 -> Dec 2.97 (flat), then Jan-Apr down to 2.09
      (-30 %), May 2.24; next Jun 2.26, then 1.64. The loss is in the
      winter: herring rests 0.94-1.00 Nov-Feb and eats 0.00-0.36 %BW/d
      Dec-Feb (literature winter ration 0.4-1.0 %BW/d, Lohmeyer 1977,
      Bernreuther 2007), its reserve falls from s 0.69 (Oct) to 0.21
      (Feb), and it starves 0.07-0.09 %/d in Feb-Mar.
    - fix66 g8 (old library) bridged the winter on the early zooplankton:
      Feb-Mar ration 2.7-3.6 %BW/d, no starvation; the spring creep was
      feeding the herring. It also declines over years 2-4 (Jun 3.86 ->
      3.75 -> 3.16), with gadoids rising 0.76 -> 1.23.
    - Ingestion Q10 2.0 instead of 2.8 (fix67 g1 policies): herring year
      means 3.55 / 2.95 / 2.23 vs 3.53 / 2.81 / 2.04. Not the lever.
    - So the binding problem for the herring is the Oct-Dec zooplankton
      deficit (Nov 0.6 vs 3.5, Dec 0.26 vs 0.92 t/km2): with a realistic
      Feb-Mar spring, the herring has to bridge Nov-Apr on its reserve,
      and the autumn feeding that should fill it is missing. The autumn
      and herring problems are the same problem.

183.10 Herring winter budget (subagent, research_notes/Sillens
    vinterbudget/winter_budget.md) and a herring growth Q10 probe.
    - Literature/data: IBTS 2019-24 near the site, weight-at-length
      15-20 % lower in Jan-Feb than in August, energy-at-length -40-50 %;
      the site-population mean 12 % fat (Oct) -> 4 % (Feb) is plausible,
      but too steep for one adult (Norwegian spring spawners fasting lose
      ~2 fat-% Sep-Dec, Slotte 1996 [A]). No evidence of winter
      starvation of adult herring; juvenile Pacific herring die at ~1.3 %
      lipid (Sewall 2019); the model starts starving at ~3.5 % fat.
      Winter cost 7-14 kJ/kg/d vs the model's 16-24 (1.2-2x high).
      Adult WBSS overwinter in the Oresund / Koge Bay (Payne 2009); IBTS
      Q1 adults (3+) are ~0.2 of the August level, the winter stock
      ~90 % 1-2-year-olds. Fat bottoms in late May (4.5 %) and is 16 % by
      late June; the model refills from February.
    - The subagent's own budget: of the Jan-Apr loss only 8-15 % is
      starvation, 35-54 % is M1, the rest predation; 38 % of the Oct-Feb
      reserve drawdown is the growth term still turning fat into biomass
      (0.17-0.27 %/d Oct-Dec). Its ranking: (d) partial emigration,
      (b) winter cost, (c) starvation threshold, (a) autumn food; probe a
      seasonal growth brake first.
    - Herring growth_q10 (scratch, fix67 g1 policies), herring years 1/2:
        base 2.79/2.03; Q10 2.2 2.79/2.02; 3.0 2.70/1.92; 4.0 2.62/1.84
        with subsurface x 0.35: 3.36/2.51; +Q10 2.2 3.71/2.84; 3.0
        3.80/2.97; 4.0 3.92/3.10
      Wrong phase: the 0-50 m water peaks in Aug-Oct, so the Q10 moves
      herring growth INTO the autumn and brakes the spring; Feb-Mar
      starvation rises (0.18-0.23 %/d at 3.0). Temperature is not the
      herring's growth clock. Not adopted.
    - Net: no single lever stops the decline (20-27 %/yr in a 2-year
      probe). The two with the strongest support are the winter
      emigration of the adults (the site's winter stock is mostly
      juveniles) and a growth budget that knows the feeding season.

183.11 Season-aware herring growth budget (scratch hs/hseason.py on the
    section-183 growth table: HSEASON a-b -> herring growth branch
    g x 12/n inside months a..b, 0 outside, annual mean = the derived g;
    i.e. the budget r_max + M1 + M2 paid over the feeding season, which
    also stops the Oct-Dec fat -> biomass conversion). fix67 g1
    policies, 2 years after burn-in.

      base               2.79 2.03     2.62  2.77  1.79  1.73 0.61 0.25  0.80   0.91

    - The seasonal budget is the herring's main lever: the year-on-year
      fall drops from 27 % to 4-10 % and the mean doubles. May-Sep matches
      the literature feeding season (fat lowest late May, 16 % by late
      June, winter_budget.md). Oct-Dec growth is gone, the reserve is

      0.15-0.34 %/d in year 2 under the untrained policy).

      Apr 3.3), more than the 10-27 % weight-at-length swing in IBTS
      (the site's real amplitude comes mostly from the adults leaving,
      183.10); summer ration 3.2-3.5 %BW/d; the herring then eats the
      autumn zooplankton down (Oct-Dec 1.0/0.4/0.2), so the autumn stock
      (subsurface x 0.35) is needed with it; gadoids rise to 1.1-1.3.
    - Policies were trained without it; a trained herring would adapt.

184 GROWTH SEASON OF A DECISION MAKER (2026-10-20)

184.1 Why: 183.10-183.11. The derived growth_rate (section 160) assumes a
    DM can turn reserve into biomass every tick of the year. Herring at
    the site feeds May-Sep; the rest of the year the model's herring kept
    converting fat into biomass (Oct-Dec 0.17-0.27 %/d), entered winter
    lean and lost 25-30 %/yr. Paying the budget over the feeding season
    cut the fall to 4-10 %/yr in scratch (183.11).

184.2 Engine: ``growth_season_start`` / ``growth_season_end`` on a DM
    (calendar months 1-12, inclusive, start > end wraps; both or
    neither; 0 or empty = off). daylight.growth_season parses,
    daylight.season_multiplier gives the (T,) factor (0 outside, constant
    inside, annual mean 1 over the ticks). interactions.
    build_growth_season_tables (called after build_temperature_tables in
    state.py) folds it into env.growth_temp_table; with a growth_q10 the
    product is renormalised to mean 1. The growth branch is growth_rate x
    the table (population_change, unchanged code path); the starvation
    branch keeps the library rate. The GPU reads the same table (no
    GPU-side change beyond the error text). Refusals: non-DM (loader and
    env), no daylight calendar (env). FG editor fields + help. s* and the
    derived g are unchanged (annual mean).

184.3 Checks: tests/test_growth_season.py (18): parsing, the multiplier,
    no growth outside the season, raised rate inside, starvation
    unscaled, product with growth_q10, refusals.
    tests/test_gpu_ecosystem.py::test_growth_season_matches_reference
    (6; all fail when the GPU ignores the table). The engine with herring
    5-9 reproduces the scratch hook exactly (herring 5.478 / 5.009,
    zooplankton Sep-Dec 2.01 / 1.03 / 0.43 / 0.20). Full suite 1290
    passed, 12 skipped; 1-gen train.py smoke passed.

184.4 NOT set in the library. Open choice (user): which season (May-Sep
    fits the fat cycle but swings the herring +/- 50 %; Jun-Sep less),
    and whether to enable it before an autumn subsurface mechanism exists
    (with the season the herring eats the Oct-Dec zooplankton down to
    1.0 / 0.4 / 0.2, lZ(res) 0.80 -> 0.96). Enabling it needs a new run.

184.5 Is a calendar the right driver? (user: growth should emerge from
    biology, not an external calendar). Subagent, research_notes/Sillens
    vinterbudget/growth_allocation.md:
    - Seasonal somatic growth is established: NSS herring grow 1 Apr -
      15 Sep (Bachiller 2018 [F]); North Sea herring soma peaks May-Jun
      before gonads Jul-Sep (Iles 1964); DATRAS at the site: 65-93 % of
      the yearly length gain of 2-3-ringers between Jan-Feb and August.
    - Driver: falling food plus maintenance explains the stop; salmonid
      lab work shows allocation or an endogenous rhythm can stop growth
      with food in excess (Metcalfe & Thorpe 1992; Saether 1996); for
      herring only indirect evidence (Sewall 2019 juveniles switch to
      storage in November; Schmidt 2022 photoperiod times oocytes).
      Temperature is not the switch.
    - My citations from memory: Hurst 2007, Post & Parkinson 2001, Boeuf
      & Le Bail 1999 exist and say roughly that; Iles 1984 exists (book
      chapter, unread).
    - Models: Wisconsin bioenergetics (incl. herring), Broekhuizen-type
      reserve/structure models and DEBlipid (Martin et al. 2017) fund
      structure from this step's income; standard DEB grows on the
      reserve like Mareld, which DEB-Storage (Ortiz Duran et al. 2026,
      Ecol Model) was written to fix.
    - Ranked rules: A) kappa split of this tick's income, G = max(0,
      kappa I - C), the rest to the reserve, kappa derived per group
      (~0.75 for herring, s* unchanged 0.857), estimated Feb s 0.39 vs
      0.21; C) today's law braked to I >= C; B) a reserve target raised
      by shortening days (salmonid evidence only). Recommendation: one
      code path for all DMs, kappa per group, herring first.
    So growth_season (184.2) is a phenomenological stand-in; rule A is
    the mechanistic candidate. Not tested yet.

184.6 Rule A in scratch (hs/kappa.py: per cell G = max(0, kappa I - C), I
    this tick's assimilated intake, C its action costs, G leaves the
    eaters' reserve as G / energy_content new tonnes before movement;
    the reserve-funded branch off for herring, starvation unchanged).
    fix67 g1 policies, 2 years after burn-in, kappa 0.75 unless noted.
      variant                     herring y1/y2  Jun   Sep   Apr   Z Oct/Nov/Dec  lZ(res) starv Feb-Mar  s Feb
      base (today's law)           2.79 2.03     2.62  2.77  1.79  1.73 0.61 0.25  0.80   0.07-0.09     0.21
      calendar 5-9 (184.2)         5.48 5.01     4.60  7.11  3.25  1.03 0.43 0.20  0.96   0.15-0.34     0.19
      A, no ceiling                5.29 5.57     18.6  5.83  0.18  boom-bust: 0.2 -> 19 t/km2 Mar-Jun, s ~0 Jul-Feb
      A, ceiling B g (s-u)         1.42 0.73     1.57  1.27  0.74  2.02 0.66 0.24  0.79   0             0.54
      A, ceiling 2 g (1-u)         7.15 5.58     5.79  8.39  3.72  0.92 0.35 0.15  1.12   0.03-0.27     0.21
      A, ceiling B 2.18 g (s-u)    4.57 4.14     4.46  5.52  3.04  1.35 0.50 0.25  0.87   0             0.34

    - Income-funded growth needs a growth ceiling: without one, a few
      herring meeting the spring zooplankton grow 90x in three months
      and starve all winter (no reserve ever filled).
    - With today's g (s-u) as the ceiling the mechanism does what the
      literature says: growth stops when the food stops, the fat is
      kept (s 0.54 in Feb), no starvation. But the herring collapses:
      the derived g is sized for growth all year (section 160).
    - g sized for a 5.5-month feeding season (Apr - mid-Sep, Bachiller
      2018; x 12/5.5 = 2.18): -9 %/yr, no starvation at all, Feb s 0.34
      (~6 % fat, between the population mean 4 % and a fasting adult),
      autumn zooplankton less grazed than with the calendar. Same order
      of effect as the calendar, but the switch now comes from the food;
      the calendar survives only as a stated biological parameter of
      the budget (the length of the feeding season), not as a switch.
    - Left: ~10 %/yr decline and a +/- 50 % annual herring amplitude
      (M1 + predation ~0.35-0.45 %/d all year; gadoids rise to 1.2-1.3).

184.7 Income-funded growth in the engine (rule A with the reserve-state
    ceiling, 184.6). 184.2-184.4 (growth_season) are SUPERSEDED: the
    calendar switch is removed from both engines, the FG editor, the
    tests and AGENTS.md; the months now only size the budget.
    - Library keys on a DM: ``income_growth_kappa`` kappa (0 / empty =
      the reserve-funded law), ``feeding_season_months`` n (default 12,
      needs kappa). growth_budget.income_growth parses;
      growth_budget pays g over the season (x 12/n on growth_rate and
      per_tick; s* unchanged at the annual-mean production; the
      mass-balance ceiling checked on the season-sized g; the FG
      editor's formula shows "x 12/n", hover help growth:season).
    - Tick: movement.apply_energy_costs -> movement.income_growth, per
      cell G = min(max(0, kappa I - C), B g (s - u) ec, stationary
      reserve), I = temp_energy_gains, C = rest + eat + move cost of the
      tick (the arrays the function already had; rest_cost factored out
      with the same arithmetic order), s at the start of the tick; G
      leaves the stationary reserve and becomes G / ec tonnes before the
      movement. population_change zeroes the DM's growth branch
      (starvation unchanged). GPU: TensorEcosystem.income_growth at the
      rest + eat stage of movement(), income_off_growth mask in
      population(). Default path bit-identical (only the factoring).
    - Refusals (loader and env): non-DM; growth_q10 on the same DM; no
      starve_rate (the fallback would starve at the season-sized g).
    - Checks: tests/test_income_growth.py (parsing, budget x 12/5.5 with
      s* unchanged, the per-cell formula incl. no intake -> no growth on
      a full reserve, the settling-reserve clamp, population step,

      test_income_growth_matches_reference (8; all fail with the GPU

    - Also refused: feeding_season_months on a group without r_max (a

    - Full suite 1287 passed, 12 skipped; 1-gen train.py smoke passed
      (library unchanged, so it exercises the default path only).

    the issue. The gadoids grow near r_max - F until they have eaten
    the herring down and then crash by starvation: a predator-prey
    overshoot, regulated by food only. Open: is that cycle real (no
    data for it here) or should something else hold the gadoids near
    today's level (higher F incl. the fishing outside the grid, a
    lower r_max for a stock near capacity, density dependence)?

184.14 Literature on what regulates the gadoids (subagent, notes in
    research_notes/Torskfiskarnas reglering/: stock_trends_and_mortality,
    r_max_and_recruitment, density_dependence, predator_prey_cycles,
    recommendation).
    - r_max 0.511 is the CMSY/Schaefer r; the model kept r and dropped
      K, so at ideal food the pool grows at r_max - F ~ 0.39/yr at any
      density (184.13 measured +0.35).
    - Stocks: the pool was roughly stationary in 2010-2020 at F
      0.23-0.30, then doubled in 2020-23 from two haddock year classes,
      and has fallen ~3 %/yr since. Cod is depleted, saithe below Blim,
      hake down ~60 %. F 0.12 is right for today's haddock-heavy mix,
      0.17-0.20 for a long-term mix.
    - r today is probably 0.35-0.45 (lower recruits per spawner and
      warming; the subagent's estimate, not a published value).
    - Density dependence is mainly stock-recruit compensation (68-78 %
      of NE Atlantic stocks) plus cannibalism (~0.08/yr at B_ref).
    - No gadoid-herring overshoot cycle is documented. SMS gadoid M2 on
      herring is 0.15/yr (0.11-0.22, no trend; 60 % saithe) against
      0.5-1.2 in the model; herring is ~5 % of the SMS gadoid ration
      against 40-52 % in the model (184.13 diet confirms 40-52 %).
    - Ranking: (c) a regional logistic closure L = r_max/1460 *
      B_region/K, kept OUT of the derived g, K = B_ref/(1 - F/r_max)
      = 0.90 t/km2 at r 0.511, F 0.12 (0.8-1.0); then (b) r_max 0.40;
      (a) F 0.17-0.20; (d) cannibalism (~20 % of the gap, only if left
      out of g); (e) "recovering" is least supported. Plus (f): the
      herring share of the gadoid diet as a calibration target.
    - Caveat: the model's 0.69 t/km2 is ~4x below the IBTS density
      (2.7-3.3), which would scale K by about 4.
    Nothing implemented.

184.18 Biomass-weighted present-day r for the gadoid pool (note:
    research_notes/Torskfiskarnas reglering/r_pool_present.md).
    Method: per-species CMSY prior r_max x Euler-Lotka, r_now = r_max -
    ln(d)/T, with d = the R/SSB decline from ICES SAG (cod 2.6, haddock
    4.7 [2.7-8.3], hake 3.9, saithe 1.6, whiting 1) and T = 3/r (Froese
    et al. 2017). Per species: cod 0.35 (0.26 with Myers' T 3.9),
    haddock 0.24, whiting 0.49, saithe 0.44, hake 0.26.
    Pool: 0.34 (today's survey weights, haddock-heavy), 0.38 (box
    weights), 0.40 (Ecopath 1991 mix); range 0.29-0.42, and ~0.05-0.08
    lower with shorter generation times.
    The 0.20 of 184.17 (0.51/2.5) was too low: a recruitment decline
    lowers r by ln(d)/T, not by the factor d. At r ~0.37 and F 0.12 the
    pool still grows ~+0.2/yr at ideal food, so the lower r closes about
    half of the surplus. The rest needs density dependence at today's
    effective capacity (habitat loss and warming lower it below the
    historical ceiling).

185 REGIONAL CARRYING CAPACITY AND PRESENT-DAY r FOR THE GADOIDS
    (2026-10-21)
185.1 Why: 184.13-184.19. The derived g pays r_max at any density, so
    the gadoid pool grew at r_max - F, ate the pelagic pool down and
    crashed. The user's points: today's stock is depleted by decades of
    overfishing and trawled nurseries, so neither today's level nor
    2010-19 is the ceiling, and the historical stock was much larger.
    Resolution: r_max is today's low-density productivity (lower than
    the 1960s-90s priors, 184.18), and K is today's EFFECTIVE capacity
    (lowered by habitat loss and warming), separate from the historical
    ceiling.
185.2 Engine. New library key ``regional_carrying_capacity`` K (t/km2,
    DMs with r_max only):
    - growth_budget.regional_capacity / capacity_loss_rate give
      c = r_max / (1460 K); the loader (both paths) derives
      params['capacity_loss_rate'], rescaled as a "flux" (tick_time).
    - state._build_regional_capacity sets env.dm_capacity_rate and
      env._has_regional_capacity.
    - population_change: after M1, keep = 1 - c * sum(B)/n_cells,
      applied to biomass and reserve and booked in loss_natural.
      Applied with or without --mortality (it closes r_max, which g
      always pays); not scaled by --mortality_multiplier.
    - GPU mirror in TensorEcosystem.population (capacity_rate [1, G, 1],
      b.mean over cells).
    - Not in the derived g; describe() is unchanged.
    - Refusals: a non-DM (loader and env), K without r_max, c outside
      [0, 1].
185.3 Library (gadoids): r_max 0.511 -> 0.37; regional_carrying_capacity
    1.02 (= 0.69/(1 - 0.12/0.37)); stored growth_rate 0.00357051 ->
    0.00294180 (derived).

185.9 Trawling, nursery habitat and K (subagent; notes in
    research_notes/ folder "Tralning och uppvaxtomraden" (Swedish
    letters in the real name): mechanism_evidence, quantitative_links,
    nursery_areas, benthic_recovery_and_wind_farms, recommendation).
    - The form K(H) = f + gH exists (Foley et al. 2012; Atlantis habitat
      scaling of recruitment). No published function links SAR or effort
      to gadoid juvenile survival, recruitment or K; RBS = 1 - SAR d/r is
      quantified for the benthos only.
    - Shelter effects are shown for 0-group cod on shallow cobble,
      sponge, eelgrass and maerl; nothing links mud epifauna to juvenile
      gadoids. The food pathway is already in the model (gadoids eat
      benthic_community, which trawling depletes per cell), so a K(H) on
      top would count it twice.
    - Nurseries: cod, whiting and saithe are coastal; Skagerrak haddock
      0-1 group at 150-300 m (Albert 1991, 1984-87). Sites per the EIAs:
      Mareld 180-450 m, Poseidon Nord 55-230 m, soft bottom, FLOATING
      turbines; parks 521 km2 = 14.5 % of the grid and 27 % of its trawl
      effort. The grid's share of regional juvenile habitat is ~0.3-0.6 %
      (the subagent's inference).
    - Recovery: mud benthos 4-6 yr; OWEZ showed no benthic difference
      after 5 yr (Bergman et al. 2015); the Kattegat no-take zone doubled
      Nephrops but not cod (Skold et al. 2022). Turbine reef effects are
      attraction at fixed foundations and do not apply to floating
      turbines (Hywind Tampen: no fish effect).
    - Effect of the parks on K: +0.03-0.1 % central, ~0.3 % upper bound;
      ~0 if the effort is displaced within the grid.
    - Verdict: leave the K(H) coupling out of the baseline; at most a
      sensitivity case (recommendation.md: depth-weighted, read from the
      model's benthos, s_pool 0.004).
    - Larger caveat: closing the parks lowers the grid gadoid F from 0.12
      to ~0.088, which with the regional K raises the equilibrium B by
      ~13 % - but the real stock F barely changes for a closure this
      size. The same grid-versus-stock scale problem applies; the projekt
      effort map must state whether the parks' effort is removed or
      displaced.

185.14 Seals still eat no pelagic fish after the 2e-4 change (user). The
    run (train_gpu --resume, pid 588605, started 12:42 with the 2e-4
    library) is at gen 13. Measured on its 16:08 policies, seed 20260530,
    one burn-in year, then 0.5-1 year:
    - trained seals: 393.7 t gadoids, 0.03 t pelagic (0.0 %);
    - greedy seals (install_mixed) at 2e-4 on the same fields: 88 %
      pelagic by mass (243 t vs 33 t), seals stable at 17 t;
    - the trained seal policy puts 0.03 % of its eat mass on pelagic_fish
      and 99 % on gadoids, while standing on above-average pelagic
      density (8.6 vs 6.8 t/cell grid mean; gadoids 0.77 vs 0.65).

    observe pelagic_fish and have it in their menu. The pelagic eat
    logit is saturated (~-8 relative to gadoids) since the a cut of

185.15 How to reset the seals' pelagic eat channel (dry run on a copy of
    the 16:08 policies, $S/f68r/reset; script $S/seal/reset_eat.py). The
    policy output is 5 + N_all logits (move 4, rest, then eat per prey in
    env.global_fg_order: benthic_community, gadoids, microzooplankton,
    pelagic_fish, ...). Copying the gadoid row (output index 6) of
    net.2 into the pelagic row (8), with bias - 2.2, makes the pelagic
    share start at e^-2.2 ~ 0.11 of the gadoid share in every cell. The
    old pelagic bias was -0.54 vs 0.78, so the suppression sat in the
    weights. Result: eat share 9.6 % pelagic / 89.7 % gadoids (was
    0.03 / 99); diet 7.8 t pelagic of 380 t (2.0 % by mass, 2.9 % of
    energy), seals 16.2 t. Training needs --init-from into a new run
    directory: train_gpu refuses --init-from where policies exist, and
    --resume would reload the old theta from trainer.pth. obs_stats
    travel with the policy files.
185.16 fix69 (--init-from the reset policies, $S/f69_init) still gives
    the seals no pelagic fish (user). Cause: eat intake is
    B_seal * share_j * f_j(B_j) per prey with no shared handling, so
    the return is linear in the share and the optimum puts the whole
    eat mass on the best prey of the cell. Where the f69_init seals
    stand (2 years, seal-biomass weighted) gadoids give 139 and the
    pelagic pool 54 MJ per t seal, tick and unit share; the pool pays

    2e-4 of 185.10 was fitted to the water-filling greedy arm, which
    mixes prey the way an optimiser never does.

      0.66 0.66 0.68 / 0.66 0.62 0.58. Pelagic Jan 2.28 / 2.30 / 2.34
      (seed 7 2.17 / 2.26 / 2.35): stationary, +1-2 %/yr vs +15-25.
    - Herring<-zoo 78 / 71 / 71 kt/yr (base 105-150): ~3.6x the
      zooplankton standing stock per year (base 14x, Ecopath 1.9x).
      Zmean 5.56, Zmax 18.1 (base 3.22, 10.4; fix68 g3 18.7).
    - The pool settles at ~2.75, below today's 3.33 and below
      K(1 - F/r) = 3.5: ~0.05/yr more loss than the budget assumes
      (not traced). Gadoids fall ~9 %/yr: less pelagic in the ration
      (0.3 vs 0.8 %BW/d), more benthos (1.5 vs 0.7) - food or a
      policy trained in a herring-rich world, not separated.
    - Do not tune K (~6 would give 3.33) on policies trained without
      it; retrain first. Nothing applied.
185.20 APPLIED (user): pelagic_fish r_max 0.648 -> 0.34 and
    regional_carrying_capacity 5.0 t/km2 (185.18-19). Loader-derived
    growth_rate 0.00350461 -> 0.00275637 (mareld2, --mortality on),
    capacity_loss_rate 4.6575e-5. Why K and not only the lower r: the
    derived g pays r_max at any density, so without K the pool grows
    at r - F until food stops it, and in the closed grid that means
    grazing the zooplankton down (the literature finds no herring
    top-down control and weight-at-age barely density dependent). K
    stands in for stock-scale compensation (density-dependent
    recruitment; the r_max prior is itself a Schaefer r with a K) and
    net emigration; a seasonal immigration/emigration term would be
    the mechanistic version (engine code, not done). Checkpoints stay
    valid (no observation change) but were trained without it:
    retrain before judging the equilibrium (2.75 vs 3.33 on fix69)
    or the gadoid decline. tests/test_regional_capacity.py now
    expects gadoids and pelagic_fish to carry the loss.

187 GADOID RESERVE AS FOOD: LITERATURE AND A SCRATCH PROBE (2026-10-22)
187.1 Question (user): why does only pelagic_fish carry
    prey_includes_reserve? Answer: the flag came with the herring
    lean/reserve split of section 140 (it keeps the predators' herring
    quality at 7500 MJ/t once the fat became a reserve). Zooplankton
    and gadoids keep a whole-body energy_content with the reserve on
    top, so an eaten gadoid's reserve (~1750 MJ/t at s 0.7, ~30 % of
    energy_content) leaves the system unpaid; zooplankton ~7 %.
187.2 Literature (subagent; research_notes/ folder "Torskfiskars
    energiinnehall" with the Swedish a-ring, energy_density.md, 31
    sources): lean body 3850 MJ/t (3700-4000; whiting 3.9, hake 3.7
    kJ/g whole body, Spitz 2010 [F]; cod ~3.8 [S]; haddock and saithe
    ASSUMED from fillet tables), weighted by today's survey mix (haddock
    0.54, whiting 0.27, saithe 0.12, cod 0.06, hake 0.01); liver reserve
    ME 2000 MJ/t (1650-2100; cod autumn HSI 4.3-5.7 % x ~29 kJ/g);
    reference fill 0.45 -> 4750 MJ/t = mean whole body; maintenance u
    0.1 (death at fill 0.02-0.035, wild spring minimum ~0.2 survived).
    The library's 5500 equals the autumn maximum (5515), +16 % on the
    annual mean; whole-body gadoid energy swings ~1.3x over the year
    (herring ~2x). Haddock (54 % of the pool) has no wild liver or
    whole-body series; the reserve and u are the cod cycle as a proxy.
187.3 Probe (scratchpad gres/probe.py: train._ProbeEnvBuilder with a
    library copy, predation patched in memory to book the assimilated
    energy per pair exactly; frozen copy of the fix70 policies of
    2026-10-22 00:23, gen 1 / 69 updates, md5 gadoids b834b11d; seeds
    20260530 and 7, 3 years; live library untouched while fix70 trains
    with --visual). Variants: base; flagonly (prey_includes_reserve on,
    ec 5500 kept, fill 0.5 = fat counted twice, static 6750);
    split_u05 (ec 3850, ME 2000, fill 0.45, u 0.5); split_u01 (same,
    u 0.1). Year 3 mean, seed 20260530 / seed 7:
      variant    gadoids t/km2  pelagic  seals t      porpoises t  seal MJ/t gadoid
      base       0.455 / 0.412  1.69/1.39  7.5 / 5.3   0.74 / 0.02  4675
      flagonly   0.439 / 0.392  1.66/1.38  14.5 / 11.0 3.57 / 0.55  ~6050
      split_u05  0.479 / 0.445  1.76/1.42  7.8 / 3.9   0.84 / 0.02  ~4450
      split_u01  0.411 / 0.387  2.21/1.89  3.9 / 1.1   1.52 / 0.17  ~3950
    Gadoid derived g: base 0.00294, split_u05 0.00266 (s* 0.747),
    split_u01 0.00145 (s* 0.553, gate 0.45).
187.4 Reading:
    - The baseline itself is not viable on these early fix70 policies:
      porpoises collapse (10.9 -> 0.7 t, 6.8 -> 0.02 t), seals halve
      with starvation 0.24-0.6 /yr, gadoids -25-30 %, the pelagic pool
      falls to 1.4-1.7 t/km2 (equilibrium K(1-F/r) 3.5). That
      dominates every reserve variant; re-read on later generations.
    - The top predators are food-quality limited: +23 % gadoid quality
      (flagonly) keeps the seals (starvation 0.24 -> 0.06-0.08 /yr) and
      slows the porpoises. But flagonly is not a biology option (double
      count).
    - The literature split at u 0.5 is close to neutral: the realised
      reserve fill stays 0.62-0.75 all year, so predators get ~4450
      MJ/t (-5 % vs 4675 today), seals a little worse, gadoids a little
      better (cheaper biomass). The seasonal swing the model produces
      is ~5 %, against ~1.3x whole-body in nature: the gadoid policy
      keeps the reserve near full, so a fat-autumn/lean-spring prey
      quality does not emerge.
    - u 0.1 is not adoptable as a parameter change: in this engine u is
      also the knee of the hunger gate and the zero of the growth gate,
      so lowering it cuts gadoid appetite (fill falls to 0.25-0.53),
      halves the derived g and starves the seals (realised quality
      ~3950). The literature u is a starvation threshold; decoupling it
      from the hunger knee is a structural question (and the policies
      were trained at u 0.5).
187.5 Nothing applied; library, engine and tests untouched. Options for
    the user: (a) leave as is (5500 whole body, reserve lost when
    eaten; simple, ~16 % generous on quality); (b) split_u05 (lean
    3850 + liver 2000, fill 0.45, prey_includes_reserve): mass and
    energy consistent, ~neutral for the food web, needs a retrain and
    a re-read of the seal/porpoise diets; (c) a separate starvation
    threshold from the hunger knee before any u change.

    layout is no longer fixed in __init__ but derived by
    _compute_layout() from the window size and _split_frac, the

189 Viewer memory leak: band labels rendered but never blitted (2026-10-23)
================================================================
189.1 Symptom (user): after a 50-year inference rollout with --visual
    (with or without --no-capture), scrolling, zooming and switching
    plot tabs made RSS climb until the box ran out of memory.
189.2 Repro: headless (SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy) LiveVisualizer with 9
    FGs x 9 tabs x 73000 ticks, _render_full() in a loop. Random zoom
    + scroll + tabs: +650 MB over 3000 frames, linear (~0.25 MB per
    frame). Bisected: tabs alone and scroll alone flat, zoom alone
    leaks; with _draw_calendar_band or _blit_block_label stubbed out
    the leak is gone.
189.3 Mechanism: the section-60 antipattern again, in code written
    after it (section 155). In this environment (pygame 2.6.1, SDL
    2.32.56 = sdl2-compat over SDL3 - conda-forge sdl2 2.32.56 plus
    sdl3 3.4.2 in eco-evo-mixed - SDL_ttf 2.24) an antialiased
    font.render() surface that is never blitted (or locked) leaks
    its whole pixel buffer when it is freed: 200k renders of short
    strings = +215 MB unblitted, +0.4 MB when each is blitted - even
    a blit fully outside the clip rect, or lock()/unlock(), frees it.
    Non-antialiased render() does not leak. _blit_block_label rendered
    each label variant ("January", "Jan", "J") to measure it and threw
    away the ones that did not fit; zoomed out over 50 years every
    month and clock block is a pixel or two wide, so every variant of
    every block was rendered and dropped, every frame, and
    wait_for_close re-renders at ~20 fps even when idle.
189.4 Fix (lib/viz/pygame_viz.py): _blit_block_label measures with
    font.size() and returns early when even the shortest variant does
    not fit; only the label drawn (and its shadow) is rendered. The
    spawn dropdown truncation in _draw_one_heatmap had the same
    pattern (render, measure, re-render shorter) and now measures
    with font.size() and renders once. All other render() call sites
    were checked: each blits what it renders.
    Rule: never render text you will not blit - measure with
    font.size().
189.5 Result: same repro, 5000 random zoom/scroll/tab frames +12 MB
    and plateauing (glibc/numpy churn); zoomed-out idle flat over
    2000 frames. Test: tests/test_viz_calendar_band.py::
    test_every_rendered_text_is_blitted (a Surface subclass as screen
    records blits, a spy font records renders; 50-year rollout at
    three zooms) - fails on the old code, passes now. pytest 1330
    passed; 1-generation train.py smoke run OK.

193 Folded splitter drag: guide line, one resize on release (2026-10-23)
================================================================
193.1 Symptom (user): dragging the grip on the folded strip (192)
    made the window flicker, jump and stop responding. Cause: every
    MOUSEMOTION called display.set_mode with a new width. On X11 the
    window manager resizes asynchronously and may move the window,
    so event x shifted under the mouse, the next width was computed
    from a moved origin, and the drag fed back on itself; each
    set_mode also re-created the surface.
193.2 Fix (lib/viz/pygame_viz.py): while the folded splitter is
    dragged the window is not touched. _fold_drag_w holds the target
    heatmap width (clamped to [_min_hm_area_w, desktop - strip]) and
    _draw_fold_drag_guide draws a vertical guide line with the
    resulting window width ("N px"; clamped to the window edge when
    the target lies beyond it). The release (_end_fold_drag) resizes
    the window ONCE, straight to the snug width for that target
    (_snug_hm_area_w, via the column rule factored out of
    _compute_layout as _heatmap_columns). A motion event whose
    buttons say the left button is up ends the drag (a release
    outside the window can be missed); WINDOWFOCUSLOST cancels it.
    Unfolding after such a drag behaves as in 192.2. The expanded
    splitter is unchanged (live relayout inside a fixed window).
193.3 Checks: tests/test_viz_heatmap_scroll.py - no window resize
    during 21 motion events, exactly one on release, snug result,
    unfold beside the new heatmaps; a drag ended by a button-up
    motion and one cancelled by focus loss. On the real X11 display
    (DISPLAY :1, events posted into pump_events, the user's mouse not

    events at all, unfold to 1342 px. pytest 1338 passed;

194 Plot fold as a calm roll; no window re-creation (2026-10-23)
================================================================
194.1 Complaint (user): folding/unfolding blinked, the window
    "jumped", and the fold button moved away from the pointer that
    had just clicked it. Wanted: the plot area rolls out and in
    calmly.
194.2 Measured on the real X11 display (DISPLAY :1, events posted,
    the user's mouse not moved; probes in the session scratchpad):
    * pygame.display.set_mode on an open window DESTROYS AND
      RE-CREATES it here (pygame 2.6.1 / sdl2-compat): a new X
      window id on every call, ~120 ms each. That was the blink of
      sections 190-193 (one set_mode per toggle; 193 per drag
      motion).
    * SDL_SetWindowSize (pygame._sdl2.video.Window.size) resizes the
      same window in ~10-20 ms, origin unchanged.
    * The viewer opens near screen size with 9 FGs (1920x1136) and
      the window manager MAXIMISES it by itself (_NET_WM_STATE
      MAXIMIZED_HORZ/VERT). A maximised window ignores
      SetWindowSize; restore() alone moves it to its remembered
      geometry (114,100 1717x1117) - a jump. restore() immediately
      followed by position = old origin and size = target gives the
      target geometry with no intermediate one.
    * The button moved because 190's fold snugged the heatmap area
      around the panels (removing up to one cell step of slack per
      column), which moved the splitter.
194.3 Implementation (lib/viz/pygame_viz.py):
    * _set_window_width(width, render=True): SDL_SetWindowSize on
      the same window; if the size does not take (maximised),
      restore + old origin + size in one go, pumping up to 0.3 s for
      the surface; display.set_mode only as the fallback. Re-runs the
      layout and paints the frame immediately (no unpainted surface
      reaches the screen).
    * The heatmap area is pinned (_hm_area_fixed) for the fold and
      the folded state: the splitter, and the fold button under the
      pointer, never move. No snugging any more - the folded window
      is the area as arranged plus the 16 px strip (floor 600 px),
      so up to one cell step of slack per column can remain right of
      the panels. _compute_layout honours the pin; unfolding returns
      to the splitter share at exactly the pinned position (kept
      pinned only if the screen leaves the plot under its minimum
      width, until the splitter is dragged).
    * _roll_window(w0, w1): time-based glide of the right edge,

196 Plot y-axis labels in plain decimals (2026-10-23)
================================================================
196.1 Request (user): no scientific notation on the plot's y axis
    (".3g" printed 1.23e+04 from 10000 up) and no plus sign.
196.2 Implementation (lib/viz/pygame_viz.py): _axis_labels(values,
    step) - one number of decimals per axis, three significant
    digits of the label step (2 - floor(log10(step)), capped at 12),
    then the trailing zeros all five labels share are dropped; "-0"
    prints as "0". Examples: 0..60000 -> 60000 45000 ... 0;
    0..1 -> 1.00 0.75 ... 0.00; -50.7..29.8 -> 29.8 9.7 -10.4
    -30.6 -50.7; 0..0.0012 -> 0.0012 ... 0.0000. _draw_plot builds
    the labels first and widens plot_pad_l (default 36 px) to the
    widest label + 6 px, so "345000" does not run into the plot
    (px0 / pw are not used before that point). Applies to every tab,
    train and inference. The hover tooltip followed (196.4).
196.3 Tests: tests/test_viz_axis_labels.py (fixed examples; never
    "e" or a leading "+", five distinct labels, over ranges from 1e-6
    to 1e7; a rendered predation tab at 100000-345000 draws exactly
    the five plain labels and a margin wider than 36 px). Headless
    screenshot checked. pytest 1350 passed; 1-generation train.py
    smoke run OK.
196.4 Tooltip (user): the hover tooltip values use _axis_labels too,
    with the axis step, so they carry the axis's decimals and read
    against its labels (123456, 54322 on a 50000-130000 axis;
    -0.00042 on 0..-0.0012). On a log-scaled axis (labels in log10,
    values raw) the step is a tenth of the largest value's decade:
    three significant digits of the largest value. No "e", no "+".
    Tests in tests/test_viz_axis_labels.py (linear and log, small
    negative values). pytest 1353 passed; smoke run OK.

200 WORLD WARM-UP BEFORE THE SCORED ROLLOUT; LOG-UNIFORM START TOTALS (2026-10-23)
================================================================
200.1 Why (user, after a review of the training start ranges): the
    start totals ignore the season. Phytoplankton 11-28 t/km2 against the
    model's own 0.05 (summer) to 14 (February peak); zooplankton 4.9-19.4
    against 0.6 in January and 20 in April. Both 3-year inference seeds
    (early-summer starts) grazed the phytoplankton down within a week
    and gave the zooplankton a pulse (10 -> 24 t/km2 in 7 days vs 13 on
    the same date a year later); a winter start puts the zooplankton
    8-30x over its winter stock (the eval's survival_ticks 52, the
    zooplankton reward -1.4). One to two months of every 1-year episode
    were the world settling. The linear draw on [x/2, 2x] also had mean
    1.25x and put two thirds of the worlds above x.
    Ranges judged otherwise reasonable: gadoids 0.35-1.39 t/km2, pelagic
    1.7-6.7, seals 5-30 t (K 15), subsurface phytoplankton, micro- and
    benthos. Porpoises 6-18 t lie wholly below SCANS-IV's lower 95 %
    bound (33 t; central ~84 t, section 199.3) - left until the porpoise
    food calibration.
200.2 Warm-up (lib/runners/warmup.py; flag --warmup-days D on train.py
    and train_gpu.py, default 0 = off, converted with the run's tick
    length). Each world first runs D days with the UNPERTURBED policies
    (the current theta), and every candidate on that world starts its
    scored rollout from the state that reaches. Shared, not per
    candidate: the +/- candidates keep a common start (CRN, section
    150), and nothing a candidate does goes unscored (a per-candidate
    warm-up would forgive its own losses through the new baseline e0).
    The calendar runs on: the scored rollout starts D days after the
    sampled start day (still uniform over the year with
    start_day_of_year: random).
    - GPU (lib/gpu/trainer.py): a second RolloutRunner with one weight
      set over the worlds (warm_runner; no reward variant), run in
      train_step after refresh_worlds, every update (theta changes).
      Its keys are the world keys folded with 70001; reserves and
      nutrient pools are initialised as before at the sampled start;
      biomass, reserve and the last hide fractions carry over
      (RolloutRunner.reset(hidden=...)); world_scored_light = start + D
      ticks mod the year. Warm-up observations are not merged into the
      normalisation statistics. With a warm-up the per-pair reserve draw
      (spawn randomize_energy on pair keys) no longer applies: every
      candidate starts from its world's warm reserve. mean_biomass,
      reward and sigma_f in training.jsonl come from the scored rollout
      only.
    - CPU (lib/runners/trainer.py, parallel_worker.py): inside every
      co-evolution rollout task the env runs D days with the base
      weights, then the candidate's weights are set and the reward
      starts. The CPU tick draws its FG order and the seeding noise from
      the global np.random, which is not re-seeded per task (worker
      histories differ; this already made the +/- scored rollouts differ
      in that noise before section 200). run_warmup therefore runs on a
      stream seeded from the pair seed and restores the global state
      afterwards: the +/- tasks reach the same warm state on any worker,
      and the scored rollout draws as before. run_warmup clears the
      observation and
      action-statistic accumulators; --local_reward is attached after
      the warm-up. The legacy tuple-task path is skipped when a warm-up
      is on. The round-robin path (--no_coevolution) refuses it.
    - Cost: 240 ticks (60 days) on the GPU take ~1.7 s per update
      (measured with fix71 running alongside), against 110-280 s per
      update: ~1 %. On the CPU trainer every task repeats the warm-up
      (+D/n_eval_ticks, ~16 % at 60 of 365 days).
    - Example (one world, fix71_init policies, 60 days): phytoplankton
      13.1 -> 1.9 t/km2, zooplankton 10.9 -> 0.21 (a winter start),
      subsurface phytoplankton 11.7 -> 0.6, microzooplankton 0.42 ->
      0.17; gadoids 0.49 -> 0.44, pelagic 3.23 -> 2.81.
200.3 Log-uniform start totals (lib/config/config_loader.
    _sample_total_biomass, lib/gpu/spawn.WorldSpawner.biomass): exp of a
    uniform draw between log(min) and log(max), rounded to whole tonnes
    and clamped to the range, so [x/2, 2x] has median x. A non-positive
    lower bound keeps the uniform integer draw. No flag; inference
    starts (inference_initial_biomass) are unchanged.
200.4 Not changed: the survival evaluation and the --visual CPU probe
    still start from the inference biomasses with no warm-up (they
    describe an inference run from today's state), so their zooplankton
    numbers keep the start transient.
200.5 Tests: tests/test_warmup.py (12: day->tick conversion and
    refusals; run_warmup clears the accumulators and, seeded, restores
    the global stream; on a 6x6 mareld2 env two RNG histories give two
    warm states unseeded and one seeded; CPU sequential and worker paths
    reach the same warm state for two different candidate weights and
    RNG histories and restore the candidate's weights; round-robin
    refuses;
    GPU candidates start from the warm state (b0) and the warm state is
    independent of the perturbations; scored calendar start = start + D;
    CPU and GPU draws inside the range with median at the geometric
    mean, uniform fallback at min 0). pytest 1372 passed / 12 skipped;
    train.py 1-generation smoke runs with --warmup-days 2, sequential
    (--workers 1) and parallel (--workers 4), OK. CUDA end to end
    (cuda-graph, 2 deltas, 64 ticks, --warmup-days 2): --init-from run,
    then --resume with the flag, and a --visual run under
    SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy - all OK; gpu_run.json records warmup_days.
    A first 1460-tick CUDA comparison (with and without 60 days) shared
    the GPU with fix71 for ~10 min and was stopped; fix71's
    seconds_per_update for those minutes is inflated.
200.6 fix71 (started by the user 2026-10-23 23:14, --init-from
    results/pzbpgp248nsrpfix71_init, fix70's flags) predates this code
    (23:34-23:37): it trains with the seal K and a 2e-3, but without a
    warm-up and with the linear draw. A running process keeps the code
    it imported. To use both: stop it and restart with --resume
    --warmup-days 60 (the trainer state is compatible).

202 REGENERATED NITROGEN IN THE ENGINES; TYPE III ON ZOO -> PHYTOPLANKTON (2026-10-24)
================================================================
202.1 User's call after 201: build the recycling in, with Type III.
202.2 Engine (lib/environments/ecosystem_env/regeneration.py, both
    engines; no new state, no observation change, checkpoints valid):
    - Species keys mortality_regeneration (0-1, any group) and
      egestion_regeneration (0-1, a grazing NDM); refused outside
      [0, 1]; inert without nutrient pools (env._has_regeneration).
    - M1 return: the CPU records each regenerating group's M1 loss per
      cell where it is applied (DM and NDM M1; the regional K loss is
      not M1 and is not returned) and adds share x loss to the pools at
      the END of the population step, after every group's growth (the
      GPU does the same from biomass x (1 - keep)), so the order of the
      FGs does not matter and the return feeds the next tick.
    - Layer split per world and tick: a group's mixed-layer share =
      its intake from the mixed producer / its intake from both
      producers, a grazer prey (microzooplankton) counted by that
      grazer's own split; a group that fed on neither: thickness share
      M(t)/bottom (env.regen["fallback"], per year tick). The intake
      comes from this tick: env._tick_dm_intake (predation) and
      env._tick_ndm_intake (apply_ndm_grazing); on the GPU from the
      predation's actual intake (step passes dm_feed) and ndm_grazing's
      per-entry totals. Grid-level, not per cell: the zooplankton has
      moved and drifted between predation and M1 (that is also what the
      201 scratch test used). Without the subsurface layer everything
      goes to the one producer's pool.
    - Egesta: the NDM grazer entry carries pool = (1 - gge)(excretion +
      egest (1 - excretion)), returned to the grazed producer's own pool
      in apply_ndm_grazing / ndm_grazing (so the layer split is the
      prey's layer).
    - GPU: regen_fraction() keeps its DM rows as host-side ints (a
      first version read dm_index back inside the captured tick and
      broke 20 CUDA-graph / no-readback tests).
202.3 Library: zooplankton mortality_regeneration 0.5;
    microzooplankton mortality_regeneration 0.5, egestion_regeneration
    1.0 (pool share 0.7 x (0.571 + 0.429) = 0.70 of its intake: 0.40
    excretion + 0.30 egesta); zooplankton_preys_on_phytoplankton
    functional_response 3, max_intake_rate 0.05 -> 0.03 (half-saturation
    1/sqrt(a h) = 2.9 t/km2 at 10 m); the subsurface pair stays Type II.
    Caveat (pre-existing, zoo -> micro has it since 178):
    mixed_layer_reference_m scales a linearly by M_ref/M(t); for a Type
    III response on a concentration the scale would be squared, so the
    2.9 t/km2 half-saturation holds at M = 10 m only and drifts as
    sqrt(M/M_ref) otherwise. The 0.03 was fitted on the engine as it is.
    budget_gate: zooplankton "any diet". FG editor fields and help
    texts for both keys (fgconfig.py main and NDM rows, field_help.py).

208 GADOID PREY SHARES: ACCESSIBLE FRACTION AND THE BENTHIVORE SHARE AS AN EAT-SHARE CAP (2026-10-24)
================================================================
208.1 Why: after 207 the frozen fix72 gadoids ate 80-91 % benthos (Q/B
    7.2-8.9). The first idea, tuning the gadoid -> benthos attack rate
    against a stomach-content diet (207.6), was dropped on the user's
    objection: the 1991 stomachs describe the ecosystem of 1991, so a
    diet fitted to them is not biology. Parameters must come from
    measurable mechanisms; diets are checks only. A correction on the
    mechanics: the eat actions are ONE softmax with one slot per prey,
    so the pairs do not add independently; total intake <= max_j 1/h_j
    and the diet is the policy's allocation over the slots.
208.2 Literature 1, accessibility (subagent; research_notes/"Bentos
    atkomlighet for torskfiskar" (Swedish letters), benthos_
    accessibility.md + evidence A-C; uncommitted):
    - Accessible fraction f of the prey-sized infauna ~0.2 (0.08-0.45):
      27 % of the biomass in the top 0-2 cm and 51 % in 0-5 cm at 280 m
      Skagerrak mud (Dauwe et al. 1998, full text); Amphiura offers arm
      tips (2-15 %; regenerating tissue ~22 %, Skold et al. 1994). The
      reach into the sediment is a judgement. f and a act only as a
      product and the pair stays saturated (>= 89 % of the ceiling even
      in the worst corner): f does not move today's diet.
    - The attack rate cannot be derived (search width and capture
      probability never measured for gadoids on infauna: 0.007-5.8);
      the 0.04 stays.
    - The benthivore share phi (morphology only: mouth position, jaw,
      barbel; haddock 1, cod 0.5/1/1, whiting 0/0/0.3, saithe 0, hake 0)
      is the lever that moves the diet.
    - Separate finding: the gadoid ceiling is 138 kJ/kg/day, ~1.6x cod
      Cmax at 7 C (h 135-154 against the model's 87). Kept apart from
      phi so the effect is not counted twice; not changed.

      rate, 47 % cannot at all".
208.6 Changed to the CAP FORM (user: "Byt till takformen"): full a and
    1/h, and the eat share on the prey capped at phi:
    eat_j = min(eat_j, phi_j) (CPU predation.py, env.share_cap_mat /
    _has_share_cap; GPU eat = torch.minimum(actions[:, :, 5:],
    self.share_cap)). The excess above phi is wasted (not
    re-allocated). growth_budget: rate = phi * intake_ceiling(a, h) *
    assim * energy; viability caps the saturating share at phi. Tests
    rewritten (test_predator_share_caps_the_eat_share; GPU parity with
    and without visibility floors; the accessible-fraction test
    restricts the eat action to one prey, rtol 2e-3 from the harvest
    cap). pytest 1411 passed / 12 skipped.

    - Reading: the cap does what it should, but only the benthos pair
      has a share. Herring and zooplankton are uncapped, so the whole
      group (haddock included) can eat them at the full rate, and their
      energy-limited ceilings pay slightly more per eat share (27.6-27.7
      vs 24.1 MJ/t/tick, section 148): a moving optimiser finds dense
      herring/zooplankton cells and skips benthos. The error is
      symmetric: the fish and zooplankton pairs need shares from the
      same method.

211 VIEWER: UPDATES BETWEEN PROBES WAITED FOR A HOVER (2026-10-25)
================================================================
211.1 Bug (user): with the probe interval > 1 (--eval-every or the
    viewer's slider), the reward curve and the status row of an update
    without a probe only appeared when the pointer moved over the plot.
    Cause: such an update only calls update_reward / update_status and
    then pump_events; those methods store data and pump_events repainted
    only on a click, a key, a drag or a hover (plot area, section 210's
    member rects). update_biomass, the only method that renders, runs in
    probes alone. Same in train.py (both loops) and train_gpu.py.
211.2 Fix (lib/viz/pygame_viz.py): a `_dirty` flag set by update_series
    (so update_reward), update_status, update_loss_breakdown,
    update_diet_breakdown and update_action_fracs; pump_events repaints
    through the frame cap (_maybe_render) while it is set, and
    _render_full clears it. An update the cap holds back stays flagged
    and the next pump (the trainer's ~50 ms pump callback) draws it. One
    extra repaint per training update; no repaint on an idle pump.
211.3 Checks: tests/test_viz_dirty_repaint.py (each update drawn by the
    next pump and only once, cap-held update kept, the new reward point
    changes the pixels; 8 of 10 fail without the fix). pytest 1444
    passed / 12 skipped; train.py 1-generation smoke run OK.

    No code or library change.

      ~gen 4 (benthivores ~1.0, predators 0.94-0.97, planktivores
      0.87-0.95, porpoises 0.91-1.05, seals ~1.02, benthos 0.954).
      Plateaued, as fix72 (206.1). The gen 8-9 reward dip is noise
      (within-generation std 0.3-0.6 on means of ~-0.2; zooplankton

    year 1: ben 1.03/1.04, pred 0.97/0.96, plk 0.92/1.07, porp

    1.39/1.39, pred 0.78/0.83, plk 0.73/0.94 (seed 20260530 min 0.65 at

    - Benthos: realised M2 from benthivores 0.10 -> 0.17 /yr vs the
      budget 0.0374 (3-4x). Benthivore diet 97 % benthos, Q/B 6.6 by
      mass. The budget M2 implies Q/B ~2.5 on benthos, below maintenance
      for a 97 % benthos diet (2100 MJ/t retained vs eat cost 7.2 MJ/t/

      0.0023534); at fill 0.71 production ~0.72 vs losses ~0.68 ->
      +4 %/yr.

      vs 0.18. Production shortfall: s* 0.735 (g 0.0022808), fill
