220 FISH ATTACK RATES FROM ENCOUNTER THEORY (2026-10-25/26)
================================================================
220.1 Why (user): after 219 the question was whether the fish pairs'
    attack rates, handling times, dark ratios and temperature terms had
    been calibrated after the 209 split. Handling times, SMR, Q10, t_ref
    and layers were re-derived per species in 209; every fish pair's a
    was the inherited 0.04 ("cannot be derived", 209.3/209.6, "settle it
    in a probe"). User correction: setting a from the model's outcome is
    not biology-first - derive it from biology, test it on independent
    field data, never fit it to the model.
220.2 Research (three subagents + two capped gap searches; main-agent
    summary research_notes/"Attackrater ur motesteori" (Swedish letters)/
    summary.md; data/ ~420 MB of downloads, not for commit; Holmes 1979
    restricts publication of derived values, Braaten & Gokstad 1980 is
    cite-with-consent). Engine meaning: a = area cleared per tonne of
    FORAGING predator (inside phi) per 6 h tick, km2/t/tick, annual mean
    over the daylight multiplier.
    - Encounter models: pi R^2 v p (3-D, R by light and prey size,
      Gerritsen-Strickler relative speed) over the vertical overlap,
      or speed x path width x p (2-D benthos); N/t from the NS-IBTS
      length structure; herring filtering separately (dark only).
    - Central (MC 5-95 %): planktivores -> zoo 0.007 (0.0018-0.016) with
      all-fish echo overlaps; benthivores -> benthos 0.26 (0.12-0.63),
      -> planktivores 0.016 (0.0013-0.069), -> predators 0.022 (0.0018-
      0.089); predators -> planktivores 0.0056 schooling / 0.012
      dispersed, -> zoo 0.0015 (0.0009-0.0054), -> benthos 0.030, ->
      benthivores 0.18 (0.058-0.65). Pelagic-prey pairs 2-27x below
      0.04 and no longer saturated; benthic pairs saturated either way.
    - Dominant uncertainties: reactive distance in dim water (never
      measured for adult herring or any predatory member), capture
      success on fish prey, the light profile at depth, where foraging
      fish sit relative to the prey.
    - Validation (not used to set a): Rindorf & Gislason 2005 half-
      saturation -> a 0.0063 (passes, but 0.0005-0.10 after three
      judgement conversions), Type II, fish eaten at dawn and dusk;
      gadoid prey imply predators -> benthivores ~0.03 (vs 0.18, weak);
      Persson 2012 / Holmes 1979 support the benthos value; Engelhard
      2008 0.012-0.035 matches the dispersed predator variant;
      Arrhenius & Hansson YOY herring favour R proportional to length.
    - Re-runs: benthivore fish pairs at Kd 0.25 (top 20 m; Arst 1993
      0.20 vs Aas 2014 0.30): 0.019 / 0.026 (x1.19; scripts/
      benth_encounter.py kd_top argument). Planktivores with the
      foraging-fish overlap (herring and sprat O = 1.0, 0.7-1.2, J;
      scripts/planktivores_a.py --foraging-overlap): 0.017 (0.0039-
      0.032), night/day 0.02 (0.008-0.08), half detection at sun ~0 deg;
      R proportional to length gives 0.0135.

223.11 Refuge research (research_notes/"Refugium och utbyte i bentos"
    (Swedish letters), summary.md, tables/refuge_parameters.csv):
    every measurable epifauna exchange is diel (k ~365-730 /yr), so a
    single A/R pool at a biological rate reproduces today's fixed f;
    the only slow structure is taxonomic: E1 = two compartments inside
    mobile_epifauna with no exchange (exposed taxa: crabs, hermits,
    Munida, northern shrimp, small shrimps, mysids, B 3.06, r_max 1.11;
    Nephrops B 4.57, r_max 0.34, predators unchecked, benthivores 0.07
    of it). Infauna: a real slow exchange by cropping and regrowth, k
    ~2.5 /yr (1.5-3), k_in ~0.5, phi 0.20, both compartments logistic
    on their own K (Krivan 1998); it slows local depletion (93.6 -> ~37
    t/km2 in 5 yr in a doubled-benthivore cell) but does not stop it.
    The engine's Beddington-DeAngelis term is already the fast-refuge
    limit (Berardo et al. 2020). Neither form removes the saturation.
    Mackinson & Daskalov 2007 diet page for predator columns 13-24 is a
    duplicate of 1-12 (gadoid invertebrate diets lost); fish take 1.3-
    6.5 % of infauna production (Dauvin 1988).

223.13 Built (2026-10-26, uncommitted): infauna refuge, three-year
    probe tab, depleted training patches.
    - Refuge (lib/environments/ecosystem_env/refuge.py; GPU mirror in
      lib/gpu/ecosystem.py, spawner in lib/gpu/spawn.py): a NDM with
      exposed_share phi in (0, 1) keeps its accessible part A in the
      unused energy_reserve slot (tonnes), so B stays the group's
      biomass everywhere. Predation (Holling term, harvest cap, removal)
      and the observations see A; trawl, M1, the habitat mask and the
      extinction sweep scale A with B. Each tick: the exchange A <- phi B
      + (A - phi B) exp(-k) (k = refuge_exchange_rate per tick, rescaled
      as a flux by tick_time), then logistic growth per compartment on
      phi K and (1 - phi) K (variant S). Exchange BEFORE growth makes
      k -> infinity exactly the old fixed accessible fraction with a
      logistic on B (tested); the subagent's growth-then-exchange order
      did not reach that limit. A starts at phi B (FunctionalGroup.
      initialize_state, WorldSpawner.reserves). The viability rig's
      reachable prey uses A. Library: benthic_infauna exposed_share 0.2,
      refuge_exchange_rate 0.0017123288 (2.5 /yr); the benthivore ->
      infauna pair lost its accessible_fraction 0.2 (now the refuge).
      Derived growth unchanged (the loader's rule lands B* within 0.1 %
      at k 2.5, refuge note). Probe world: A/B 0.200 at start, 0.1996
      after 40 ticks, B stable.
    - Progress tab -> three-year probe (lib/runners/training_progress.
      py, lib/viz/pygame_viz.py, i18n sv/it): run_probe runs a frozen
      copy of the current policies PROBE_YEARS = 3 years (library ticks;
      the probe world is built at the library tick length, so the
      default --eval-ticks is 4380 whatever --tick-length is) and
      records every group's biomass / start once a day, the year-end
      ratios and the DMs' survival ticks. The live viewer submits it to
      a one-worker spawn process pool (4 torch threads) and records it at
      the first update after it finishes; a probe due while one runs is
      skipped; close() / the end of train.py wait for the running one.
      History progress/probe.jsonl (format_version 2; old survival.jsonl
      runs need a new --plot-dir to resume), latest trajectory
      progress/probe_latest.json. The tab shows the latest probe for
      every group (NDMs too), x = probe day with year marks, y = % of
      start (auto-scaled), title "Update N: frozen policies, seed S | n
      probes".
    - --depleted-patches SHARE (train_gpu.py, default 0.5): that share of
      the training worlds starts with benthic patches (smooth noise,
      sigma 3 cells, coverage 5-30 % of the cells, one level per world
      log-uniform 1-32 %) on the groups with a depth habitat; a refuge
      group loses accessible tonnes, its refuge stays (TensorEcosystem.
      deplete). Keyed by the world (CRN), applied before the warm-up.
      Training-world design so the fish meet emptied beds and can learn
      to leave them (223.8 found the frozen policy staying on emptied
      beds), not biology. GPU trainer only; train.py has no such worlds.
    - Tests: tests/test_refuge.py (10: share checks, A at phi B, plain

223.18 Viability score on the progress probe (user, 2026-10-26). Every
      probe now scores VIABILITY.md section 1 on the trained policies
      (training_progress.probe_viability, in run_probe before _record
      drops the trajectory). Windows are whole probe years from the
      daily series (sample i = tick i*every_ticks, index 0 = start): eq
      = mean of the last complete year, prev = the year before, so the
      season cancels and year 1 (transient from the inference start)
      is out of a three-year probe. Survival = the whole series > 0
      (not survival_ticks, which count the training --biomass-bounds).
      Floor 0.10, ceiling 10, max_drift 2 from ViabilityCriterion.
      Every group present at spawn is scored, non decision makers too.
      Per group a log10 margin to the nearest bound, normalised per
      condition (1 at spawn / no drift, 0 at the bound, < 0 fails;
      extinct = no margin, binding "extinct"); V = the worst group,
      since the criterion holds for each. A margin, not a distance to
      the start: 0.23x spawn is a calibration fact. years_to_floor
      extrapolates a declining group's year-on-year ratio (indicative).
      probe.jsonl keeps the block with the annual means (re-scorable);
      the terminal prints a table per probe; the tab a second line
      "Viable n/m, V +x.xx | worst <fg>: +m to <bound>[, floor in ~N
      yr] | probe years 2-3" (sv/it in i18n; the margin sits next to
      the bound so "worst X: floor" is not read as "below the floor").
      A floor horizon over 50 yr (10x the rig's 5) is not shown. On
      fix77's update-190 probe: 12/12 viable, V +0.16 (phytoplankton
      at 0.14x start nearest the floor), benthivores bound by drift
      (1.38, 0.55 -> 0.40, floor in ~4 yr). One seed and three years: a
      progress measure, not a verdict, and never a reward or tuning
      target. Tests: tests/test_training_progress.py (+5),
      tests/test_viz_i18n.py (+1).
223.19 Ctrl+C without tracebacks from the probe worker (user, 2026-10-26:
      "no traces on Ctrl+C"). The terminal sends SIGINT to the whole
      process group, so the live probe's spawn worker died with a
      KeyboardInterrupt traceback (idle in call_queue.get, or mid-probe).
      Now the worker ignores SIGINT: the parent sets SIG_IGN around the
      submit that spawns it (_sigint_ignored_by_children; an ignored
      signal survives exec and Python keeps it - the initializer alone
      left the first seconds of torch imports exposed, the test caught
      it), plus an _ignore_sigint initializer. The trainer decides:
      LiveTrainingProgress.wait(cancel) records a running probe at the
      end of a finished run, and stops it (terminate, "[progress] probe
      N (update S) cancelled") when cancel is true - a bool, or a
      callable polled every 0.5 s, since train_gpu's handler only sets
      stop_requested (visual.close(cancel=lambda: stop_requested or not
      finished), handlers still restored after it so a Ctrl+C cannot
      skip the checkpoint). A KeyboardInterrupt while waiting cancels
      too. train.py's interrupt path calls wait(cancel=True); before, it
      never stopped the worker. Verified end to end (train_gpu: worker
      starting, mid-probe, idle; train.py mid-probe): exit 0, no
      traceback, checkpoint saved. tests/test_training_progress.py (+2).

223.23 Fix to 223.19: _stop_worker no longer joins the cancelled probe
      worker itself. The pool's manager thread joins it too, and two
      threads racing os.waitpid made the loser's Popen.poll() catch
      ECHILD and return None, so is_alive() read True for a dead
      process (test_ctrl_c... failed ~1 in 15 runs). Now: terminate,
      then shutdown(wait=True) and let the manager thread reap; 0

    - Common mechanism: per-pair Holling with no shared handling and a
      linear eat share (185.16, 199.8). A saturated pair delivers its
      ceiling down to a few % of the prey's start density, so the
      pressure is eat share x B_pred / h, set by the policy, not by
      prey abundance; pairs that pay little per unit share
      (benthivores -> whiting, benthivores -> plk 0.0035 vs 0.245,
      water column -> zoo 0.006 vs 0.076) are never chosen, saturated
      pairs realise 5-25x their budget M2. The growth budget and the
      return structure are inconsistent.
    - Options (user's call; no a moved per the rule): (a) the budget
      books M2 on pairs the engine makes unchoosable - a budget/
      engine consistency question; (b) the multi-prey response with
      shared handling of 199.8, intake_j = a_j B_j / (1 + sum_k a_k
      h_k B_k) (both engines, every pair rechecked, retrain), the
      documented mechanism that makes dense prey self-limit and lets
      the encounter-theory a set the diet.
    - Follow-up (user question: why would herring not pay for whiting?
      2026-10-27). Rig scratchpad wht_plk.py: frozen fix78 policies, 2
      years, seed 20260530; per cell the engine's own return per unit
      eat share (visible prey, pair access, light, interference,
      reserve offset), weighted by whiting biomass x hunger, against
      the policy's eat shares. Herring does pay: in summer-autumn
      (visible fraction ~1.0) planktivores give 25-27 MJ/t/tick vs
      epifauna 22, and the policy puts 0.55-0.89 of its eat share on
      them. In winter the herring hide (visible fraction 0.34-0.50;
      the light multiplier is low too) and the return falls to ~14,
      while epifauna (an NDM, no hide, saturated down to ~3 % of its
      start) pays 23-24 all year; the policy goes 0.87-0.94 to
      epifauna. The policy's shares follow the per-cell best prey
      closely (share of whiting where each prey is best: same
      pattern), so this is not a learning failure. Diet by mass
      exaggerates the epifauna: herring carries 5700 vs 3000 MJ/t
      (as eaten by whiting), so year 1's 81/18 % by mass is ~70/30 %
      by energy. The epifauna loss therefore comes from winter, when
      the herring are out of reach and the bed is an always-saturated,
      never-hiding food.

    - Shared handling, worked through (user question, 2026-10-27;
      scratchpad shared_handling.py: the probe world's start state,
      library a/h/f/Type III/refuge/interference, no hiding, annual-
      mean light; effort scaled so each predator eats its budget
      ration). Two facts make it decisive: (1) the library sets every
      pair's h = E/Cmax, so E/h is the same for all prey of a
      predator (water column 26.2, whiting 25.1, benthivores 18.3-
      20.9); by the optimal-diet rule there is then no profitability
      reason to reject any prey, and the diet is set by encounter, a f
      x visible B (x B for Type III). (2) The denominator is shared,
      so within a predator M2_j / M2_k = a_j f_j / a_k f_k (Type II,
      equal visibility) - a closed-form, density-free consistency
      test of the a's against the budget M2. Diets at budget ration
      (shared / budget %, M2 shared vs library):
      water column ben 21.5/6.2 (0.29 vs 0.083), plk 27.2/54.9 (0.17
      vs 0.34), wht 9.1/3.4 (0.42 vs 0.157), zoo 42.2/35.6;
      whiting epi 85.6/17.7 (0.33 vs 0.069), plk 4.8/36.3, zoo 5.8/
      36.0, ben 3.8/10.0; benthivores infauna 64.1/54.4, epi 31.3/29.9
      (0.56 vs 0.54), Nephrops 3.7/1.5, plk 0.8/12.0, whiting 0.2/2.3
      (0.024 vs 0.345); seals ben 96.7/60.1, plk 0.0/25.1; porpoises
      plk 88.6/64.8, whiting 2.2/13.0. So shared handling alone would
      not fix the two chains: with today's a it gives whiting an even
      more epifauna-heavy diet and the water column ~3.5x the budget
      M2 on benthivores (vs 6.4x realised now). What it changes: the
      policy no longer chooses the prey (one forage action; diet from
      encounter, where/when to forage and the prey's hiding); hiding
      pays again (benthivores to the floor 0.55 cut the water-column
      take ~40 % vs ~6 % now); alternative prey dilute the pressure on
      a declining prey (whiting -> epifauna per-capita M2 rises ~2.4x
      as epifauna vanishes, vs up to ~28x per unit share now); and the
      a/budget inconsistency becomes explicit and must be resolved
      from biology (which of a/e/f or the diet-based M2 is wrong per
      pair), never from model output. A habitat-mode variant (effort
      per layer, bed vs water column, shared handling within and
      across) would keep a learned choice with a biological meaning.
    - User question (2026-10-27): are infauna and epifauna unrealistically
      easy to find and handle? The project's own field notes say yes
      for the density response, with three mechanisms recommended and
      never applied (research_notes/"Fodoniva och mattnad i falt",
      Swedish letters, mechanisms table; "Exponering av bottenbyten"):
      (a) armour on the ceiling of shelled prey, h x ~1.5-2 (Andersen
      1999: brown shrimp evacuated ~2x slower in whiting; Couturier
      2013), ~94 % of the exposed epifauna is crustacean; on the fix78
      returns it takes whiting -> epifauna from 23-24 to 16 (x1.5) or
      12 (x2) MJ/t/tick against herring's winter 14; (b) a seasonal
      feeding window (ICES stomach data: whiting 45 % empty in Q1,
      cod/haddock 16-18 % vs 6-10 %; gadoid Q1 ration ~0.6-0.8, J) -
      the winter is exactly when all three rigs found the fallback onto
      the bed and the benthivores; a physiological rate in the response
      (as herring's feeding season), not a cap on the action; (c) the
      benthic density response: Hiddink 2016 (Kattegat, intake and
      condition fall with prey per fish) needs x = a h f B ~1-4 at
      today's prey, the engine has 19-66 (whiting -> epifauna ~35 at
      the start: at 10 % of the start it still pays 78 % of the
      ceiling; at x 3 it would pay 23 %). Open conflict with the
      mechanistic e (0.15-0.5), which found no step that lowers a by
      1-2 orders; unresolved, user's call. Capture window tau 0.1-0.2
      on fish prey (Rindorf & Gislason 2005) concerns the fish pairs,
      not the bed.
    - Correction (user, 2026-10-27): behaviour must not come from the
      engine identifying a season; the physical changes of the season
      must drive it (as herring's winter rest). The seasonal feeding
      window (b) above is withdrawn as a month-keyed multiplier. The
      physical candidates for the field's low Q1 rations: (i) water
      temperature on Cmax, ingestion_q10 on the fish (section 181's
      mechanism, a and 1/h together, annual mean 1): Q10 2-3 gives
      Q1/other quarters 0.83-0.89 on at_50m (6.6-11.7 C) but only
      0.96-0.97 on the bottom layer (6.6-8.5 C) - real but too small
      for the field 0.6-0.8, and none for the bed feeders; (ii) light
      does not help: bottom prey are eaten MORE at night by North Sea
      whiting (Rindorf 2003; research_notes/"Torskfiskars ljusberoende
      vid jakt"), so the winter shift to the bed is right in direction;
      (iii) spawning (cod Q1, whiting Feb-Jun) is not represented. So
      the field's Q1 empty stomachs say that when the herring are out
      of reach the bed does NOT refill gadoid stomachs to the ceiling -
      evidence for (a) armour and (c) the benthic density response,
      not for a separate seasonal mechanism.
    - Literature search on the saturation conflict (user, 2026-10-27;
      research_notes/"Mattnad hos bottenbyten" (Swedish letters),
      summary.md saved by the main agent). Both earlier notes right
      about different quantities: a and e stand (lab cod on Crangon a
      0.065-0.13 vs library 0.15, Persson 2012; no search-side step of
      5-50x); the response to ONE prey rises at field densities (cod on
      Pandalus x ~0.25-0.5, Hvingel & Kingsley 2006; diets track prey
      over 5-250x with flat total intake, Smith 2013, Berenboim 2000).
      They reconcile only if co-occurring bed prey share one search and
      one gut (Murdoch 1973, Jeschke 2002): benthivores X_bed 123, x_eff
      infauna 1.2, epifauna 0.7, Nephrops 0.05; intake at 10 % of a prey
      0.10-0.20 vs 0.42-0.88 per pair. Structural, not a library value.
      Whiting stays saturated with bed-only sharing (its one bed pair,
      x 35). Main-agent addition: if whiting's bed and water-column
      search share time (X 56.8 at the start: epi 35.4, plk 15.9, zoo
      3.2, ben 2.3), epifauna x_eff 1.6 and intake at 10 % epifauna
      0.22, but the diet by mass at the start is ~73 % epifauna (a f B)
      vs 18 % in the budget - the a/budget inconsistency remains; open
      whether whiting's modes share time (Rindorf 2003: bottom prey by
      night, free-swimming by day). Armour (h x1.7-2 shrimps, x2-3
      crabs, J) halves the crustacean ceiling; under sharing it adds to
      X and does not change diet by mass. Field feeding level 0.22-0.53
      of Cmax stays unexplained by any of this (time/risk; a predator
      cue cut cod intake to 0.22-0.44, Persson 2012). Kattegat: flat
      prey, flatfish x0.5, condition independent of B - consumer
      density open.

    - Benthivore movement speed (user question, 2026-10-28: too slow to
      escape?). movement_speed is the share of the moving biomass that
      leaves the cell per tick (movement.apply_movement: b_out =
      moving x dm_v; engine cap 1 cell = 1 km per 6 h). Benthivores 0.2
      (research_notes/"Fiskgrupper i rutan" params_benthivorous_fish.md:
      "haddock, cod 0.25 (as gadoids), gurnard 0.2, flatfish and rays
      sedentary 0.1", J) - the old gadoid value and a residence reading,
      while the same research set the predators to 1.0 because "residence
      is behaviour, not a speed limit" (0.25 was "below the physiology of
      every pelagic member"). By that rule cod/haddock at ~0.5 BL/s
      (40-50 cm: ~4-5 km per 6 h) and plaice (km/day in tagging) are
      physically above the cap: an inconsistency, not a measured limit.
      Every other fish prey (planktivores, whiting) has 1.0. Effect now:
      a move action costs the full movement_cost while only 20 % leaves,
      so flight and food-tracking barely pay (fix78 benthivore actions:
      move 0.13, rest 0.03, eat 0.84); hiding does not pay either under
      saturation (~6 %) - the benthivores have no working defence, the
      only fish prey without one, and the only one eaten at 6x its
      budget M2. Water column co-location on benthivores is only 1.16x,
      so avoidance has room (overlap < 1). Not quantified; needs
      retraining (library value only, checkpoints valid, --init-from).
      Independent of the shared-denominator question (bed prey).

    - Correction to the refuge cross-check: Skold et al. 1994 give a
      REALISED Amphiura regeneration flux ~0.06 B /yr (13 % of production
      x P/B 0.46) under the field's light cropping - a demand-limited
      flux, a lower bound on what the exposed layer can supply, not a
      ceiling; comparing it with k_in 0.5 (a rate constant) mixed
      quantities. Flux against flux: fix78's year-1 take 5.6 t/km2/yr is
      about that observed flux (0.06 x 94); the engine's supply capacity
      with A emptied is k_in B ~47 t/km2/yr, near the production bound
      (P/B 0.46 -> ~43; lugworm cropping 0.39 /yr ~60 % of production,
      Beukema & de Vlas 1979). The take is ~12 % of capacity; the refuge
      is not the binding limit. Untested: whether capacity at 6 C bottom
      water sits nearer the production bound or the realised flux.

    - Why the water column takes 4-5x its booked M2 on the benthivores
      (user question, 2026-10-28; rig wht_plk.py on f80, predatory_fish,
      1 year, rig months from late May). (1) The pair is saturated, so
      the take is set by the policy's eat share, not by benthivore
      density: share of the ceiling 0.78 at today's densities, ~4.8 /yr
      of M2 per unit eat share, ceiling demand 6.2 t/km2/yr vs the
      benthivores' whole gross production 1.25 (params_split_223.md
      section 6). The booked 0.083 corresponds to an eat share of ~0.04;
      the policy uses 0.04-0.27 (year mean 0.15), highest in rig months
      5-9 (~Oct-Feb, 0.19-0.27) when herring hide (visible 0.28-0.40,
      return 12.7-17 vs 22-26 in rig months 2-4 and 11-12) and zooplankton pays ~0. It
      tracks the per-cell best prey (got/best 0.90-0.99; benthivores
      best for 0.06-0.28 of the water column, in their dense patches),
      so this is foraging on the engine's returns, not a learning
      failure. (2) The benthivores have no defence that pays: rest 0.01,
      visible = the pair access 0.24 all year (hiding under saturation
      cuts the take ~6 %, 223.27). (3) Decomposition of realised M2 =
      diet share x Q/B x B_wc/B_ben against the budget 0.062 x 2.74 x
      0.49: year 1 0.23 x 2.6 x 0.56 (x3.7 diet, x0.95, x1.13), year 3
      0.15 x 2.4 x 1.07 (x2.4, x0.88, x2.2). Year 1 is the diet; by year
      3 half is the ratio: the water column holds on herring while the
      benthivores fall, and per-capita take on them falls only x0.6 for
      a x0.42 density drop. (4) The library itself disagrees with the
      budget: by encounter alone (a f B at start, 0.053 x 0.24 x 1.53 vs
      herring 0.0117 x 3.3) the benthivores are ~0.5 of the herring
      encounter; the shared-handling test (223.27) gives 21.5 % of the
      diet vs the booked 6.2 % (M2 0.29). Only a near the bottom of its
      range (0.018 of 0.018-0.17) or a larger diet share (range M2
      0.05-0.23) would reconcile them - a biology question per the rule,
      not a fit. (5) The accessible 0.24 (gape slice: juveniles + 0-
      group) is a fixed share of the current biomass that never runs
      out, so 0.35 /yr on the group is ~1.5 /yr on the slice without
      the juveniles being depleted (no size structure). No change.

    - Why the water column leaves its zooplankton (user, 2026-10-29;
      scratchpad wc_zoo.py on the frozen u550 policies, calendar months
      from light_index; the probe world starts 27 May, light_start 590).
      The model's zooplankton is right in time: A17 score zoo log-RMSE
      0.91 (r +0.80; f80 u300 1.03), 14-21 t/km2 Apr-Jul. At the
      predator in Apr-Jul: zoo 15-20 t/km2, visible 0.36-0.77 (the zoo
      hides), x = a h B_vis 0.68-1.08 -> 10-13 MJ/t/tick per unit eat
      share, half the ceiling (~26); herring at the same time 3-8 t/km2
      at the predator (it gathers on herring; grid 2.3-3.7), visible
      0.98-0.99, x 8-25 -> 19-22. Every other month zoo pays 0.4-7.
      Zoo never pays more than herring on the group mean in any month;
      eat share on zoo < 0.005. Half-saturation: herring 1/(a h) = 0.39
      t/km2, zoo 12 t/km2 visible (a 0.0006 vs 0.0117, 20x). The
      derivation predicted it (params_split_223.md: wc share of the
      ceiling at today's B, zoo 0.51 / 0.05 vs herring 0.92 / 0.79).
      Three causes: (1) the eat share is linear and exclusive (no shared
      handling), so a half-saturated prey adds nothing beside a
      saturated one - the learned diet is all herring; (2) the wc ->
      planktivores pair is the "layer" upper form at f 1 (partial gape
      scores dropped; mackerel 0.49 of its a), so herring pays as if
      every member could swallow adult herring - an f to derive as for
      the benthivores, but minor here: herring is saturated (x 8-25), a
      halved f leaves it at 0.8-0.9 of the ceiling, so it cannot flip
      the zoo season; the zoo a is already the upper (layer) form; (3) the booked M2 0.0756 (34 % of the wc diet)
      assumes krill, the pool is the A17 resident copepods (220.3
      decision 4; library comment "Open (209/220)"). A small learned
      part: 8-21 % of the wc biomass in ~Jun-Jul sits where zoo is the
      best prey, eat share there < 0.02. The booking does not constrain
      the diet: the wc eats to its hunger gate on the best payer, so the
      ~0.7 t/t/yr zoo ration it does not take (x wc 0.57 t/km2 / herring
      2.0 t/km2 = 0.20 /yr) shows up on herring, the wc's excess over
      booked (0.58 vs 0.34). Changing the zoo M2 moves only the
      zooplankton's derived growth, not the herring pressure. Earlier today's fix81 month labels corrected to rig
      months (above). No library change.

    - Mechanics: J inside B (FunctionalGroup.juvenile; GPU a [E, G, C]
      tensor through TensorEcosystem.step (appended return), RolloutRunner
      (buffer, reset(juvenile=None -> start share), absorb, snapshot) and
      the trainer warm-up). Reserve pro rata (fill, hunger, prey quality,
      growth budget unchanged). New tonnes to J in the share (kappa J +
      rho(t) A)/(kappa J + rho(t) A + A) of the cell's state when they are
      made (income growth in apply_energy_costs; the growth delta in the
      DM population step, after M1 and the capacity loss); then
      graduation J exp(-gamma/T), T the calendar's ticks per year.
      Losses with B (M1, capacity, starvation, sweep, mask, empty cells).
      Fishing: impact `fishing_selectivity` s_J, group loss unchanged, J
      loses sum(bf s_J) J clipped to [0, min(J, loss)] (GPU: one more row
      per staged group in the impact loss field, `impact_rows`). Movement

      Predation: pair `stage_access [f_J, f_A]` (default both = the pair's

223.36 Stock-scale regulation instead of the regional K: research
    (user, 2026-10-29/30; research_notes/"Bestandsreglering" (Swedish
    letters: a-ring): plan.md, stock_recruitment.md (WP1),
    migration.md (WP2), box_share.md (WP3), summary.md; three subagents;
    no engine or library change).
    - WP3: the box (off Bohuslan, Lysekil-Smogen, not Hvaler) holds
      0.1-0.6 % of herring, haddock, whiting, saithe, pout, sprat (Q1),
      cod ~2 % (Viking 5-7 %), witch 6-9 %, long rough dab ~1.7 %; its
      share of recruits is 2-5x its share of spawners (nursery);
      weight of the box's own adults in its recruitment w 0.003 / 0.03
      / 0.004 / 0.02 (planktivores / benthivores / water column /
      whiting). The earlier 0.3-0.6 % juvenile-habitat note is low.
    - WP1 (24 SAG series): post-2000 recruitment flat in SSB, e =
      dln(R/S)/dlnS at today's SSB -0.74 / -0.97 / -0.65 / -0.98;
      origin slope not identified; R/S fell after ~2000 (haddock 0.24,
      cod 0.27-0.46, herring 0.63-0.66); WBSS herring e 0 (below Blim).
    - WP2 (DATRAS cohorts relative to the stock, upper bounds): net
      emigration e_J / e_A per yr: planktivores 0.1 / 0.6, benthivores
      1.1 / 0.17, whiting 0.2 / 0.3, water column - / 0.1 with Feb/Aug
      presence 0.09; weak density dependence of the outflow (c ~0.3).
    - Synthesis: the compensation is outside the box; from the box,
      recruitment is a donor-controlled import and the box exports, so
      B = I / (L - P) is regulated without K. Proposed form: imported
      recruit flux into J (replaces the rho allocation, which creates
      no mass), somatic-only growth budget (r_max would count
      recruitment twice), per-stage emigration losses, optional
      seasonal visitors; K kept for whiting (export 0.3 < r - F 0.41)
      and seals. Rough benthivore closure with field rates only: supply
      P 0.73 + I/B 0.11-0.22 vs losses 0.99 /yr.
    - Closure, all four groups (scripts/closure.py, SMS 2023 per-tonne
      growth at the box J/B, library M1 + booked M2 + F, WP2 emigration,
      SMS stock biomass at the recruit stage x WP3 box share; user,
      2026-10-30): L - P / imported recruits I/B / covered:
      planktivores 1.00 / 0.08-0.24 / 8-24 %; benthivores 0.25 /
      0.10-0.14 / 38-57 % (CORRECTS the hand estimate above, 0.11-0.22
      "within 5-15 %"); whiting 0.18 / 0.27-0.50 / 153-282 % (regulated,
      level 1.5-2.8x today); water column 0.26 / 0 / 0 % (the need is
      ~10 % of the visitor turnover 2.4 /yr). Benthivores and whiting
      are resident nursery groups (recruit import + emigration; whiting

223.38 Why the zooplankton never learned to rest in winter (user,
    2026-10-30; analysis only). Frozen fix83 u327, probe world, seed
    20260530, 2 yr (scratchpad zoo_rest.py): the policy eats 0.96-0.99
    of its biomass Oct-Feb (rest 0.001-0.012); B/b0 0.04-0.10 in Jan-
    Feb. Overlay moving the zooplankton's eat mass into Rest in Dec-Feb
    or Nov-Mar (moves unchanged): extinct within that winter (B 0 by
    January, reward proxy -15 / -18 vs -1.16). A full reserve lasts
    max_energy_reserve / resting_metabolism = 675 / 22.5 = 30 ticks
    (~7.5 days; Q10 2 in winter gives ~10 days); real C. finmarchicus
    diapause runs 4-6 months on wax esters at 10-20 % of active
    respiration (140.3). Eating all winter is the right answer in this
    engine: no sigma or lr can teach a rest that kills. The missing
    mechanism is diapause (a reduced rest metabolism and a lipid store
    sized from the literature; a payoff change, the choice still
    learned), open since 138.7. Hyperparameters: lr/sigma = 0.6 is at
    the upper bound of 154.8 (|step|/probe radius ~ (lr/sigma) k /
    sqrt(b)); for an --init-from run in the changed world lr 0.03 keeps
    the noise-dominated random walk smaller; sigma 0.1 kept.
    - Move vs rest (user: earlier runs settled at ~35 % rest; fix83 moves
      ~30 %). GPU action logs [entropy, move, rest, eat], zooplankton,
      end of run: fix70 0.01/0.22/0.77, fix72 0.02/0.31/0.66, fix73
      0.04/0.27/0.69, fix76-78 0.03-0.08/0.18-0.29, fix80 0.02/0.31/0.67,
      fix82 0.13/0.21/0.66 (u78) - but fix79 0.27/0.00/0.73 (1x16) and
      fix83 0.28/0.03/0.69 (2x16): every run starts at move ~0.5 and
      most trade it for rest within ~150 updates; two did not (path-
      dependent, not the net). Frozen fix83 final (u492), 2 yr, overlay
      moving the zooplankton's move mass into Rest all year: reward
      proxy -1.068/-1.164 -> -1.023/-1.111 (seed 20260530), -1.105/
      -1.129 -> -1.047/-1.075 (seed 7), +0.05 /yr ~ 1 sigma_f; the
      policy moves 0.5-0.78 of its biomass May-Sep, ~0 in winter. So
      rest beats move in summer: a stuck policy, unlike the winter
      case. Next run: --init-from a copy of fix83 WITHOUT
      policy_zooplankton.pth (import_policies skips a missing file, so
      the zooplankton starts fresh; obs layout unchanged); keep lr 0.06
      / sigma 0.1 (the setting under which most runs found rest),
      replacing the lr 0.03 suggestion above.

    User: a check box labelled "restart" deciding what a new slider value

      so the run's local state (history, loss/diet snapshots) survives:
      unticked, a slider released after the end applies the change and
      the same world runs another rollout length (the length slider's
      value) from the last tick. The film and the plot series continue
      (LiveVisualizer.resume_rollout_recording; begin_rollout_recording
      would clear them). A spawn dropdown change always restarts. A dead
      world or a closed window falls back to main's wait as before.

      the colours (the reference is the start maximum); display only.
